# 4) Pyomo AML object model: `Model`, `Block`, and component hierarchy — deep dive

Style target: uploaded advanced technical-doc plan. 

Pyomo’s **AML core** is exposed through `pyomo.environ`: `ConcreteModel`, `AbstractModel`, `Block`, `Set`, `RangeSet`, `Param`, `Var`, `Objective`, `Constraint`, `ExternalFunction`, `Reference`, and `SOSConstraint`. The stable AML reference defines `ConcreteModel` as non-deferred construction, `AbstractModel` as deferred construction, `Block` as an indexed component that contains other components, `Set`/`RangeSet` as indexing components, `Param` as indexed/scalar data, `Var` as indexed/scalar decision variables, `Objective`/`Constraint` as expression-bearing modeling components, `ExternalFunction` as a non-algebraic function interface, `Reference` as a component reference, and `SOSConstraint` as special ordered set support. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

---

## 4.0 Hierarchy mental model

```text id="560md7"
ConcreteModel / instantiated AbstractModel
  = root Block
  = namespace owner
  = component container
  = traversal root
  = solver-export root

Block
  = nested namespace
  = modular submodel
  = component container
  = optional indexed family of submodels
  = activation/deactivation boundary

Component
  = named object attached to a Block
  = e.g., Set, Param, Var, Objective, Constraint, Block, SOSConstraint

ComponentData
  = scalar data object inside an indexed component
  = e.g., model.x[i], model.c[j], model.sub[k]
```

Core invariant:

```text id="l8ewmo"
Assigning a Pyomo component to a model/block attribute registers it in that block’s scope.
Component name = attribute path.
Block hierarchy = namespace hierarchy.
Solver writers traverse active components from the root block.
```

Pyomo’s `Block` docs state that models use blocks to define hierarchical structure and scoping; when modeling components are assigned to a block, they are automatically added to that block’s scope. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

---

## 4.1 Canonical import

```python id="ufj5gz"
import pyomo.environ as pyo
```

Use `pyo.` consistently:

```python id="d5mgpm"
m = pyo.ConcreteModel()
m.I = pyo.RangeSet(1, 3)
m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=sum(m.x[i] for i in m.I))
m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=sum(m.x[i] for i in m.I) >= 1)
```

Avoid:

```python id="n8d7lr"
from pyomo.environ import *
```

Reason:

```text id="j2bz5w"
harder static analysis
namespace collisions
unclear symbolic/numeric boundary
weaker agent refactoring safety
```

---

## 4.2 Root model objects

### 4.2.1 `ConcreteModel`

```python id="bnfw71"
m = pyo.ConcreteModel(name="production")
```

Semantics:

```text id="2hz015"
root block
component construction occurs immediately
data embedded at declaration time
solver receives m directly
```

Example:

```python id="gidlf7"
m = pyo.ConcreteModel(name="toy_lp")

m.x = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.x)
m.lb = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= 1)
```

### 4.2.2 `AbstractModel`

```python id="rex1d8"
template = pyo.AbstractModel()
```

Semantics:

```text id="o55fok"
root block template
component construction deferred until data instantiation
solve target = instance, not template
```

Example:

```python id="jyz6se"
template = pyo.AbstractModel()

template.I = pyo.Set()
template.c = pyo.Param(template.I)
template.x = pyo.Var(template.I, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

def obj_rule(m):
    return sum(m.c[i] * m.x[i] for i in m.I)

template.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule)

instance = template.create_instance(data)
```

---

## 4.3 Core component taxonomy

| Component          | Role                                  | Scalar syntax                               | Indexed syntax                                          |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Block`            | hierarchical container/submodel       | `m.b = pyo.Block()`                         | `m.b = pyo.Block(m.I)`                                  |
| `Set`              | arbitrary index/domain                | `m.S = pyo.Set(initialize=[...])`           | usually scalar component with indexed members           |
| `RangeSet`         | numeric range index                   | `m.T = pyo.RangeSet(1, 24)`                 | usually scalar                                          |
| `Param`            | immutable/mutable data                | `m.p = pyo.Param(initialize=1)`             | `m.p = pyo.Param(m.I, initialize=...)`                  |
| `Var`              | decision variable                     | `m.x = pyo.Var()`                           | `m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, m.J)`                               |
| `Objective`        | objective expression                  | `m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=...)`           | rare; multiple objectives require activation discipline |
| `Constraint`       | algebraic relation                    | `m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=...)`            | `m.c = pyo.Constraint(m.I, rule=...)`                   |
| `ExternalFunction` | callback / compiled external function | `m.f = pyo.ExternalFunction(...)`           | rarely indexed directly                                 |
| `Reference`        | alias/view into other components      | `m.r = pyo.Reference(m.b[:].x)`             | returned object is indexed                              |
| `SOSConstraint`    | special ordered set constraint        | `m.sos = pyo.SOSConstraint(var=m.x, sos=2)` | `m.sos = pyo.SOSConstraint(m.K, rule=...)`              |

---

## 4.4 Component vs `ComponentData`

### 4.4.1 Indexed component container

```python id="rr8p7w"
m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=["A", "B", "C"])
m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
```

Objects:

```python id="0llwhg"
m.x          # Indexed Var component container
m.x["A"]     # VarData object
m.x["B"]     # VarData object
```

### 4.4.2 Scalar component

```python id="yyf6ca"
m.y = pyo.Var()
```

Access:

```python id="9q0kll"
m.y          # scalar Var component / scalar variable object
pyo.value(m.y)
```

Agent rule:

```text id="nvo6vw"
Use component_objects(...) when you need component containers.
Use component_data_objects(...) when you need scalar leaf objects sent to solvers.
```

Pyomo’s block API exposes `component_objects(...)` for component objects and `component_data_objects(...)` for component data objects; both support recursive descent into sub-blocks by default. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

---

## 4.5 `Block` as modular submodel/container

### 4.5.1 Scalar block

```python id="oub4db"
m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

m.prod = pyo.Block()

m.prod.P = pyo.Set(initialize=["A", "B"])
m.prod.x = pyo.Var(m.prod.P, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
m.prod.capacity = pyo.Constraint(expr=sum(m.prod.x[p] for p in m.prod.P) <= 100)
```

Fully qualified names:

```python id="7w4p70"
m.prod.x["A"].name        # "prod.x[A]"
m.prod.capacity.name      # "prod.capacity"
m.prod.x.local_name       # "x"
```

Pyomo component APIs expose `.name` as the fully qualified name and `.local_name` as the name in the immediate parent container. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 4.5.2 Indexed block family

```python id="8go6av"
m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

m.TECH = pyo.Set(initialize=["solar", "wind", "gas"])
m.tech = pyo.Block(m.TECH)

for t in m.TECH:
    b = m.tech[t]
    b.capacity = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    b.dispatch = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    b.limit = pyo.Constraint(expr=b.dispatch <= b.capacity)
```

Object distinction:

```python id="lg6f21"
m.tech              # IndexedBlock component
m.tech["solar"]     # BlockData object
m.tech["solar"].capacity
```

### 4.5.3 Block rule/decorator construction

```python id="4y8ij6"
m.TECH = pyo.Set(initialize=["solar", "wind", "gas"])

def tech_block_rule(b, t):
    b.capacity = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    b.dispatch = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    b.limit = pyo.Constraint(expr=b.dispatch <= b.capacity)

m.tech = pyo.Block(m.TECH, rule=tech_block_rule)
```

Decorator style:

```python id="mpkc82"
@m.Block(m.TECH)
def tech(b, t):
    b.capacity = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    b.dispatch = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    b.limit = pyo.Constraint(expr=b.dispatch <= b.capacity)
```

Agent guidance:

```text id="d7ve9b"
Use explicit rule functions for production code.
Use decorators for compact examples/tests.
Use factory functions for reusable submodel templates.
```

---

## 4.6 Block factory pattern

### 4.6.1 Submodel builder

```python id="k99gks"
def build_generator_block(b, data):
    b.capacity = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    b.dispatch = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    b.capital_cost = pyo.Param(initialize=data["capital_cost"])
    b.variable_cost = pyo.Param(initialize=data["variable_cost"])
    b.max_capacity = pyo.Param(initialize=data["max_capacity"])

    b.capacity_limit = pyo.Constraint(expr=b.capacity <= b.max_capacity)
    b.dispatch_limit = pyo.Constraint(expr=b.dispatch <= b.capacity)

    b.cost = pyo.Expression(
        expr=b.capital_cost * b.capacity + b.variable_cost * b.dispatch
    )
```

### 4.6.2 Use inside model

```python id="0c5yug"
m = pyo.ConcreteModel()
m.G = pyo.Set(initialize=["g1", "g2"])
m.gen = pyo.Block(m.G)

for g in m.G:
    build_generator_block(m.gen[g], data["generators"][g])

m.demand = pyo.Param(initialize=data["demand"])
m.balance = pyo.Constraint(expr=sum(m.gen[g].dispatch for g in m.G) >= m.demand)
m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=sum(m.gen[g].cost for g in m.G))
```

Value case:

```text id="567pu3"
block factory:
  reusable unit model
  local names remain small
  hierarchical reporting
  selective activation/deactivation
  easier decomposition/refactoring
```

---

## 4.7 Component naming and lookup

### 4.7.1 Attribute registration

```python id="60x2ag"
m.x = pyo.Var()
```

Equivalent explicit registration:

```python id="msq0ea"
m.add_component("x", pyo.Var())
```

Pyomo block APIs include `add_component(name, val)` for adding a component to a block, and `component(name_or_object)` / `find_component(...)` for lookup. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 4.7.2 Lookup APIs

```python id="mchv8j"
m.component("x")
m.find_component("prod.x")
m.find_component("tech[solar].capacity")
```

### 4.7.3 Names

```python id="95f92g"
comp = m.tech["solar"].capacity

comp.name          # "tech[solar].capacity"
comp.local_name    # "capacity"
comp.parent_block()
comp.model()
```

Pyomo block/component APIs expose `model()`, `parent_block()`, `parent_component()`, `root_block()`, `.name`, and `.local_name`, supporting hierarchy-aware lookup and reporting. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 4.7.4 Naming best practices

```text id="l4wc3p"
Use noun names for components:
  capacity, dispatch, balance, objective

Use block names for domains/subsystems:
  gen, storage, network, market, policy

Avoid:
  x1, con2, tmp, test, expr unless genuinely temporary

Keep stable names:
  solver logs
  IIS/MIS diagnostics
  warm starts
  reporting
  downstream dashboards
```

---

## 4.8 Activation/deactivation semantics

### 4.8.1 Component-level activation

```python id="29ej9h"
m.c.deactivate()
m.c.activate()
```

Block APIs expose `activate()` to set the active attribute true and `deactivate()` to set it false. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 4.8.2 Objective switching

```python id="v37wsx"
m.cost_obj = pyo.Objective(expr=cost_expr, sense=pyo.minimize)
m.emissions_obj = pyo.Objective(expr=emissions_expr, sense=pyo.minimize)

m.emissions_obj.deactivate()

# later
m.cost_obj.deactivate()
m.emissions_obj.activate()
```

Agent rule:

```text id="k3gi6d"
Most solvers expect one active objective.
Multiple Objective components are allowed structurally, but active objective discipline is required.
```

### 4.8.3 Constraint-set toggles

```python id="uk18e6"
m.policy = pyo.Block()
m.policy.co2_cap = pyo.Constraint(expr=emissions <= cap)
m.policy.renewable_target = pyo.Constraint(expr=renewable >= target)

m.policy.deactivate()   # disables block and active descendants for traversal/export
m.policy.activate()
```

### 4.8.4 Scenario toggles

```python id="achao5"
for s in m.SCENARIOS:
    m.scenario[s].deactivate()

m.scenario["base"].activate()
```

Caution:

```text id="pqbxud"
Deactivation changes solver-exported algebraic system.
It does not delete components.
It does not clear variable values.
It does not invalidate Python references.
```

---

## 4.9 Cloning and copying

### 4.9.1 Full model clone

```python id="s0tzfi"
m2 = m.clone()
```

### 4.9.2 Block clone

```python id="379xm1"
sub = m.tech["solar"].clone()
```

Pyomo’s `clone()` deep-copies a block and recursively copies components owned by that block, including sub-blocks; components referenced from outside the block scope are not duplicated. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 4.9.3 Clone use cases

```text id="4d3fwn"
scenario branching
what-if analysis
Benders/decomposition subproblem copies
safe mutation experiments
unit tests with baseline model
```

### 4.9.4 Clone caveats

```text id="m0bmhw"
References to external components remain external.
Persistent solver instances are not automatically synchronized to clones.
Mutable Python objects embedded in user attributes may require audit.
Large model cloning can be memory-expensive.
```

### 4.9.5 Safe pattern

```python id="y40rgd"
base = build_model(data)

case_a = base.clone()
case_b = base.clone()

case_a.policy.co2_cap.deactivate()
case_b.policy.co2_cap.activate()
```

---

## 4.10 `Reference`: alias/view over existing components

### 4.10.1 Purpose

```text id="w200k1"
Reference = indexed component view into existing ComponentData.
It does not own its own data.
It provides a clean alias over slices across block hierarchy.
```

Pyomo’s `Reference` documentation states that it creates an indexed component that does not contain data but references data stored in other components through a component slice; changes through the reference reflect in the original objects. ([Pyomo Documentation][3])

### 4.10.2 Indexed block reference

```python id="h7ftmx"
m.G = pyo.Set(initialize=["g1", "g2"])

def gen_rule(b, g):
    b.p = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    b.cap = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    b.limit = pyo.Constraint(expr=b.p <= b.cap)

m.gen = pyo.Block(m.G, rule=gen_rule)

m.P = pyo.Reference(m.gen[:].p)
m.CAP = pyo.Reference(m.gen[:].cap)
```

Use:

```python id="524pjz"
m.balance = pyo.Constraint(expr=sum(m.P[g] for g in m.G) >= demand)
m.total_cap = pyo.Expression(expr=sum(m.CAP[g] for g in m.G))
```

### 4.10.3 Reference mutation

```python id="ej74qj"
m.P["g1"].setlb(10)
# equivalent to:
m.gen["g1"].p.setlb(10)
```

### 4.10.4 Best practices

```text id="ohgxzi"
Use Reference for reporting aliases and cross-block aggregate constraints.
Use Reference when slicing indexed block contents.
Avoid Reference when simple direct indexing is clearer.
Do not confuse Reference with cloning/copying; it aliases existing data.
```

---

## 4.11 `ExternalFunction`

### 4.11.1 Purpose

```python id="pc7b5u"
m.f = pyo.ExternalFunction(function=my_callback)
m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.f(m.x) <= 0)
```

`ExternalFunction` declares user-provided external functions and embeds calls to those functions in Pyomo expressions; it supports Python callback functions and AMPL external functions. The docs explicitly warn that representability does not imply solvability: linear solvers do not accept external functions, and ASL support for nonlinear solvers is interface-specific. ([Pyomo Documentation][4])

### 4.11.2 Python callback forms

```python id="3sbvb4"
def f(x):
    return x**2

m.f = pyo.ExternalFunction(function=f)
```

Gradient/Hessian-aware forms are supported by the API, but production use requires solver-interface compatibility and derivative correctness. ([Pyomo Documentation][4])

### 4.11.3 Deployment guidance

```text id="9t4edb"
Use only for nonlinear workflows where solver interface supports it.
Do not use with LP/MILP solvers.
Prefer native algebraic Pyomo expressions when possible.
Test callback numerically outside Pyomo.
Document derivative availability.
Avoid nondeterministic callbacks, IO, network calls, mutable global state.
```

---

## 4.12 `SOSConstraint`

### 4.12.1 Purpose

```python id="ge1a3s"
m.x = pyo.Var(m.I)
m.sos = pyo.SOSConstraint(var=m.x, sos=2)
```

Pyomo’s SOS docs define special ordered sets as variable sets where only a limited number of variables can be nonzero and nonzero members must be adjacent in a given order; explicit SOS declarations can shorten formulations because the logical enforcement can be handled algorithmically by compatible solvers. ([Pyomo Documentation][5])

### 4.12.2 Weighted SOS

```python id="0m95m1"
m.w = pyo.Param(m.I, initialize=weights)
m.sos = pyo.SOSConstraint(var=m.x, weights=m.w, sos=2)
```

### 4.12.3 Indexed SOS

```python id="dnf4mr"
m.K = pyo.Set(initialize=["seg1", "seg2"])
m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=[1, 2, 3, 4])
m.x = pyo.Var(m.K, m.I)

def sos_rule(m, k):
    return ([m.x[k, i] for i in m.I], list(m.I))

m.sos = pyo.SOSConstraint(m.K, rule=sos_rule, sos=2)
```

Deployment rule:

```text id="ajwwdw"
SOSConstraint value depends on solver support.
If solver lacks SOS support, use explicit linear/MIP reformulation instead.
```

---

## 4.13 Traversal APIs

### 4.13.1 `component_objects`

```python id="x2oyx4"
for var_component in m.component_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True):
    print(var_component.name, len(var_component))
```

Purpose:

```text id="5g30j5"
iterate component containers
e.g., all Var components: m.x, m.block.y, m.sub[i].z
not individual VarData leaf objects unless scalar
```

### 4.13.2 `component_data_objects`

```python id="xx89uk"
for v in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True):
    print(v.name, v.value, v.lb, v.ub)
```

Purpose:

```text id="tmbl74"
iterate leaf ComponentData objects
e.g., m.x[i], m.block.y[j], m.sub[k].z
best for reporting, fixing, bound audits, model statistics
```

### 4.13.3 `component_map`

```python id="h2240q"
var_map = m.component_map(pyo.Var, active=True)
for local_name, component in var_map.items():
    print(local_name, component.name)
```

Purpose:

```text id="hs0l63"
direct child components only unless you traverse manually
mapping-like object
good for local block introspection
```

### 4.13.4 `block_data_objects`

```python id="60ies1"
for b in m.block_data_objects(active=True, descend_into=True):
    print(b.name)
```

Purpose:

```text id="b2x3u6"
iterate root/sub-block data objects
honors active filter
supports hierarchy audits
```

Pyomo block APIs define `block_data_objects(...)`, `component_objects(...)`, `component_data_objects(...)`, and `component_map(...)`, with active filtering, sorting controls, and recursive descent behavior; deprecated `active_components`/`all_components`-style methods should be replaced with these modern APIs. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

---

## 4.14 Traversal filter semantics

### 4.14.1 `ctype`

```python id="hb3ifk"
m.component_data_objects(pyo.Var)
m.component_data_objects(pyo.Constraint)
m.component_data_objects((pyo.Var, pyo.Constraint))
```

Meaning:

```text id="d9n4t0"
None        -> all component types
single type -> only that ctype
iterable    -> any ctype in iterable
```

### 4.14.2 `active`

```python id="iwqrr9"
active_vars = list(m.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True))
inactive_cons = list(m.component_data_objects(pyo.Constraint, active=False))
all_objs = list(m.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=None))
```

Meaning:

```text id="9deizo"
active=True   -> active only
active=False  -> inactive only
active=None   -> all
```

### 4.14.3 `descend_into`

```python id="tt4jli"
local_vars = list(m.component_objects(pyo.Var, descend_into=False))
all_vars = list(m.component_objects(pyo.Var, descend_into=True))
```

Meaning:

```text id="9qofq5"
False -> current block only
True  -> recursively descend into sub-blocks
```

Pyomo’s block traversal docs state that `component_objects` and `component_data_objects` recursively descend into sub-blocks by default, while `block_data_objects(..., descend_into=False)` returns only the current block. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 4.14.4 `sort`

```python id="yndvs7"
for v in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, sort=True):
    ...
```

Meaning:

```text id="m10vwn"
sort=False -> declaration order
sort=True  -> deterministic alphabetic/component-index order
```

Pyomo’s API documents sorting behavior: `sort=True` uses alphabetized component/index ordering; `sort=False` uses declaration order. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

---

## 4.15 Model statistics helpers

### 4.15.1 Count variables and constraints

```python id="t2b9hh"
def model_stats(m: pyo.Block) -> dict:
    vars_ = list(m.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True))
    cons = list(m.component_data_objects(pyo.Constraint, active=True, descend_into=True))
    objs = list(m.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=True, descend_into=True))

    return {
        "n_vars": len(vars_),
        "n_binary": sum(v.is_binary() for v in vars_),
        "n_integer": sum(v.is_integer() for v in vars_),
        "n_continuous": sum(v.is_continuous() for v in vars_),
        "n_constraints": len(cons),
        "n_active_objectives": len(objs),
    }
```

### 4.15.2 Bound audit

```python id="zmmuoy"
def unbounded_variables(m: pyo.Block):
    return [
        v.name
        for v in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True)
        if v.lb is None and v.ub is None and not v.fixed
    ]
```

### 4.15.3 Active objective check

```python id="ktfpl4"
def require_single_active_objective(m: pyo.Block) -> None:
    objs = list(m.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=True, descend_into=True))
    if len(objs) != 1:
        raise ValueError(f"expected exactly one active objective, found {len(objs)}")
```

## 4.16 Component activation utilities

### 4.16.1 Deactivate by name pattern

```python id="cftyc0"
def deactivate_components_by_prefix(m: pyo.Block, prefix: str, ctype=pyo.Constraint):
    for comp in m.component_objects(ctype, active=True, descend_into=True):
        if comp.name.startswith(prefix):
            comp.deactivate()
```

### 4.16.2 Activate a scenario block

```python id="4rgq35"
def activate_only_scenario(m, scenario_name):
    for s in m.SCENARIOS:
        m.scenario[s].deactivate()
    m.scenario[scenario_name].activate()
```

### 4.16.3 Toggle formulation variant

```python id="zp5hau"
m.formulation = pyo.Block()
m.formulation.big_m = pyo.Block()
m.formulation.hull_like = pyo.Block()

# build both variants
m.formulation.big_m.activate()
m.formulation.hull_like.deactivate()
```

Deployment rule:

```text id="iofggs"
Do not delete components for scenario/formulation switches unless memory pressure requires it.
Prefer activate/deactivate for reversible switches.
```

---

## 4.17 Large hierarchical model architecture

### 4.17.1 Recommended tree

```text id="35mn3q"
model
  sets
  data
  units[unit_id]
    variables
    local constraints
    local expressions
  network
    flow variables
    arc constraints
  policy
    emissions constraints
    renewable constraints
  objective
  reporting References
```

### 4.17.2 Example skeleton

```python id="52ks4c"
def build_model(data):
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel(name="energy_system")

    m.U = pyo.Set(initialize=data.units)
    m.T = pyo.RangeSet(1, data.n_periods)

    m.unit = pyo.Block(m.U)
    for u in m.U:
        build_unit_block(m.unit[u], data.units[u], m.T)

    m.network = pyo.Block()
    build_network_block(m.network, data, m)

    m.policy = pyo.Block()
    build_policy_block(m.policy, data, m)

    m.dispatch = pyo.Reference(m.unit[:].dispatch[:, :])

    m.obj = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(m.unit[u].cost for u in m.U) + m.network.cost + m.policy.penalty
    )

    return m
```

### 4.17.3 Cross-block coupling rule

```text id="aq4buz"
Local constraints live inside the responsible block.
Coupling constraints live in a higher-level block.
Global constraints live at root or in dedicated policy/network blocks.
```

Good:

```python id="okn6o0"
m.unit[u].capacity_limit
m.network.balance[t]
m.policy.emissions_cap
```

Bad:

```python id="qp25p0"
m.c1
m.c2
m.c3
m.tmp_constraint_287
```

---

## 4.18 Submodel ownership boundaries

### 4.18.1 Local-only block

```python id="xvnbkw"
def build_storage_block(b, storage_data, T):
    b.T = pyo.Reference(T)  # or use T directly without storing
    b.energy = pyo.Var(T, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    b.charge = pyo.Var(T, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    b.discharge = pyo.Var(T, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    b.soc_limit = pyo.Constraint(T, rule=lambda b, t: b.energy[t] <= storage_data.capacity)
```

### 4.18.2 Parent-owned coupling

```python id="lyrx79"
def build_system(data):
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    m.T = pyo.RangeSet(1, data.n_periods)
    m.storage = pyo.Block()
    build_storage_block(m.storage, data.storage, m.T)

    m.load_balance = pyo.Constraint(
        m.T,
        rule=lambda m, t: m.storage.discharge[t] - m.storage.charge[t] >= data.load[t],
    )
    return m
```

Agent rule:

```text id="cct5ck"
Blocks should not reach upward into parent state unless explicitly passed.
Avoid hidden parent dependencies inside block builders.
```

## 4.22 Agent-safe introspection utilities

### 4.22.1 Component inventory

```python id="5e3b52"
def component_inventory(m: pyo.Block) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    out = {}
    for ctype in [pyo.Set, pyo.Param, pyo.Var, pyo.Objective, pyo.Constraint, pyo.Block]:
        out[ctype.__name__] = [
            comp.name
            for comp in m.component_objects(ctype, active=None, descend_into=True)
        ]
    return out
```

### 4.22.2 Leaf inventory

```python id="oicn0m"
def leaf_inventory(m: pyo.Block) -> dict[str, int]:
    return {
        "vars": sum(1 for _ in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True)),
        "constraints": sum(1 for _ in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Constraint, active=True)),
        "objectives": sum(1 for _ in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=True)),
        "blocks": sum(1 for _ in m.block_data_objects(active=True)),
    }
```

### 4.22.3 Hierarchy dump

```python id="4smus9"
def dump_blocks(m: pyo.Block):
    for b in m.block_data_objects(active=None, descend_into=True):
        print(b.name)
        for comp in b.component_objects(active=None, descend_into=False):
            print("  ", comp.local_name, comp.ctype.__name__)
```

## 4.23 Best practices for large hierarchical models

### 4.23.1 Architecture

```text id="z4e2uv"
Use Blocks for repeated units/subsystems/scenarios.
Use local constraints inside the block that owns local variables.
Use root or dedicated coupling blocks for cross-subsystem constraints.
Use References for clean aggregate/reporting aliases.
Use stable component names for diagnostics and reporting.
Use factories to build blocks; avoid copy-paste component declarations.
```

### 4.23.2 Traversal

```text id="uaytvg"
Use component_data_objects for leaf-level audits.
Use component_objects for container-level toggles.
Use descend_into=False for local block operations.
Use active=True for solver-export-relevant counts.
Use sort=True for deterministic reports/tests.
Avoid deprecated traversal APIs.
```

### 4.23.3 Activation

```text id="c1ztu2"
Use deactivate/activate for scenario/formulation toggles.
Keep exactly one active objective unless solver/interface explicitly supports otherwise.
Deactivate experimental constraints instead of deleting during model development.
Use block-level activation to toggle entire policy/scenario modules.
```

### 4.23.4 Cloning

```text id="g19r3e"
Clone before destructive what-if edits.
Do not assume references become independent copies.
Do not reuse persistent solver instance across clones without reset.
Record clone lineage in experiments.
```

### 4.23.5 Component naming

```text id="dmc5ch"
Prefer:
  m.unit[u].capacity
  m.unit[u].dispatch[t]
  m.network.balance[n, t]
  m.policy.emissions_cap

Avoid:
  m.x
  m.y
  m.c
  m.c2
  m.temp
for production-scale models unless mathematically conventional and documented.
```

---

## 4.24 Common anti-patterns

| Anti-pattern                                                           | Failure mode                              | Replacement                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| One flat model with thousands of anonymous constraints                 | impossible debugging/reporting            | block hierarchy by subsystem                                        |
| Cross-block constraints hidden inside child block using parent globals | tight coupling, reuse failure             | parent-level coupling constraints                                   |
| Using `component_objects` when leaf values needed                      | extracts containers, not scalar variables | `component_data_objects`                                            |
| Forgetting `descend_into=True`                                         | missing nested components                 | explicit traversal parameter                                        |
| Multiple active objectives                                             | solver/export ambiguity                   | deactivate inactive objectives                                      |
| Deleting components for reversible scenario switch                     | expensive/error-prone                     | `deactivate()`/`activate()`                                         |
| Cloning huge models in loops                                           | memory blowup                             | mutable params / persistent solver / rebuild targeted blocks        |
| Treating `Reference` as copy                                           | mutations affect original                 | use `clone()` for copy                                              |
| External functions with MILP solver                                    | unsolvable model                          | native algebraic expression or compatible NLP solver                |
| Relying on deprecated traversal APIs                                   | future compatibility risk                 | `component_objects`, `component_data_objects`, `block_data_objects` |

---

## 4.25 Minimal production skeleton

```python id="s4xkza"
import pyomo.environ as pyo


def build_unit_block(b, unit_data, T):
    b.T = pyo.Reference(T)

    b.capacity = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    b.dispatch = pyo.Var(T, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    b.max_capacity = pyo.Param(initialize=unit_data.max_capacity)
    b.variable_cost = pyo.Param(initialize=unit_data.variable_cost)

    b.capacity_limit = pyo.Constraint(expr=b.capacity <= b.max_capacity)

    def dispatch_limit_rule(b, t):
        return b.dispatch[t] <= b.capacity

    b.dispatch_limit = pyo.Constraint(T, rule=dispatch_limit_rule)

    b.cost = pyo.Expression(expr=sum(b.variable_cost * b.dispatch[t] for t in T))


def build_model(data):
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel(name="hierarchical_dispatch")

    m.U = pyo.Set(initialize=data.units, ordered=True)
    m.T = pyo.RangeSet(1, data.n_periods)

    m.unit = pyo.Block(m.U)
    for u in m.U:
        build_unit_block(m.unit[u], data.unit[u], m.T)

    m.dispatch = pyo.Reference(m.unit[:].dispatch[:])
    m.capacity = pyo.Reference(m.unit[:].capacity)

    def balance_rule(m, t):
        return sum(m.unit[u].dispatch[t] for u in m.U) >= data.demand[t]

    m.balance = pyo.Constraint(m.T, rule=balance_rule)
    m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=sum(m.unit[u].cost for u in m.U))

    return m
```

# 5) Sets and indexing — Pyomo deep dive

Style target: uploaded advanced technical-doc plan. 

Pyomo `Set` objects are **indexing substrates**, **domain validators**, and **model-shape controls**. Pyomo’s `Set` class is a Pyomo component used to index other components; it is API-compatible with Python set objects but adds member validation/filtering and symbolic set expressions whose operands remain linked to the source sets. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

---

## 5.0 Core mental model

```text id="7m7p2i"
Set:
  finite or virtual membership collection
  indexes Var / Param / Constraint / Block / Set
  validates dimensionality and allowed members
  controls generated model size

RangeSet:
  compact numeric sequence set
  preferred for simple ordered numeric ranges

Virtual set:
  expression over sets, e.g. A * B, A | B
  stores expression / references, not necessarily concrete members

Sparse set:
  explicit valid tuple subset
  avoids dense Cartesian product explosion
```

High-impact agent invariant:

```text id="29roqy"
Index sets define the algebraic shape of the model.
Bad index sets create wrong constraints, large memory footprints, slow construction, or invalid solver exports.
```

---

## 5.1 Declaration surface

### 5.1.1 Empty / data-deferred set

```python id="0wnobf"
import pyomo.environ as pyo

m = pyo.ConcreteModel()
m.A = pyo.Set()
```

Pyomo docs show `model.A = pyo.Set()` as the simplest declaration, postponing member creation. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 5.1.2 Initialized finite set

```python id="ehthd5"
m.COLORS = pyo.Set(initialize=["red", "green", "blue"])
```

`initialize` accepts Python iterables such as `set`, `list`, or `tuple`, directly or returned from a function. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 5.1.3 Numeric range

```python id="rqc1r4"
m.T = pyo.RangeSet(1, 24)
m.K = pyo.RangeSet(0, 10, 2)
m.GRID = pyo.RangeSet(1.5, 10, 3.5)
```

`RangeSet` compactly represents simple numeric sequences; with one argument, the value is the final value and start/step default to one; with two arguments, they are first and last; with three, the third is the step. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 5.1.4 Multi-dimensional tuple set

```python id="or29i4"
m.ARCS = pyo.Set(dimen=2)
m.TRIANGLES = pyo.Set(dimen=3)
```

`dimen` specifies the arity / tuple length required for set members; `None` permits jagged sets. Pyomo attempts to infer dimensionality, but explicit `dimen` is needed when inference is impossible or when the modeler wants to assert member arity. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

---

## 5.2 `Set(...)` keyword taxonomy

```python id="p45lfe"
m.S = pyo.Set(
    initialize=...,
    dimen=...,
    ordered=...,
    within=...,
    domain=...,
    bounds=...,
    filter=...,
    validate=...,
    doc="...",
)
```

| Keyword      | Meaning                                             | Failure / behavior                        |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `initialize` | iterable, generator, function, dict-for-indexed-set | populates members at construction         |
| `dimen`      | tuple arity / member dimensionality                 | rejects wrong-length members              |
| `ordered`    | iteration ordering policy                           | affects deterministic iteration/reporting |
| `within`     | super-set / domain of valid members                 | invalid members rejected                  |
| `domain`     | synonym-style domain restriction                    | intersects with `within` / `bounds`       |
| `bounds`     | numeric bounds restriction                          | intersects with `domain` / `within`       |
| `filter`     | construction-time predicate                         | invalid candidates silently ignored       |
| `validate`   | construction-time predicate                         | invalid candidates raise `ValueError`     |
| `doc`        | documentation string                                | introspection / `pprint` metadata         |

The `Set` API documents `initialize`, `dimen`, `ordered`, `within`, `domain`, `bounds`, `filter`, and `validate`; `filter` returns true for accepted members and quietly ignores false members, while `validate` returns true for valid members and raises `ValueError` for false members. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

---

## 5.3 Ordering semantics

### 5.3.1 Default insertion order

```python id="08hkxo"
m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=["b", "a", "c"], ordered=True)
```

`ordered=True` means insertion order; the API identifies insertion order as the default ordered behavior. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

### 5.3.2 Explicit sorted order

```python id="5hybv2"
m.I = pyo.Set(
    initialize=["b", "a", "c"],
    ordered=pyo.Set.SortedOrder,
)
```

### 5.3.3 Unordered set

```python id="rl1bk7"
m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=["b", "a", "c"], ordered=False)
```

Agent guidance:

```text id="5n7a1x"
Use ordered=True / insertion order for data-preserving reproducibility.
Use Set.SortedOrder for deterministic canonical output independent of input order.
Avoid unordered sets for generated reports, tests, warm starts, and diffable artifacts.
```

---

## 5.4 Dimensionality and tuple indexing

### 5.4.1 One-dimensional set

```python id="zvaqtp"
m.NODES = pyo.Set(initialize=["A", "B", "C"])
m.supply = pyo.Param(m.NODES, initialize={"A": 2, "B": 0, "C": 0})
```

### 5.4.2 Two-dimensional tuple set

```python id="lyzg0i"
m.ARCS = pyo.Set(
    dimen=2,
    initialize=[("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("C", "B")],
)

m.flow = pyo.Var(m.ARCS, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
m.cost = pyo.Param(
    m.ARCS,
    initialize={
        ("A", "B"): 1.4,
        ("A", "C"): 2.7,
        ("C", "B"): 1.6,
    },
)
```

### 5.4.3 Tuple flattening in rule signatures

```python id="bzn5p8"
def arc_capacity_rule(m, i, j):
    return m.flow[i, j] <= m.capacity[i, j]

m.arc_capacity = pyo.Constraint(m.ARCS, rule=arc_capacity_rule)
```

Rule-signature invariant:

```text id="2ntsnr"
Constraint(m.ARCS, rule=f), where ARCS has dimen=2:
  f(m, i, j)

Constraint(m.I, m.ARCS, rule=f):
  f(m, i, arc_i, arc_j)
```

### 5.4.4 Jagged sets

```python id="esxva9"
m.JAGGED = pyo.Set(dimen=None)
```

Use sparingly:

```text id="jw8yo8"
dimen=None permits variable-length members.
Good for metadata collections.
Bad for optimization indexing unless every downstream access handles shape variation.
```

---

## 5.5 Initialization patterns

### 5.5.1 Direct list/tuple/set

```python id="vpnc2h"
m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=["A", "B", "C"])
m.J = pyo.Set(initialize=("x", "y", "z"))
m.K = pyo.Set(initialize={1, 2, 3})
```

### 5.5.2 Generator function

```python id="cl1sqr"
def odd_init(m):
    for i in range(10):
        yield 2 * i + 1

m.ODD = pyo.Set(initialize=odd_init)
```

Pyomo docs show generator initialization where every yielded value becomes an initial set member. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 5.5.3 Function returning iterable

```python id="uiefz2"
def odd_list_init(m):
    return [2 * i + 1 for i in range(10)]

m.ODD2 = pyo.Set(initialize=odd_list_init)
```

Pyomo supports initialization functions that return an iterable such as a `set`, `list`, or `tuple`. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 5.5.4 Element-by-element initializer with `Set.End`

```python id="1ifpwz"
def z_init(m, i):
    if i > 10:
        return pyo.Set.End
    return 2 * i + 1

m.Z = pyo.Set(initialize=z_init)
```

The element-by-element initializer receives an element number starting at 1 and continues until the initializer returns `Set.End`. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 5.5.5 Derived set from another set

```python id="u9x6f5"
m.A = pyo.Set(initialize=[1, 2, 3])

def doubled_init(m):
    return (2 * i for i in m.A)

m.DOUBLE_A = pyo.Set(initialize=doubled_init)
```

Pyomo docs show deriving one set from another using an initialization function that returns a generator expression. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

---

## 5.6 Indexed sets: set arrays

### 5.6.1 Set indexed by another set

```python id="vjr9ha"
m.PLANTS = pyo.Set(initialize=["P1", "P2"])
m.PRODUCTS_AT_PLANT = pyo.Set(m.PLANTS)
```

If sets are passed to `Set` positionally, Pyomo interprets them as indexes for an array of sets. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 5.6.2 Indexed set with dimensional members

```python id="mgefed"
m.F = pyo.Set(m.PLANTS, dimen=3)
```

Pyomo supports combining positional indexing sets with `dimen`, e.g., an array of sets where each local set contains three-dimensional members. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 5.6.3 Indexed-set initialization by indexed function

```python id="7bse24"
plant_to_products = {
    "P1": ["A", "B"],
    "P2": ["B", "C"],
}

def products_at_plant_init(m, p):
    return plant_to_products[p]

m.PRODUCTS_AT_PLANT = pyo.Set(m.PLANTS, initialize=products_at_plant_init)
```

### 5.6.4 Indexed-set initialization by dictionary

```python id="c4uuun"
m.PRODUCTS_AT_PLANT = pyo.Set(
    m.PLANTS,
    initialize={
        "P1": ["A", "B"],
        "P2": ["B", "C"],
    },
)
```

Use indexed sets for **adjacency**, **allowed assignments**, **local product menus**, **scenario-specific support**, and **sparse neighbor lists**.

---

## 5.7 AbstractModel data override rule

```python id="ccumf7"
template = pyo.AbstractModel()
template.I = pyo.Set(initialize=["default_a", "default_b"])

instance = template.create_instance({
    None: {
        "I": {None: ["data_a", "data_b", "data_c"]},
    }
})
```

For abstract models, set data supplied in an input file or through `AbstractModel.create_instance(data=...)` overrides values specified by `initialize`. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

Agent rule:

```text id="q283az"
In AbstractModel, initialize is a default/template hint.
create_instance data is authoritative.
```

---

## 5.8 Validation: `within`, `domain`, `bounds`, `filter`, `validate`

### 5.8.1 `within`: membership domain

```python id="mfqdrq"
m.NODES = pyo.Set(initialize=["A", "B", "C"])
m.ARCS = pyo.Set(
    dimen=2,
    within=m.NODES * m.NODES,
    initialize=[("A", "B"), ("C", "B")],
)
```

`within` defines a set of valid values; when combined with cross products, it constrains tuple members to valid Cartesian combinations. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

### 5.8.2 Virtual numeric domains

```python id="cttozp"
m.NEGATIVE_IDS = pyo.Set(within=pyo.NegativeIntegers)
m.PROB_LEVELS = pyo.Set(within=pyo.UnitInterval)
m.BINARY_CODES = pyo.Set(within=pyo.Binary)
```

Pyomo provides predefined virtual sets such as `Any`, `Reals`, `NonNegativeReals`, `Integers`, `NonNegativeIntegers`, `Boolean`, and `Binary` for domains of sets, parameters, and variables. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 5.8.3 `domain` / `within` / `bounds` intersection

```python id="2rmrqf"
m.SMALL_POSITIVE = pyo.Set(
    within=pyo.PositiveIntegers,
    bounds=(1, 10),
)
```

The `Set` API notes that `domain=`, `within=`, and `bounds=` all restrict valid values; when more than one is supplied, valid members are restricted to the intersection of those restrictions. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

### 5.8.4 `filter`: silently ignore candidates

```python id="qox0uf"
def even_filter(m, i):
    return i % 2 == 0

m.EVEN = pyo.Set(
    initialize=range(10),
    filter=even_filter,
)
```

Result members:

```text id="m5etcd"
0, 2, 4, 6, 8
```

`filter` returns true when data belongs in the set and silently ignores candidates where the rule returns false. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

### 5.8.5 `validate`: raise on invalid candidates

```python id="gfwvsr"
def nonzero_validate(m, i):
    return i != 0

m.NONZERO = pyo.Set(
    initialize=[1, 2, 0, 3],
    validate=nonzero_validate,
)
```

`validate` returns true for valid members and raises `ValueError` for members where the rule returns false. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

### 5.8.6 `filter` vs `validate` decision table

| Goal                              | Use                                        |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| silently drop unusable candidates | `filter`                                   |
| fail fast on bad data             | `validate`                                 |
| enforce domain membership         | `within` / `domain`                        |
| enforce numeric bounds            | `bounds`                                   |
| enforce tuple length              | `dimen`                                    |
| enforce complex relationship      | `validate` with explicit error expectation |

Agent default:

```text id="3ha2lu"
Production data pipelines:
  prefer validate for bad input
  use filter only when candidate rejection is intended behavior
```

---

## 5.9 Set algebra

### 5.9.1 Union

```python id="i8ox5n"
m.ALL_PRODUCTS = m.DOMESTIC | m.IMPORTED
```

### 5.9.2 Intersection

```python id="0brtgm"
m.ACTIVE_AND_ELIGIBLE = m.ACTIVE & m.ELIGIBLE
```

### 5.9.3 Difference

```python id="ms0x2j"
m.NON_RENEWABLE = m.TECH - m.RENEWABLE
```

### 5.9.4 Symmetric difference

```python id="z1i57p"
m.EXACTLY_ONE_SIDE = m.A ^ m.B
```

Pyomo supports set operations including union `|`, intersection `&`, difference `-`, and symmetric difference `^`. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 5.9.5 Cross product

```python id="b57qrh"
m.IJ = m.I * m.J
```

The cross-product operator is `*`; `model.B * model.C` creates a virtual set holding references to the original sets, so updates to those original sets are reflected in the virtual set. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 5.9.6 Concrete materialization of set expression

```python id="ny5e1y"
m.IJ_concrete = pyo.Set(initialize=m.I * m.J)
```

Materializing with `pyo.Set(initialize=...)` directly stores values of the cross product at construction time and does not reflect later changes to the source sets. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 5.9.7 Domain restriction with set algebra

```python id="hc81wh"
m.ARCS = pyo.Set(within=m.NODES * m.NODES)
```

Use `within=m.B * m.C` when members should be validated against a Cartesian domain without materializing every pair. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

---

## 5.10 Virtual sets vs concrete sets

```python id="wb9xpv"
m.IJ_virtual = m.I * m.J
m.IJ_concrete = pyo.Set(initialize=m.I * m.J)
```

| Feature                             | Virtual expression       | Concrete set               |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------- |
| Stores members                      | not necessarily          | yes                        |
| Tracks source set updates           | yes                      | no                         |
| Good for domains                    | yes                      | sometimes                  |
| Good for iteration with fixed data  | sometimes                | yes                        |
| Memory footprint                    | lower for large products | higher                     |
| Deterministic materialized contents | source-dependent         | construction-time snapshot |

Agent rule:

```text id="29olml"
Use virtual cross products for domains and compact declarations.
Use concrete sparse sets for actual variables/constraints when only a subset is valid.
```

---

## 5.11 Sparse indexing: network model pattern

### 5.11.1 Dense anti-pattern

```python id="8h52es"
m.NODES = pyo.Set(initialize=nodes)
m.ARCS = m.NODES * m.NODES
m.flow = pyo.Var(m.ARCS, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
```

This creates variables for all ordered node pairs. Pyomo’s docs note that a dense node cross product can suffice only when all nodes are always connected; for sparse networks, it forces the data/model to avoid nonexistent arcs indirectly, e.g., by assigning high costs, which the docs call inelegant and non-robust. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 5.11.2 Sparse arc set

```python id="ot0fjs"
m.NODES = pyo.Set(initialize=["CityA", "CityB", "CityC"])

m.ARCS = pyo.Set(
    dimen=2,
    within=m.NODES * m.NODES,
    initialize=[
        ("CityA", "CityB"),
        ("CityA", "CityC"),
        ("CityC", "CityB"),
    ],
)

m.flow = pyo.Var(m.ARCS, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
m.flow_cost = pyo.Param(m.ARCS)
```

Pyomo docs recommend declaring arcs as a sparse two-dimensional set, optionally with `within=model.Nodes * model.Nodes`, to represent sparse networks naturally. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 5.11.3 Naive sparse balance: membership checks inside dense node loops

```python id="bvmq1o"
def balance_rule(m, n):
    return (
        m.supply[n]
        + sum(m.flow[i, n] for i in m.NODES if (i, n) in m.ARCS)
        - m.demand[n]
        - sum(m.flow[n, j] for j in m.NODES if (n, j) in m.ARCS)
        == 0
    )

m.balance = pyo.Constraint(m.NODES, rule=balance_rule)
```

Pyomo docs show this pattern as a valid sparse rewrite but warn that, for very large sparse networks, repeatedly scanning all nodes during constraint generation can become an issue. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 5.11.4 Adjacency indexed sets: efficient balance

```python id="kxbwv0"
def nodes_out_init(m, n):
    for i, j in m.ARCS:
        if i == n:
            yield j

def nodes_in_init(m, n):
    for i, j in m.ARCS:
        if j == n:
            yield i

m.NODES_OUT = pyo.Set(m.NODES, initialize=nodes_out_init, within=m.NODES)
m.NODES_IN = pyo.Set(m.NODES, initialize=nodes_in_init, within=m.NODES)

def balance_rule(m, n):
    return (
        m.supply[n]
        + sum(m.flow[i, n] for i in m.NODES_IN[n])
        - m.demand[n]
        - sum(m.flow[n, j] for j in m.NODES_OUT[n])
        == 0
    )

m.balance = pyo.Constraint(m.NODES, rule=balance_rule)
```

Pyomo docs recommend inbound/outbound adjacency sets (`NodesIn`, `NodesOut`) to avoid scanning the full node set in each flow-balance constraint; they also note that providing these adjacency sets directly in input data may be the most efficient option. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 5.11.5 Dictionary-based adjacency initialization

```python id="tugj22"
def nodes_in_init(m):
    d = {n: [] for n in m.NODES}
    for i, j in m.ARCS:
        d[j].append(i)
    return d

def nodes_out_init(m):
    d = {n: [] for n in m.NODES}
    for i, j in m.ARCS:
        d[i].append(j)
    return d

m.NODES_IN = pyo.Set(m.NODES, initialize=nodes_in_init, within=m.NODES)
m.NODES_OUT = pyo.Set(m.NODES, initialize=nodes_out_init, within=m.NODES)
```

Pyomo docs present dictionary-returning initialization as more efficient than repeatedly scanning arcs for each node because it iterates over arcs only twice. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 5.11.6 Concrete post-declaration population

```python id="htjccq"
m.NODES_IN = pyo.Set(m.NODES, within=m.NODES)
m.NODES_OUT = pyo.Set(m.NODES, within=m.NODES)

for i, j in m.ARCS:
    m.NODES_IN[j].add(i)
    m.NODES_OUT[i].add(j)
```

Pyomo docs describe direct `.add(...)` population after declaration for concrete models and identify it as an efficient and clear alternative outside `Set` initialization. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 5.11.7 AbstractModel deferred population with `BuildAction`

```python id="lj55ab"
template.NODES_IN = pyo.Set(template.NODES, within=template.NODES)
template.NODES_OUT = pyo.Set(template.NODES, within=template.NODES)

def populate_in_and_out(m):
    for i, j in m.ARCS:
        m.NODES_IN[j].add(i)
        m.NODES_OUT[i].add(j)

template.POPULATE_ADJACENCY = pyo.BuildAction(rule=populate_in_and_out)
```

For abstract models, Pyomo docs state that concrete population actions must be deferred to instance construction time using `BuildAction`. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

---

## 5.12 Sparse indexing: assignment / nested-support pattern

### 5.12.1 Problem shape

```text id="5w3ol9"
Need constraints:
  for all i in I, k in K, v in V[k]

Bad dense index:
  I * K * V_all
```

### 5.12.2 Build sparse `(k, v)` support

```python id="gaj1ab"
m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=["i1", "i2"])
m.K = pyo.Set(initialize=["k1", "k2"])

m.V = pyo.Set(
    m.K,
    initialize={
        "k1": ["v1", "v2"],
        "k2": ["v3"],
    },
)

def kv_init(m):
    return ((k, v) for k in m.K for v in m.V[k])

m.KV = pyo.Set(dimen=2, initialize=kv_init)
```

### 5.12.3 Use sparse tuple support in variables/constraints

```python id="u5g0ky"
m.a = pyo.Param(m.I, m.K, default=1)
m.y = pyo.Var(m.I)
m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, m.KV)

def c1_rule(m, i, k, v):
    return m.x[i, k, v] <= m.a[i, k] * m.y[i]

m.c1 = pyo.Constraint(m.I, m.KV, rule=c1_rule)
```

Pyomo’s sparse-index example recommends creating a set of tuples for all `(k, v)` pairs from `K` and indexed set `V[k]`, then using `Constraint(model.I, model.KV, rule=...)`. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

---

## 5.13 Sparse variable construction patterns

### 5.13.1 Sparse tuple index only

```python id="48o65c"
m.x = pyo.Var(m.ARCS, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
```

Access:

```python id="b34y1d"
m.x["A", "B"]
```

### 5.13.2 Mixed dense × sparse

```python id="kf9e0i"
m.x = pyo.Var(m.TIME, m.ARCS, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

def cap_rule(m, t, i, j):
    return m.x[t, i, j] <= m.arc_capacity[i, j]

m.cap = pyo.Constraint(m.TIME, m.ARCS, rule=cap_rule)
```

### 5.13.3 Sparse support as one explicit tuple set

```python id="apvrc9"
def time_arc_init(m):
    return ((t, i, j) for t in m.TIME for (i, j) in m.ARCS if available(t, i, j))

m.TIME_ARCS = pyo.Set(dimen=3, initialize=time_arc_init)
m.x = pyo.Var(m.TIME_ARCS, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

def cap_rule(m, t, i, j):
    return m.x[t, i, j] <= m.arc_capacity[i, j]

m.cap = pyo.Constraint(m.TIME_ARCS, rule=cap_rule)
```

Agent rule:

```text id="p4v1b3"
If feasibility/availability is sparse in the combined index space, build the combined sparse tuple set.
Do not create dense products and skip most constraints unless the model is small.
```

---

## 5.14 Constraint-generation performance

### 5.14.1 Avoid nested full-set scans inside indexed rules

Slow for large sparse networks:

```python id="s5f1ub"
def balance_rule(m, n):
    return (
        sum(m.flow[i, n] for i in m.NODES if (i, n) in m.ARCS)
        - sum(m.flow[n, j] for j in m.NODES if (n, j) in m.ARCS)
        == rhs(n)
    )
```

Complexity:

```text id="dyf8s3"
O(|N|^2) membership loop pattern for all node constraints
```

Better:

```python id="9gkv80"
def balance_rule(m, n):
    return (
        sum(m.flow[i, n] for i in m.NODES_IN[n])
        - sum(m.flow[n, j] for j in m.NODES_OUT[n])
        == rhs(n)
    )
```

Complexity:

```text id="6yszvu"
O(|A|) aggregate term-generation across all node constraints
```

Pyomo docs explicitly flag full-node scans in sparse network constraints as a construction-time issue for very large sparse networks and present `NodesIn`/`NodesOut` adjacency sets as the remedy. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 5.14.2 Precompute Python dictionaries before Pyomo construction

```python id="x9ghos"
from collections import defaultdict

nodes_in = defaultdict(list)
nodes_out = defaultdict(list)

for i, j in arcs:
    nodes_out[i].append(j)
    nodes_in[j].append(i)

m.NODES_IN = pyo.Set(m.NODES, initialize=lambda m, n: nodes_in[n], within=m.NODES)
m.NODES_OUT = pyo.Set(m.NODES, initialize=lambda m, n: nodes_out[n], within=m.NODES)
```

Use when:

```text id="wpbnp6"
ConcreteModel
large graph
data already Python-native
index construction is a performance bottleneck
```

### 5.14.3 Avoid `Constraint.Skip` as a primary sparsity mechanism

Dense-skip anti-pattern:

```python id="7a27ow"
def assignment_rule(m, i, j):
    if (i, j) not in m.ALLOWED:
        return pyo.Constraint.Skip
    return m.x[i, j] <= 1

m.assign = pyo.Constraint(m.I, m.J, rule=assignment_rule)
```

Sparse-index replacement:

```python id="b6pr5g"
m.ALLOWED = pyo.Set(dimen=2, initialize=allowed_pairs, within=m.I * m.J)

def assignment_rule(m, i, j):
    return m.x[i, j] <= 1

m.assign = pyo.Constraint(m.ALLOWED, rule=assignment_rule)
```

Agent rule:

```text id="lr4928"
Use Constraint.Skip for rare conditional exclusions.
Use sparse sets for structural sparsity.
```

---

## 5.15 Dense vs sparse model-size example

### 5.15.1 Dense assignment

```python id="k3wd51"
m.W = pyo.Set(initialize=workers)
m.T = pyo.Set(initialize=tasks)

m.assign = pyo.Var(m.W, m.T, domain=pyo.Binary)
```

Variable count:

```text id="jp9ru6"
|W| * |T|
```

### 5.15.2 Sparse assignment

```python id="5f6lqn"
m.ALLOWED = pyo.Set(
    dimen=2,
    within=m.W * m.T,
    initialize=allowed_worker_task_pairs,
)

m.assign = pyo.Var(m.ALLOWED, domain=pyo.Binary)
```

Variable count:

```text id="38zrcc"
|ALLOWED|
```

### 5.15.3 Cost objective

```python id="37n4au"
m.cost = pyo.Param(m.ALLOWED)

m.obj = pyo.Objective(
    expr=sum(m.cost[w, t] * m.assign[w, t] for (w, t) in m.ALLOWED)
)
```

### 5.15.4 Task coverage

Efficient indexed set:

```python id="e1jlnc"
def workers_for_task_init(m):
    d = {t: [] for t in m.T}
    for w, t in m.ALLOWED:
        d[t].append(w)
    return d

m.WORKERS_FOR_TASK = pyo.Set(m.T, initialize=workers_for_task_init, within=m.W)

def cover_rule(m, t):
    return sum(m.assign[w, t] for w in m.WORKERS_FOR_TASK[t]) == 1

m.cover = pyo.Constraint(m.T, rule=cover_rule)
```

## 5.16 ConcreteModel set mutation

### 5.16.1 Add member to scalar set

```python id="cs7mhv"
m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=["A"])
m.I.add("B")
```

### 5.16.2 Add member to indexed set

```python id="xwhv7g"
m.NODES_IN = pyo.Set(m.NODES, within=m.NODES)

m.NODES_IN["B"].add("A")
```

Pyomo’s sparse-index docs show adding members to indexed sets after declaration for concrete models using `.add(...)`. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 5.16.3 Rebuild-warning for indexed components

```text id="2bcrkz"
Adding elements to an index set after Var/Param/Constraint construction does not automatically create new variable/constraint data everywhere in the way novice users expect.
For structural changes, rebuild the model or use controlled dynamic component creation.
```

Production rule:

```text id="93jsxz"
Treat sets as structural input.
Finalize sets before declaring variables and constraints.
Use mutable Params for repeated numeric changes.
Rebuild for structural index changes.
```

## 5.17 AbstractModel set mutation

```python id="iapne4"
template.NODES_IN = pyo.Set(template.NODES, within=template.NODES)
template.NODES_OUT = pyo.Set(template.NODES, within=template.NODES)

def populate(m):
    for i, j in m.ARCS:
        m.NODES_OUT[i].add(j)
        m.NODES_IN[j].add(i)

template.populate_adjacency = pyo.BuildAction(rule=populate)
```

Use `BuildAction` when abstract-model set population must occur after instance data is loaded; Pyomo docs explicitly state that this action must be deferred to instance construction time for abstract models. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])
