## 5.19 Deployment advisory

### 5.19.1 Data-validation layer

Validate before model construction:

```python id="rcl0x1"
def validate_arcs(nodes, arcs):
    nodes = set(nodes)

    bad = [(i, j) for i, j in arcs if i not in nodes or j not in nodes]
    if bad:
        raise ValueError(f"arcs reference unknown nodes: {bad[:10]}")

    duplicates = len(arcs) != len(set(arcs))
    if duplicates:
        raise ValueError("duplicate arcs detected")
```

Then declare:

```python id="7kpn7w"
m.NODES = pyo.Set(initialize=nodes, ordered=True)
m.ARCS = pyo.Set(dimen=2, within=m.NODES * m.NODES, initialize=arcs)
```

### 5.19.2 Large-model memory control

```text id="4nz0xd"
Avoid m.I * m.J * m.K for large dimensions unless truly dense.
Prefer explicit sparse tuple sets.
Precompute adjacency maps.
Avoid repeated membership checks in rule bodies.
Use ordered sets for reproducible artifacts.
Keep set members lightweight: str/int tuples preferred.
Avoid mutable Python objects as set members.
```

### 5.19.3 Reporting contract

```python id="elsv8e"
def write_index_manifest(m):
    return {
        "sets": {
            "NODES": len(m.NODES),
            "ARCS": len(m.ARCS),
        },
        "variables": {
            "flow": len(m.flow),
        },
        "constraints": {
            "balance": len(m.balance),
        },
    }
```

### 5.19.4 CI checks

```text id="4c0zik"
[ ] set cardinalities match expected data
[ ] tuple dimensions match formulation
[ ] sparse variables have sparse counts
[ ] no unintended dense products
[ ] domain validation catches invalid data
[ ] adjacency sets agree with tuple support
[ ] generated constraints use adjacency sets, not dense filtering loops
```

---

## 5.20 Anti-pattern table

| Anti-pattern                                                 | Failure mode                     | Replacement                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| Dense Cartesian product for sparse arcs                      | huge variable/constraint count   | `Set(dimen=2, initialize=arcs)`             |
| `if (i, j) in m.ARCS` inside every node loop                 | slow model construction          | `NODES_IN[n]`, `NODES_OUT[n]`               |
| Using `filter` to hide bad data                              | silent data loss                 | `validate` / pre-Pyomo validation           |
| Omitting `dimen` for tuple sets                              | shape ambiguity                  | `Set(dimen=2)` / `Set(dimen=3)`             |
| Unordered sets in reproducible pipelines                     | nondeterministic output          | `ordered=True` or `Set.SortedOrder`         |
| `Constraint.Skip` for structural sparsity                    | expensive dense iteration        | sparse index set                            |
| Mutating sets after dependent components built               | missing component data           | finalize sets before component declarations |
| Using cross product as actual index when subset is valid     | dense model and artificial costs | sparse tuple set with `within=`             |
| AbstractModel post-data set population in normal Python loop | runs before data exists          | `BuildAction`                               |
| Jagged sets as optimization indexes                          | rule-shape bugs                  | fixed `dimen` tuple sets                    |

---

## 5.21 Agent-ready production template: sparse network

```python id="2bpo4v"
from __future__ import annotations

from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass

import pyomo.environ as pyo


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NetworkData:
    nodes: tuple[str, ...]
    arcs: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]
    cost: dict[tuple[str, str], float]
    supply: dict[str, float]
    demand: dict[str, float]


def validate_network_data(data: NetworkData) -> None:
    nodes = set(data.nodes)
    arcs = set(data.arcs)

    if len(arcs) != len(data.arcs):
        raise ValueError("duplicate arcs")

    bad_arcs = [(i, j) for i, j in data.arcs if i not in nodes or j not in nodes]
    if bad_arcs:
        raise ValueError(f"arcs reference unknown nodes: {bad_arcs[:10]}")

    missing_cost = arcs - set(data.cost)
    if missing_cost:
        raise ValueError(f"missing cost for arcs: {sorted(missing_cost)[:10]}")

    missing_supply = nodes - set(data.supply)
    if missing_supply:
        raise ValueError(f"missing supply for nodes: {sorted(missing_supply)}")

    missing_demand = nodes - set(data.demand)
    if missing_demand:
        raise ValueError(f"missing demand for nodes: {sorted(missing_demand)}")


def build_network_model(data: NetworkData) -> pyo.ConcreteModel:
    validate_network_data(data)

    nodes_in = defaultdict(list)
    nodes_out = defaultdict(list)
    for i, j in data.arcs:
        nodes_out[i].append(j)
        nodes_in[j].append(i)

    m = pyo.ConcreteModel(name="sparse_network_flow")

    m.NODES = pyo.Set(initialize=data.nodes, ordered=True)
    m.ARCS = pyo.Set(
        dimen=2,
        within=m.NODES * m.NODES,
        initialize=data.arcs,
        ordered=True,
    )

    m.NODES_IN = pyo.Set(
        m.NODES,
        within=m.NODES,
        initialize=lambda m, n: nodes_in[n],
    )
    m.NODES_OUT = pyo.Set(
        m.NODES,
        within=m.NODES,
        initialize=lambda m, n: nodes_out[n],
    )

    m.cost = pyo.Param(m.ARCS, initialize=data.cost)
    m.supply = pyo.Param(m.NODES, initialize=data.supply)
    m.demand = pyo.Param(m.NODES, initialize=data.demand)

    m.flow = pyo.Var(m.ARCS, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    def balance_rule(m, n):
        return (
            m.supply[n]
            + sum(m.flow[i, n] for i in m.NODES_IN[n])
            - m.demand[n]
            - sum(m.flow[n, j] for j in m.NODES_OUT[n])
            == 0
        )

    m.balance = pyo.Constraint(m.NODES, rule=balance_rule)

    m.obj = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(m.cost[i, j] * m.flow[i, j] for i, j in m.ARCS),
        sense=pyo.minimize,
    )

    return m
```

---

## 5.22 Final checklist

```text id="wl5gum"
[ ] Use import pyomo.environ as pyo.
[ ] Declare structural indexes as Set / RangeSet before dependent components.
[ ] Use RangeSet for simple numeric sequences.
[ ] Use explicit dimen for tuple sets.
[ ] Use within/domain/bounds to enforce membership domains.
[ ] Use validate to fail fast on bad data.
[ ] Use filter only for intentional silent exclusion.
[ ] Use ordered=True or SortedOrder for reproducibility.
[ ] Use virtual set expressions for domains and compact algebra.
[ ] Materialize set expressions only when snapshot semantics are needed.
[ ] Avoid dense Cartesian products for sparse supports.
[ ] Build sparse tuple sets for allowed arcs/assignments.
[ ] Precompute adjacency sets for large sparse networks.
[ ] Avoid repeated full-set membership scans inside constraint rules.
[ ] Avoid Constraint.Skip as the main sparsity mechanism.
[ ] In ConcreteModel, populate derived indexed sets before dependent components.
[ ] In AbstractModel, use BuildAction for post-data derived sets.
[ ] Unit-test cardinality, dimensionality, sparse counts, and adjacency consistency.
```

[1]: https://pyomo.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/pyomo.core.base.set.Set.html "Set — Pyomo 6.10.0 documentation"
[2]: https://pyomo.readthedocs.io/en/6.9.3/explanation/modeling/math_programming/sets.html "Sets — Pyomo 6.9.3 documentation"

# 6) Parameters and data contracts — Pyomo deep dive

Style target: uploaded advanced technical-doc plan. 

Pyomo `Param` = **model data component**: scalar or indexed values required to solve for decision variables. Core options: `default`, `initialize`, `mutable`, `validate`, `within`, and `doc`; `validate` receives the model, proposed value, and indices, and `within` provides a domain set for value validation. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

---

## 6.0 Mental model

```text id="5v2q2r"
Param:
  algebraic data, not a decision variable
  scalar or indexed
  immutable by default
  optionally mutable for repeated solves
  optionally domain-validated with within=
  optionally callback-validated with validate=
  optionally default-filled with default=
  initialized from Python object, rule, AbstractModel data, DataPortal, or .dat
```

Critical distinction:

```text id="zeavzw"
Var  = solver chooses value
Param = user/data pipeline supplies value
```

Pyomo construction rule: a parameter is constructed from initialization data or data loaded from an external source; Pyomo first sets values from the initialization rule, then allows the data dictionary to overwrite those values. Undefined `Param` values may exist structurally, but Pyomo throws an exception if a user attempts to use an uninitialized value. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

---

## 6.1 Declaration taxonomy

### 6.1.1 Scalar immutable parameter

```python id="7v61mg"
import pyomo.environ as pyo

m = pyo.ConcreteModel()
m.alpha = pyo.Param(initialize=3.5)
```

Use:

```python id="dr1wc5"
m.x = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= m.alpha)
```

### 6.1.2 Scalar mutable parameter

```python id="uiycef"
m.rhs = pyo.Param(initialize=10.0, mutable=True)
m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x <= m.rhs)

m.rhs.set_value(12.0)
# or:
m.rhs = 12.0
```

### 6.1.3 Indexed immutable parameter

```python id="3y2ffg"
m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=["A", "B", "C"])
m.cost = pyo.Param(
    m.I,
    initialize={"A": 10.0, "B": 12.5, "C": 7.25},
)
```

### 6.1.4 Indexed mutable parameter

```python id="p1v3tb"
m.demand = pyo.Param(
    m.I,
    initialize={"A": 5.0, "B": 6.0, "C": 3.0},
    mutable=True,
)

m.demand["A"] = 9.0
m.demand["B"].set_value(8.0)
```

### 6.1.5 Multi-index parameter

```python id="taafmq"
m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=["plant1", "plant2"])
m.J = pyo.Set(initialize=["cust1", "cust2", "cust3"])

m.ship_cost = pyo.Param(
    m.I,
    m.J,
    initialize={
        ("plant1", "cust1"): 2.0,
        ("plant1", "cust2"): 3.0,
        ("plant1", "cust3"): 1.5,
        ("plant2", "cust1"): 4.0,
        ("plant2", "cust2"): 2.5,
        ("plant2", "cust3"): 2.0,
    },
)
```

Access:

```python id="3shat7"
m.ship_cost["plant1", "cust2"]
pyo.value(m.ship_cost["plant1", "cust2"])
```

---

## 6.2 Constructor syntax reference

```python id="z251is"
m.p = pyo.Param(
    *index_sets,
    initialize=...,
    default=...,
    mutable=False,
    within=...,
    validate=...,
    doc="...",
)
```

| Argument      | Type                                       | Purpose                                 |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- |
| `*index_sets` | `Set`, `RangeSet`, tuple-domain sets       | scalar if omitted; indexed if supplied  |
| `initialize`  | scalar, dict, function, rule-like callback | explicit initial data                   |
| `default`     | scalar or function                         | value for unspecified indices           |
| `mutable`     | `bool`                                     | allow post-construction value changes   |
| `within`      | Pyomo set/domain                           | value-domain validation                 |
| `validate`    | callback                                   | custom semantic validation              |
| `doc`         | `str`                                      | metadata for `pprint`, docs, inspection |

---

## 6.3 `initialize=` patterns

### 6.3.1 Scalar constant

```python id="yq9ybg"
m.tax_rate = pyo.Param(initialize=0.08)
```

### 6.3.2 Indexed dictionary

```python id="ssk5ow"
m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=["A", "B"])
m.price = pyo.Param(m.I, initialize={"A": 100.0, "B": 120.0})
```

### 6.3.3 Sparse dictionary + default

```python id="88xs19"
m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=[1, 2, 3])
m.J = pyo.Set(initialize=[1, 2, 3])

m.diag = pyo.Param(
    m.I,
    m.J,
    initialize={(1, 1): 9, (2, 2): 16, (3, 3): 25},
    default=0,
)
```

Pyomo’s parameter docs use this exact pattern conceptually: sparse diagonal data through `initialize`, zero elsewhere through `default`. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

### 6.3.4 Rule function, scalar

```python id="0no41t"
def alpha_init(m):
    return 3.14

m.alpha = pyo.Param(initialize=alpha_init)
```

### 6.3.5 Rule function, one-dimensional

```python id="yxzcsa"
def cost_init(m, i):
    return raw_cost[i]

m.cost = pyo.Param(m.I, initialize=cost_init)
```

### 6.3.6 Rule function, multi-dimensional

```python id="vwmrbw"
def ship_cost_init(m, i, j):
    return raw_ship_cost[i, j]

m.ship_cost = pyo.Param(m.I, m.J, initialize=ship_cost_init)
```

Rule signature invariant:

```text id="8cqwej"
Param(m.I, initialize=f)       -> f(model, i)
Param(m.I, m.J, initialize=f)  -> f(model, i, j)
Param(initialize=f)            -> f(model)
```

### 6.3.7 Derived initialization from other components

```python id="38jmmk"
m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=["A", "B", "C"])
m.base = pyo.Param(m.I, initialize={"A": 10, "B": 20, "C": 30})

def derived_init(m, i):
    return 2 * pyo.value(m.base[i])

m.derived = pyo.Param(m.I, initialize=derived_init)
```

Agent rule:

```text id="o1hhgi"
Only derive Params from components already declared/constructed.
For ConcreteModel, declaration order matters immediately.
For AbstractModel, construction order occurs during create_instance in declaration order.
```

---

## 6.4 `default=` semantics

### 6.4.1 Constant default

```python id="644qx8"
m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=["A", "B", "C"])
m.penalty = pyo.Param(m.I, initialize={"A": 10.0}, default=0.0)

pyo.value(m.penalty["A"])  # 10.0
pyo.value(m.penalty["B"])  # 0.0
pyo.value(m.penalty["C"])  # 0.0
```

### 6.4.2 Function default

```python id="93y95h"
def default_cost(m, i):
    return 999.0

m.cost = pyo.Param(m.I, initialize={"A": 10.0}, default=default_cost)
```

The `Param.default()` API documents three default categories: `Param.NoValue` for no default, a numeric constant used for all undefined indices, or a function `f(model, i)` returning the default for an index. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 6.4.3 No default / missing values

```python id="jz5dw5"
m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=["A", "B"])
m.p = pyo.Param(m.I, initialize={"A": 1.0})

# pyo.value(m.p["B"]) -> error: undefined Param value
```

Agent guidance:

```text id="6ynkcc"
Use no default when missing data is an error.
Use default=0 only when zero is mathematically correct.
Use large default penalties only when explicitly modeling fallback arcs/options.
Do not use default as a substitute for data validation.
```

---

## 6.5 `initialize` vs `default`

| Feature                | `initialize=`                 | `default=`                      |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| Purpose                | explicit values               | fallback for unspecified values |
| Stored values          | usually explicit entries      | may not materialize every index |
| Missing-index behavior | missing unless default exists | supplies value when accessed    |
| Sparse matrix use      | diagonal/nonzero entries      | zeros elsewhere                 |
| Data quality           | expected data                 | fallback semantics              |
| Risk                   | incomplete dict errors later  | hides missing data if misused   |

Sparse extraction distinction:

```python id="tkqrp0"
all_values = m.penalty.extract_values()
sparse_values = m.penalty.extract_values_sparse()
```

`extract_values()` returns all index-value pairs defined for a parameter; `extract_values_sparse()` returns index-value pairs with non-default values, useful when repeated `__getitem__` calls are expensive. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

---

## 6.6 `mutable=True`

### 6.6.1 Use cases

```text id="zr1tsk"
parametric studies
sensitivity sweeps
scenario loops
RHS changes
objective-coefficient changes
bound expressions referencing Params
Benders / decomposition master-subproblem iterations
calibration workflows
rolling-horizon updates
```

### 6.6.2 Repeated solve: RHS update

```python id="d04788"
m = pyo.ConcreteModel()
m.x = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
m.rhs = pyo.Param(initialize=10.0, mutable=True)

m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= m.rhs)
m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.x)

opt = pyo.SolverFactory("highs")

for rhs in [5.0, 10.0, 15.0]:
    m.rhs.set_value(rhs)
    results = opt.solve(m)
```

Pyomo’s manipulation guide emphasizes that model manipulation commands must be applied to a concrete model instance and shows repeated-solve scripting patterns. ([Pyomo Documentation][3])

### 6.6.3 Repeated solve: indexed objective coefficients

```python id="9ukrgj"
m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=["A", "B", "C"])
m.c = pyo.Param(m.I, initialize={"A": 1, "B": 2, "C": 3}, mutable=True)
m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=sum(m.c[i] * m.x[i] for i in m.I))

for scenario_c in scenario_coefficients:
    for i, val in scenario_c.items():
        m.c[i] = val
    opt.solve(m)
```

### 6.6.4 Mutable Param expression semantics

Important expression behavior:

```text id="zqdntr"
immutable Param in expression:
  Pyomo may substitute associated numeric value when expression is generated

mutable Param in expression:
  ParamData remains a leaf node in expression tree
  later Param value updates can affect subsequent solves
```

Pyomo expression design docs explicitly state that mutable `Param` objects appear as expression-tree leaves, while immutable parameters are identified during expression generation and replaced with their associated numeric value. ([Pyomo Documentation][4])

### 6.6.5 Critical anti-pattern: `pyo.value()` around mutable Param in expression

Wrong:

```python id="9444vx"
m.rhs = pyo.Param(initialize=10.0, mutable=True)
m.x = pyo.Var()

# BAD: freezes numeric value at construction time
m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= pyo.value(m.rhs))
```

Correct:

```python id="0mloif"
m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= m.rhs)
```

Rationale:

```text id="9vvoec"
pyo.value(m.rhs) converts the current value to a Python numeric.
The expression no longer references the mutable Param.
Future m.rhs updates will not change the constraint expression.
```

---

## 6.7 Mutability decision table

| Scenario                                                    | `mutable=False` | `mutable=True` |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | --------------: | -------------: |
| fixed input data                                            |             yes |    unnecessary |
| symbolic data should be substituted for compact expressions |             yes |             no |
| repeated RHS/objective coefficient updates                  |              no |            yes |
| scenario loop without rebuilding model                      |              no |            yes |
| data should never change after build                        |             yes |             no |
| expression should retain parameter node                     |              no |            yes |
| memory/performance-sensitive huge static data               |     usually yes | only if needed |

Agent rule:

```text id="u7msua"
Default to immutable.
Enable mutable only when later reassignment is required.
Never wrap mutable Params in pyo.value(...) inside algebraic expressions.
```

---

## 6.8 `within=` domain validation

### 6.8.1 Numeric domains

```python id="wbbysn"
m.discount = pyo.Param(within=pyo.UnitInterval, initialize=0.95)
m.capacity = pyo.Param(m.I, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals, initialize=capacity)
m.count = pyo.Param(within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers, initialize=10)
```

### 6.8.2 String/category domains

```python id="axl4g5"
m.MODES = pyo.Set(initialize=["truck", "rail", "ship"])
m.mode = pyo.Param(m.I, within=m.MODES, initialize=item_mode)
```

### 6.8.3 Tuple-domain validation through indexed data

```python id="wfodez"
m.NODES = pyo.Set(initialize=["A", "B", "C"])
m.ARCS = pyo.Set(dimen=2, within=m.NODES * m.NODES, initialize=arcs)

m.cost = pyo.Param(m.ARCS, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals, initialize=cost)
```

Agent guidance:

```text id="rt9l64"
Always set within= for production Params where domain is known.
within=Any is flexible but weak.
Domain validation catches strings, negative values, invalid categories, and bad sentinel values early.
```

---

## 6.9 `validate=` callback

### 6.9.1 Scalar validation

```python id="j2b3ir"
def validate_alpha(m, value):
    return 0 <= value <= 1

m.alpha = pyo.Param(initialize=0.7, validate=validate_alpha)
```

### 6.9.2 Indexed validation

```python id="38dtx9"
def validate_capacity(m, value, i):
    return value >= m.min_capacity[i]

m.capacity = pyo.Param(
    m.I,
    initialize=capacity,
    within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
    validate=validate_capacity,
)
```

### 6.9.3 Multi-index validation

```python id="s37f3z"
def validate_ship_cost(m, value, i, j):
    return value >= 0 and i != j

m.ship_cost = pyo.Param(
    m.I,
    m.J,
    initialize=ship_cost,
    within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
    validate=validate_ship_cost,
)
```

### 6.9.4 Validation design rules

```text id="jh0980"
within=:
  domain/type/range membership

validate=:
  data-dependent semantic rules
  index-dependent rules
  cross-parameter checks
  business rules

pre-Pyomo validation:
  missing keys
  duplicate records
  schema shape
  external-file integrity
```

Pyomo’s parameter docs define `validate` as a callback receiving the model, proposed value, and proposed value indices, returning true when valid; false generates an exception. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

---

## 6.10 Data typing and conversion

### 6.10.1 Numeric conversion before Param construction

```python id="m8mdd3"
raw = {"A": "10.5", "B": "7.25"}

m.cost = pyo.Param(
    m.I,
    initialize={i: float(v) for i, v in raw.items()},
    within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
)
```

### 6.10.2 Category normalization

```python id="njvtye"
m.MODES = pyo.Set(initialize=["truck", "rail", "ship"])

m.mode = pyo.Param(
    m.I,
    initialize={i: raw_mode[i].strip().lower() for i in m.I},
    within=m.MODES,
)
```

### 6.10.3 Boolean-like flags

```python id="0vb7mq"
m.enabled = pyo.Param(
    m.I,
    initialize={i: bool(raw_enabled[i]) for i in m.I},
    within=pyo.Boolean,
)
```

Agent rule:

```text id="5ngdbv"
Normalize external data before Param.
Use within= to enforce final domain.
Do not rely on solver errors to discover malformed data.
```

---

## 6.11 Missing data strategies

### 6.11.1 Fail-fast missing data

```python id="4gpkok"
m.cost = pyo.Param(m.ARCS, initialize=cost, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
```

If `cost` omits a required arc and no default exists, later access to `m.cost[i, j]` fails.

Use when:

```text id="uvnpcf"
every index must be provided
missing data means bad input
```

### 6.11.2 Zero default

```python id="fup75o"
m.fixed_charge = pyo.Param(m.ARCS, initialize=nonzero_charge, default=0.0)
```

Use only when:

```text id="1ivif9"
mathematical default is exactly zero
not provided means zero, not unknown
```

### 6.11.3 Penalty sentinel default

```python id="n7e3pr"
BIG_COST = 1e6

m.cost = pyo.Param(
    m.ARCS,
    initialize=known_cost,
    default=BIG_COST,
    within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
)
```

Use cautiously:

```text id="1svz0k"
valid for soft fallback modeling
dangerous if it hides missing data
must be documented and tested
```

### 6.11.4 Explicit sentinel object outside Pyomo

```python id="ams7qd"
MISSING = object()

def validate_complete(index_set, data, name):
    missing = [i for i in index_set if data.get(i, MISSING) is MISSING]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"{name} missing indices: {missing[:10]}")
```

Agent rule:

```text id="xla96d"
Prefer Python validation for missing required data.
Use Param default only for intentional model semantics.
```

---

## 6.12 AbstractModel data override rules

### 6.12.1 Template initialization

```python id="qvvzkj"
template = pyo.AbstractModel()
template.I = pyo.Set(initialize=["A", "B"])
template.cost = pyo.Param(template.I, initialize={"A": 1.0, "B": 2.0})
```

### 6.12.2 Data overrides during instantiation

```python id="5tp933"
instance = template.create_instance({
    None: {
        "I": {None: ["C", "D"]},
        "cost": {"C": 3.0, "D": 4.0},
    }
})
```

`create_instance(...)` constructs a new concrete instance out-of-place, leaving the original abstract model untouched; external data supplied to `create_instance` overrides data specified in original component declarations and may be supplied through a `dict`, `DataPortal`, or DAT file. ([Pyomo Documentation][5])

Agent rule:

```text id="zc4mud"
For AbstractModel:
  template Param initialize= is fallback/template data
  create_instance data is authoritative
  mutate instance, not template
```

### 6.12.3 Raw dict grammar for Params

```python id="ej286z"
data = {
    None: {
        "I": {None: ["A", "B"]},
        "scalar_param": {None: 10.0},
        "indexed_param": {"A": 1.0, "B": 2.0},
        "matrix_param": {("A", "A"): 1.0, ("A", "B"): 2.0},
    }
}
```

Grammar:

```text id="tk8sm3"
data[namespace][component_name][index] = value

default namespace:
  None

scalar Param:
  "p": {None: value}

1D Param:
  "p": {i: value}

nD Param:
  "p": {(i, j, ...): value}
```

---

## 6.13 DataPortal and Param data

### 6.13.1 Concrete model: explicit use

```python id="vslzb9"
data = pyo.DataPortal()
data.load(filename="cost.tab", param="cost", format="param")

m = pyo.ConcreteModel()
m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=["A", "B"])
m.cost = pyo.Param(m.I, initialize=data["cost"])
```

### 6.13.2 Abstract model: component-aware use

```python id="6kzbwf"
template = pyo.AbstractModel()
template.I = pyo.Set()
template.cost = pyo.Param(template.I)

data = pyo.DataPortal()
data.load(filename="I.tab", set=template.I)
data.load(filename="cost.tab", param=template.cost)

instance = template.create_instance(data)
```

Pyomo’s DataPortal docs distinguish these modes: concrete models load by name and require an explicit format, while abstract models load by component and can often infer format; `load` can be called multiple times for sets/parameters or to override earlier data. ([Pyomo Documentation][6])

### 6.13.3 Structured JSON/YAML pattern

For structured sources, Pyomo’s DataPortal docs describe simple parameters as scalar string/numeric values and indexed parameters as dictionaries mapping indices to numeric values. ([Pyomo Documentation][6])

Example JSON:

```json id="yqfytj"
{
  "I": ["A", "B", "C"],
  "cost": {
    "A": 10.0,
    "B": 12.5,
    "C": 7.25
  },
  "budget": 100.0
}
```

---

## 6.14 Param in algebraic expressions

### 6.14.1 Immutable parameter

```python id="ucy1hk"
m.c = pyo.Param(m.I, initialize=cost)
m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=sum(m.c[i] * m.x[i] for i in m.I))
```

If immutable, Pyomo may inline numeric values in generated expression trees.

### 6.14.2 Mutable parameter

```python id="0o0y55"
m.c = pyo.Param(m.I, initialize=cost, mutable=True)
m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=sum(m.c[i] * m.x[i] for i in m.I))
```

If mutable, the parameter data object remains in the expression tree, allowing later changes.

### 6.14.3 Numeric extraction

```python id="f3q5rw"
float_cost = pyo.value(m.c["A"])
```

Use `pyo.value(...)` for reporting, validation outside algebraic expressions, or control logic after values exist. Do not use it inside expressions when mutability is needed.

---

## 6.15 Param assignment and update syntax

### 6.15.1 Scalar mutable

```python id="5xcynw"
m.p = pyo.Param(initialize=1.0, mutable=True)

m.p = 2.0
# or:
m.p.set_value(2.0)
```

### 6.15.2 Indexed mutable

```python id="46tobg"
m.p = pyo.Param(m.I, initialize=init, mutable=True)

m.p["A"] = 2.0
m.p["A"].set_value(2.0)
```

### 6.15.3 Bulk update

```python id="5opcej"
def update_param(param, values: dict):
    for idx, val in values.items():
        param[idx] = val

update_param(m.demand, {"A": 10.0, "B": 12.0})
```

### 6.15.4 Safe bulk update with index check

```python id="uxdf5k"
def update_indexed_param(param, values: dict, *, strict: bool = True):
    valid = set(param.index_set())

    extra = set(values) - valid
    if strict and extra:
        raise KeyError(f"unknown Param indices: {sorted(extra)[:10]}")

    for idx, val in values.items():
        if idx in valid:
            param[idx] = val
```

---

## 6.16 Persistent solver caveat

```text id="bmp608"
File-based solver:
  updating mutable Param then solve(model) generally rebuilds exported model

Persistent/APPSI solver:
  model-side changes may require interface-specific update/config behavior
  verify solver interface detects or is notified of mutable parameter changes
```

Agent deployment rule:

```text id="qc035m"
For repeated solves:
  small/medium model -> mutable Params + normal solve
  high-frequency large model -> APPSI/persistent solver + tested update path
  structural index changes -> rebuild model or explicitly update persistent solver
```

---

## 6.17 Param data extraction

### 6.17.1 Extract all values

```python id="plorjd"
values = m.cost.extract_values()
```

### 6.17.2 Extract sparse non-default values

```python id="7fohvx"
sparse_values = m.cost.extract_values_sparse()
```

Use cases:

```text id="qc6lvg"
audit loaded data
write manifests
compare scenario data
avoid repeated __getitem__ in large Params
serialize model input snapshot
```

The `Param` API documents both `extract_values()` and `extract_values_sparse()` as utilities for dictionary extraction, especially when key iteration plus repeated `__getitem__` calls are too expensive. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

---

## 6.18 Data contract patterns

### 6.18.1 Required dense vector

```python id="m8fu6f"
def validate_dense_vector(index_set, values, name):
    missing = set(index_set) - set(values)
    extra = set(values) - set(index_set)
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"{name} missing keys: {sorted(missing)[:10]}")
    if extra:
        raise ValueError(f"{name} extra keys: {sorted(extra)[:10]}")
```

Then:

```python id="x3sfmb"
validate_dense_vector(data.items, data.cost, "cost")
m.cost = pyo.Param(m.I, initialize=data.cost, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
```

### 6.18.2 Sparse matrix with zero default

```python id="vkn08o"
m.A = pyo.Set(dimen=2, initialize=nonzero_pairs, within=m.I * m.J)
m.coeff = pyo.Param(m.I, m.J, initialize=nonzero_values, default=0.0)
```

### 6.18.3 Sparse matrix over sparse support only

```python id="cknnnj"
m.A = pyo.Set(dimen=2, initialize=nonzero_pairs, within=m.I * m.J)
m.coeff = pyo.Param(m.A, initialize=nonzero_values)
```

Decision:

| Form                         | Memory / model shape                | Use                                                  |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `Param(m.I, m.J, default=0)` | dense logical domain, sparse values | expression naturally loops dense                     |
| `Param(m.A)` where `A ⊂ I×J` | sparse logical domain               | expression loops sparse support                      |
| Python dict only             | no Pyomo component                  | coefficient used once; no Pyomo introspection needed |

Agent rule:

```text id="6z58ms"
If a coefficient is used only in one expression and never inspected/mutated, Python dict may be sufficient.
If it belongs to the algebraic model contract, use Param.
```

---

## 6.19 Concrete vs Abstract data contracts

### 6.19.1 ConcreteModel contract

```python id="lf30g5"
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ModelData:
    items: tuple[str, ...]
    cost: dict[str, float]
    demand: float

def build_model(data: ModelData) -> pyo.ConcreteModel:
    validate_data(data)
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=data.items)
    m.cost = pyo.Param(m.I, initialize=data.cost, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    m.demand = pyo.Param(initialize=data.demand, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    ...
    return m
```

### 6.19.2 AbstractModel contract

```python id="e86cm0"
template = pyo.AbstractModel()
template.I = pyo.Set()
template.cost = pyo.Param(template.I, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
template.demand = pyo.Param(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

instance = template.create_instance({
    None: {
        "I": {None: ["A", "B"]},
        "cost": {"A": 1.0, "B": 2.0},
        "demand": {None: 10.0},
    }
})
```

### 6.19.3 Recommendation

```text id="cqprbp"
Python-native apps:
  dataclass/Pydantic validation -> ConcreteModel -> Param

AMPL-style/data-file apps:
  AbstractModel -> create_instance(.dat/DataPortal/raw dict) -> instance Params
```

Pyomo’s abstract-data guide lists three data construction routes—standard Python objects, `DataPortal`, and Pyomo data command files—and notes that `DataPortal`/data-command workflows are mainly necessary for abstract models because their data components are initialized after construction. ([Pyomo Documentation][7])

---

## 6.20 Advanced pattern: mutable scenario loop

```python id="826bsa"
import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.opt import SolverStatus, TerminationCondition

def build_model(data):
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=data.items)
    m.cost = pyo.Param(m.I, initialize=data.cost, mutable=True, within=pyo.Reals)
    m.rhs = pyo.Param(initialize=data.rhs, mutable=True, within=pyo.Reals)

    m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=sum(m.cost[i] * m.x[i] for i in m.I))
    m.con = pyo.Constraint(expr=sum(m.x[i] for i in m.I) >= m.rhs)

    return m

def update_scenario(m, scenario):
    for i, c in scenario.cost.items():
        m.cost[i] = c
    m.rhs = scenario.rhs

def solve_scenarios(base_data, scenarios, solver_name="highs"):
    m = build_model(base_data)
    opt = pyo.SolverFactory(solver_name)

    out = {}
    for scenario in scenarios:
        update_scenario(m, scenario)

        results = opt.solve(m, load_solutions=False)
        if (
            results.solver.status == SolverStatus.ok
            and results.solver.termination_condition == TerminationCondition.optimal
        ):
            m.solutions.load_from(results)
            out[scenario.name] = {
                "objective": pyo.value(m.obj),
                "x": {i: pyo.value(m.x[i]) for i in m.I},
            }
        else:
            out[scenario.name] = {
                "status": str(results.solver.status),
                "termination": str(results.solver.termination_condition),
            }

    return out
```

## 6.21 Validation examples

### 6.21.1 Discount factor

```python id="hy58ru"
m.discount = pyo.Param(
    initialize=0.95,
    within=pyo.UnitInterval,
)
```

### 6.21.2 Strictly positive demand

```python id="p83bgr"
def positive_demand(m, val, i):
    return val > 0

m.demand = pyo.Param(
    m.CUSTOMERS,
    initialize=demand,
    within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
    validate=positive_demand,
)
```

### 6.21.3 Capacity must exceed minimum

```python id="7fs68s"
m.min_cap = pyo.Param(m.F, initialize=min_cap, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

def capacity_validate(m, val, f):
    return val >= m.min_cap[f]

m.capacity = pyo.Param(
    m.F,
    initialize=capacity,
    within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
    validate=capacity_validate,
)
```

### 6.21.4 Probability vector

```python id="5qu2ua"
m.SCENARIOS = pyo.Set(initialize=["s1", "s2", "s3"])
m.prob = pyo.Param(
    m.SCENARIOS,
    initialize={"s1": 0.2, "s2": 0.3, "s3": 0.5},
    within=pyo.UnitInterval,
)

if abs(sum(pyo.value(m.prob[s]) for s in m.SCENARIOS) - 1.0) > 1e-9:
    raise ValueError("scenario probabilities must sum to one")
```

Cross-index aggregate constraints are usually cleaner as pre-Pyomo validation or `BuildCheck`, not per-value `validate`.

## 6.22 Unit testing Param contracts

### 6.22.1 Shape

```python id="25zobz"
def test_param_shape(m):
    assert len(m.cost) == len(m.I)
```

### 6.22.2 Values

```python id="tv2o09"
def test_param_values(m):
    assert pyo.value(m.cost["A"]) == 10.0
```

### 6.22.3 Missing data fails

```python id="vxf7hh"
import pytest

def test_missing_cost_fails(data):
    bad = data.replace(cost={})
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        validate_data(bad)
```

### 6.22.4 Domain validation fails

```python id="l57xdk"
import pytest

def test_negative_capacity_rejected():
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=["A"])
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        m.capacity = pyo.Param(
            m.I,
            initialize={"A": -1.0},
            within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
        )
```

### 6.22.5 Mutable update propagates

```python id="xp2qid"
def test_mutable_param_reference_not_frozen():
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    m.x = pyo.Var()
    m.rhs = pyo.Param(initialize=1.0, mutable=True)
    m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= m.rhs)

    m.rhs = 2.0

    # expression still references m.rhs; actual propagation is verified by solve
    assert pyo.value(m.rhs) == 2.0
```

## 6.23 Deployment advisory

### 6.23.1 Production parameter policy

```text id="zib2zo"
[ ] Every production Param has within= unless category-free Any is intentional.
[ ] Required dense Params are validated before model construction.
[ ] default=0 is used only when zero is mathematically valid.
[ ] Mutable Params are limited to values changed across solves.
[ ] Mutable Params are not wrapped in pyo.value() inside constraints/objectives.
[ ] AbstractModel data overrides are tested with create_instance.
[ ] Scenario updates mutate instance Params, not AbstractModel template Params.
[ ] Param extraction is used for manifests and data audits.
```

### 6.23.2 Service/API policy

```text id="a0bozc"
payload -> schema validation -> domain dataclass -> Param construction
never:
  raw API string -> Param without normalization
  missing JSON fields -> default silently
  mutable Param exposed as uncontrolled request-global state
```

### 6.23.3 Batch/scenario policy

```text id="k4rww9"
same structure, changing numbers:
  mutable Params

changing index sets:
  rebuild model or use explicit dynamic component lifecycle

changing constraints:
  ConstraintList / activate/deactivate / rebuild / persistent update path
```

### 6.23.4 Manifest policy

```python id="0po0a3"
def param_manifest(m):
    return {
        "cost": m.cost.extract_values_sparse(),
        "demand": m.demand.extract_values(),
    }
```

---

## 6.24 Anti-pattern table

| Anti-pattern                                             | Failure mode                                     | Replacement                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| No `within=` on numeric production Params                | strings/object values reach solver writer        | `within=pyo.Reals`, `NonNegativeReals`, etc. |
| `default=0` for required data                            | missing data silently hidden                     | pre-validate dense keys                      |
| mutable RHS but expression uses `pyo.value(m.rhs)`       | updates do not propagate                         | use `m.rhs` symbolically                     |
| mutate `AbstractModel` template                          | solved instance unchanged                        | mutate `instance`                            |
| use mutable for all Params                               | larger expression trees / unnecessary complexity | immutable unless update needed               |
| update indexed Param with unknown keys                   | KeyError or silent pipeline bug                  | strict bulk-update function                  |
| use penalty defaults without tests                       | wrong feasible route selected                    | explicit sentinel policy                     |
| use Param for one-off Python constants                   | unnecessary component clutter                    | Python local constant                        |
| use Python dict when data should be introspected/mutated | hidden model contract                            | `Param`                                      |
| rely on solver errors for bad input                      | late obscure failure                             | pre-validation + `within` + `validate`       |

---

## 6.25 Agent-ready production template

```python id="y9xn17"
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

import pyomo.environ as pyo


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DemandData:
    products: tuple[str, ...]
    cost: dict[str, float]
    demand: dict[str, float]
    capacity: float


def validate_demand_data(data: DemandData) -> None:
    products = set(data.products)

    for name, mapping in {
        "cost": data.cost,
        "demand": data.demand,
    }.items():
        missing = products - set(mapping)
        extra = set(mapping) - products
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} missing products: {sorted(missing)}")
        if extra:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} extra products: {sorted(extra)}")

    if any(v < 0 for v in data.cost.values()):
        raise ValueError("cost values must be nonnegative")
    if any(v < 0 for v in data.demand.values()):
        raise ValueError("demand values must be nonnegative")
    if data.capacity < 0:
        raise ValueError("capacity must be nonnegative")


def build_model(data: DemandData) -> pyo.ConcreteModel:
    validate_demand_data(data)

    m = pyo.ConcreteModel(name="param_contract_demo")

    m.P = pyo.Set(initialize=data.products, ordered=True)

    m.cost = pyo.Param(
        m.P,
        initialize=data.cost,
        within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
        doc="Unit production cost.",
    )

    m.demand = pyo.Param(
        m.P,
        initialize=data.demand,
        mutable=True,
        within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
        doc="Scenario-dependent product demand.",
    )

    m.capacity = pyo.Param(
        initialize=data.capacity,
        mutable=True,
        within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
        doc="Scenario-dependent total capacity.",
    )

    m.x = pyo.Var(m.P, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    m.obj = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(m.cost[p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P),
        sense=pyo.minimize,
    )

    def demand_rule(m, p):
        return m.x[p] >= m.demand[p]

    m.meet_demand = pyo.Constraint(m.P, rule=demand_rule)

    m.capacity_con = pyo.Constraint(
        expr=sum(m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= m.capacity
    )

    return m


def update_scenario(m: pyo.ConcreteModel, demand: dict[str, float], capacity: float) -> None:
    products = set(m.P)

    extra = set(demand) - products
    missing = products - set(demand)

    if extra:
        raise KeyError(f"unknown demand products: {sorted(extra)}")
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(f"missing demand products: {sorted(missing)}")
    if capacity < 0:
        raise ValueError("capacity must be nonnegative")

    for p, val in demand.items():
        if val < 0:
            raise ValueError(f"demand[{p}] must be nonnegative")
        m.demand[p] = val

    m.capacity = capacity
```

---

## 6.26 Final checklist

```text id="vkh1kc"
[ ] Use Param for algebraic data that belongs to the model contract.
[ ] Use Python constants/dicts for one-off helper data.
[ ] Use scalar Param when data is global.
[ ] Use indexed Param when data is indexed by Sets.
[ ] Use tuple-indexed Param for sparse or matrix-like data.
[ ] Use initialize= for explicit values.
[ ] Use default= only for mathematically valid fallback values.
[ ] Use within= for all typed production Params.
[ ] Use validate= for index-dependent semantic checks.
[ ] Use mutable=True only for values changed after construction.
[ ] Do not call pyo.value(mutable_param) inside algebraic expressions.
[ ] Use raw dict grammar `{None: {"p": {None: value}}}` for AbstractModel scalar Params.
[ ] Use `{None: {"p": {idx: value}}}` for AbstractModel indexed Params.
[ ] Remember create_instance data overrides template initialization.
[ ] Mutate instantiated models, not AbstractModel templates.
[ ] Use extract_values / extract_values_sparse for Param audits and manifests.
[ ] Unit-test missing data, domain errors, mutable updates, and scenario loops.
```

[1]: https://pyomo.readthedocs.io/en/6.8.0/pyomo_modeling_components/Parameters.html "Parameters — Pyomo 6.8.0 documentation"

[4]: https://pyomo.readthedocs.io/en/6.8.2/explanation/philosophy/expressions/design.html "Design Details — Pyomo 6.8.2 documentation"

# 7) Variables, domains, bounds, and initialization — Pyomo deep dive

Style target: uploaded advanced technical-doc plan. 

Pyomo `Var` = **numeric decision variable component**. A `Var` may be scalar or indexed; key constructor controls include `domain`, `within`, `bounds`, `initialize`, `rule`, `dense`, `units`, `name`, and `doc`. `domain` defines valid values and defaults to `Reals`; `within` is an alias for `domain`; `bounds` is a `(lower, upper)` pair or rule; `initialize` gives an initial value or rule; `rule` aliases `initialize`; and `dense=False` constructs only variable entries returned by initialization/rule rather than all index-set members. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

---

## 7.0 Mental model

```text id="q49nsh"
Var:
  numeric unknown selected by solver
  scalar or indexed
  domain-constrained
  optionally bounded
  optionally initialized / warm-started
  optionally fixed / unfixed
  value loaded after solve
  structural model component, not input data

Param:
  user/data-supplied coefficient/RHS/etc.

Constraint:
  relation involving Vars, Params, Expressions

Objective:
  optimization target involving Vars
```

Core distinction:

```text id="k5hdcu"
Var.value:
  current incumbent / initial guess / loaded solver solution

Var bounds:
  feasible interval exported to solver

Var domain:
  type + implicit domain restrictions, e.g. Reals, Integers, Binary

Var.fixed:
  solver must treat variable as fixed at current/fixed value
```

---

## 7.1 Canonical import

```python id="zqyb6h"
import pyomo.environ as pyo
```

Use:

```python id="cjckep"
m.x = pyo.Var()
m.y = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
m.z = pyo.Var(within=pyo.Binary)
```

Avoid:

```python id="w4catn"
from pyomo.environ import *
```

Reason:

```text id="awmrnv"
clear symbolic namespace
less collision risk
better static-analysis behavior
agent-friendly generated code
```

Pyomo’s manipulation examples use `import pyomo.environ as pyo` and then prefix Pyomo names with `pyo.`. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

---

## 7.2 Declaration taxonomy

### 7.2.1 Scalar continuous variable

```python id="xgjk7e"
m.x = pyo.Var()
```

Equivalent conceptual default:

```python id="bxjda3"
m.x = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.Reals, bounds=(None, None))
```

### 7.2.2 Scalar nonnegative variable

```python id="hgj52a"
m.x = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
```

or:

```python id="7qdyr7"
m.x = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
```

`within` aliases `domain`, so both forms are valid. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

### 7.2.3 Scalar bounded continuous variable

```python id="ltzoh4"
m.x = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.Reals, bounds=(0, 100))
```

### 7.2.4 Scalar integer variable

```python id="goudf2"
m.n = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.Integers, bounds=(0, 10))
```

### 7.2.5 Scalar binary variable

```python id="xr52r5"
m.y = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.Binary)
```

### 7.2.6 Indexed variable

```python id="dayseq"
m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=["A", "B", "C"])
m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
```

Access:

```python id="2jbi0c"
m.x["A"]
m.x["B"].value
pyo.value(m.x["C"])
```

### 7.2.7 Multi-index variable

```python id="fo5xia"
m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=["plant1", "plant2"])
m.J = pyo.Set(initialize=["cust1", "cust2"])

m.ship = pyo.Var(m.I, m.J, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
```

Access:

```python id="szk7pr"
m.ship["plant1", "cust2"]
```

### 7.2.8 Sparse tuple-index variable

```python id="75rkt2"
m.ARCS = pyo.Set(
    dimen=2,
    initialize=[("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("C", "B")],
)

m.flow = pyo.Var(m.ARCS, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
```

Use sparse tuple sets for structural sparsity; do not create `m.NODES * m.NODES` unless every pair is valid.

---

## 7.3 Constructor syntax reference

```python id="d5sr0f"
m.x = pyo.Var(
    *index_sets,
    domain=...,
    within=...,
    bounds=...,
    initialize=...,
    rule=...,
    dense=...,
    units=...,
    doc="...",
)
```

| Keyword       | Meaning                                                           | Agent usage                                       |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `*index_sets` | omitted → scalar; supplied → indexed                              | define model shape                                |
| `domain`      | valid-value set or domain rule                                    | `Reals`, `NonNegativeReals`, `Integers`, `Binary` |
| `within`      | alias for `domain`                                                | use either, prefer `domain` in new code           |
| `bounds`      | `(lb, ub)` tuple or rule                                          | physical/numerical bounds                         |
| `initialize`  | value, dict, or rule                                              | starting point / warm start                       |
| `rule`        | alias for `initialize`                                            | use sparingly; prefer `initialize`                |
| `dense`       | construct all index members vs only initialized/rule-created ones | sparse variable construction                      |
| `units`       | Pyomo units expression                                            | unit consistency workflows                        |
| `doc`         | component documentation                                           | introspection / generated docs                    |

The current stable `Var` API documents `domain`, `within`, `bounds`, `initialize`, `rule`, `dense`, `units`, `name`, and `doc`, including the default domain and default bounds. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

---

## 7.4 Domains

### 7.4.1 Continuous domains

```python id="lruy85"
m.x = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.Reals)
m.x_nonneg = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
m.x_pos = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.PositiveReals)
m.x_nonpos = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonPositiveReals)
m.x_neg = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NegativeReals)
```

### 7.4.2 Integer domains

```python id="gzkq3c"
m.n = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.Integers)
m.n_nonneg = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
m.n_pos = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.PositiveIntegers)
```

### 7.4.3 Binary domain

```python id="3ek79x"
m.y = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.Binary)
```

Use for MILP binary decisions.

### 7.4.4 Boolean domain vs `BooleanVar`

```python id="z1i3oj"
m.y_numeric = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.Boolean)
```

Use `Var(domain=pyo.Binary)` for numeric MIP 0/1 decisions. Use `BooleanVar` for logical propositions in GDP/logical models:

```python id="07knoi"
from pyomo.gdp import BooleanVar
from pyomo.core import LogicalConstraint

m.Y = BooleanVar(m.I)
```

Pyomo.GDP documents `BooleanVar` as analogous to `Var` for logical variables and usable in `LogicalConstraint` expressions. ([Pyomo Documentation][3])

### 7.4.5 Domain effects

```text id="yza78m"
domain=pyo.Reals:
  continuous unbounded unless bounds add limits

domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals:
  continuous lb >= 0

domain=pyo.Integers:
  integer unbounded unless bounds add limits

domain=pyo.Binary:
  integer 0/1, solver treats as binary

domain=pyo.Boolean:
  numeric Boolean domain in Var context; prefer Binary for algebraic MILP
```

Pyomo’s variable docs note that many predefined virtual sets used as domains imply bounds; `Boolean` is explicitly given as an example implying zero/one bounds. ([Pyomo Documentation][4])

---

## 7.5 Bounds

### 7.5.1 Static bounds tuple

```python id="n7u0ai"
m.x = pyo.Var(bounds=(0, 10))
m.y = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.Reals, bounds=(-5, 5))
m.z = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.Integers, bounds=(0, None))
```

`None` means no finite bound:

```text id="r4mmqt"
bounds=(None, None)  -> free variable
bounds=(0, None)     -> lower bounded
bounds=(None, 100)   -> upper bounded
bounds=(0, 100)      -> two-sided bounded
```

### 7.5.2 Rule-based bounds

```python id="624qdg"
m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=["Scones", "Tea"])

lb = {"Scones": 2, "Tea": 4}
ub = {"Scones": 5, "Tea": 7}

def price_bounds(m, i):
    return (lb[i], ub[i])

m.price = pyo.Var(m.I, domain=pyo.PositiveIntegers, bounds=price_bounds)
```

Pyomo’s variable docs show indexed bounds supplied by a rule whose signature begins with the model and then index arguments. ([Pyomo Documentation][4])

### 7.5.3 Bounds from Params

```python id="38a50g"
m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=["A", "B"])
m.lb = pyo.Param(m.I, initialize={"A": 0, "B": 5})
m.ub = pyo.Param(m.I, initialize={"A": 10, "B": 20})

def x_bounds(m, i):
    return (m.lb[i], m.ub[i])

m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, bounds=x_bounds)
```

### 7.5.4 Bounds from data object

```python id="u4sqtu"
def build_model(data):
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=data.items)

    def bounds_rule(m, i):
        return data.lower[i], data.upper[i]

    m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, domain=pyo.Reals, bounds=bounds_rule)
    return m
```

### 7.5.5 Bound update after construction

```python id="ksd1ur"
m.x.setlb(0.0)
m.x.setub(100.0)

m.x[i].setlb(0.0)
m.x[i].setub(100.0)
```

Pyomo’s model-manipulation guide shows changing variable bounds with `setlb(...)` and `setub(...)` and warns that fixing a variable and setting bounds are semantically different. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

---

## 7.6 `domain` vs `bounds`

| Requirement                          |           Use domain |                        Use bounds |
| ------------------------------------ | -------------------: | --------------------------------: |
| continuous vs integer vs binary type |                  yes |                                no |
| finite lower/upper limits            | sometimes via domain |                               yes |
| nonnegative continuous               |   `NonNegativeReals` |     `bounds=(0, None)` also works |
| integer 0..10                        |           `Integers` |                  `bounds=(0, 10)` |
| binary 0/1                           |             `Binary` | do not use only bounds for binary |
| physical limits                      |                maybe |                               yes |
| numerical scaling/solver aid         |                   no |                               yes |

Good:

```python id="gcs0by"
m.build = pyo.Var(m.F, domain=pyo.Binary)
m.production = pyo.Var(m.P, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=production_bounds)
m.units = pyo.Var(m.K, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers, bounds=(0, 10))
```

Bad:

```python id="99ds1d"
# This is a continuous variable between 0 and 1, not binary.
m.y = pyo.Var(bounds=(0, 1))
```

Correct:

```python id="r2ztzx"
m.y = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.Binary)
```

---

## 7.7 Initialization

### 7.7.1 Scalar initialization

```python id="j3ep1q"
m.x = pyo.Var(initialize=1.5)
```

Pyomo’s variable docs describe `initialize` as a function or Python object that supplies a starting value and note that initialization is particularly important for nonlinear models. ([Pyomo Documentation][4])

### 7.7.2 Indexed initialization with constant

```python id="krloky"
m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, initialize=0.0)
```

### 7.7.3 Indexed initialization with dictionary

```python id="d0ks88"
m.x = pyo.Var(
    m.I,
    initialize={"A": 1.0, "B": 2.0, "C": 0.5},
)
```

### 7.7.4 Indexed initialization with rule

```python id="0n0kbi"
def x_init(m, i):
    return initial_x[i]

m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, initialize=x_init)
```

### 7.7.5 Multi-index initialization with rule

```python id="tqc3u4"
def flow_init(m, i, j):
    return initial_flow.get((i, j), 0.0)

m.flow = pyo.Var(m.ARCS, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, initialize=flow_init)
```

### 7.7.6 Assignment after construction

```python id="8yphhu"
m.x = pyo.Var()
m.x.value = 1.5
# or:
m.x.set_value(1.5)
```

For indexed variables:

```python id="90w9p7"
m.x[i].value = 2.0
m.x[i].set_value(2.0)
```

The `Var` API documents scalar `set_value(...)`, `set_values(...)` for dictionaries, `extract_values(...)`, and `get_values(...)` utilities. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

### 7.7.7 Bulk set values

```python id="fnfqhg"
m.x.set_values({"A": 1.0, "B": 2.0, "C": 3.0})
```

---

## 7.8 Initial values vs fixed values vs solutions

```text id="vta8m2"
initialize / .value before solve:
  starting point / warm-start candidate / incumbent guess

solver-loaded .value after solve:
  solution value, if result was loaded

fix(value):
  removes variable freedom by fixing at value

bounds=(lb, ub):
  restricts but does not fix unless lb == ub and variable not separately fixed
```

Critical examples:

```python id="q3h373"
m.x = pyo.Var(initialize=5.0)  # solver may move x
m.x.fix(5.0)                  # solver must keep x at 5
m.x.setlb(5.0); m.x.setub(5.0) # bound-fixed but fixed flag is False
```

---

## 7.9 Dense vs sparse variable construction

### 7.9.1 Dense default

```python id="i81pxt"
m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=range(1_000_000))
m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, dense=True)
```

Default:

```text id="cw1gz1"
dense=True
construct all entries in index_set()
```

The stable `Var` API states that `dense=True` instantiates all elements from `index_set()` during construction, while `dense=False` constructs only variables returned by `initialize`/`rule`; default is `True`. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

### 7.9.2 Sparse construction with `dense=False`

```python id="6bp0e6"
m.I = pyo.RangeSet(1, 1_000_000)

def init_sparse(m, i):
    if i in active_indices:
        return 0.0
    return None

m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, initialize=init_sparse, dense=False)
```

### 7.9.3 Explicit sparse tuple set usually better

```python id="yqae26"
m.ACTIVE = pyo.Set(initialize=active_indices)
m.x = pyo.Var(m.ACTIVE, initialize=0.0)
```

Agent rule:

```text id="ep1zok"
Prefer sparse index sets over dense=False unless you need dynamic add(index) behavior.
Structural sparsity belongs in Sets.
```

### 7.9.4 Add variable to sparse indexed Var

```python id="pp8tw7"
m.x.add(new_index)
m.x[new_index].set_value(0.0)
```

`Var.add(index)` adds a variable at a particular index. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

---

## 7.10 Rule signatures

### 7.10.1 Bounds rule signatures

```python id="dws6me"
def scalar_bounds(m):
    return (0, 10)

def one_dim_bounds(m, i):
    return (lb[i], ub[i])

def two_dim_bounds(m, i, j):
    return (lb[i, j], ub[i, j])
```

Use:

```python id="wp0dbx"
m.x = pyo.Var(bounds=scalar_bounds)
m.y = pyo.Var(m.I, bounds=one_dim_bounds)
m.z = pyo.Var(m.I, m.J, bounds=two_dim_bounds)
```

### 7.10.2 Initialization rule signatures

```python id="d6iosh"
def scalar_init(m):
    return 0.0

def one_dim_init(m, i):
    return init[i]

def two_dim_init(m, i, j):
    return init[i, j]
```

Use:

```python id="q7ef87"
m.x = pyo.Var(initialize=scalar_init)
m.y = pyo.Var(m.I, initialize=one_dim_init)
m.z = pyo.Var(m.I, m.J, initialize=two_dim_init)
```

Agent rule:

```text id="8cxe3u"
Rule signature = (model, *index_tuple)
Returning wrong shape for bounds or invalid numeric value produces construction-time or solve-time failures.
```

---

## 7.11 Fixing and unfixing

### 7.11.1 Fix scalar variable

```python id="0g8f74"
m.x.fix(3.0)
```

Equivalent semantics documented by Pyomo:

```python id="2o9gnd"
m.x.value = 3.0
m.x.fixed = True
```

Pyomo’s manipulation guide states that `x.fix(1)` is equivalent to assigning value 1 and setting `fixed=True`, while `x.fix()` sets `fixed=True` using the current value. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 7.11.2 Fix at current value

```python id="eeqfkl"
m.x.value = 3.0
m.x.fix()
```

### 7.11.3 Unfix

```python id="epd9nf"
m.x.unfix()
```

### 7.11.4 Fix indexed variable entries

```python id="yoksp1"
m.x["A"].fix(1.0)
m.x["B"].fix(0.0)
```

### 7.11.5 Fix entire indexed component

```python id="e8x0mg"
m.x.fix(0.0)
```

### 7.11.6 Unfix entire indexed component

```python id="4bh856"
m.x.unfix()
```

### 7.11.7 Flip binary and re-solve

```python id="jr1848"
if pyo.value(m.y[i]) < 0.5:
    m.y[i].fix(1)
else:
    m.y[i].fix(0)

results = opt.solve(m)
```

Pyomo’s manipulation guide shows fixing a binary variable to the opposite value after solving, then re-solving the instance. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

---

## 7.12 Fixing vs bound-tightening

### 7.12.1 Fixing

```python id="fv4shu"
m.x.fix(5)
```

Effects:

```text id="4z86wl"
fixed flag = True
solver treats x as fixed at its value
bounds may be ignored by solver for fixed variable handling
```

### 7.12.2 Bound-tightening to a point

```python id="czf6pr"
m.x.setlb(5)
m.x.setub(5)
```

Effects:

```text id="x43h8b"
fixed flag = False
lb = ub = 5
solver sees variable with equal bounds
```

Pyomo’s guide warns that fixing and setting equal lower/upper bounds are not identical: if `fixed=True`, the solver ignores bounds and fixes the variable at its current value. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 7.12.3 Decision table

| Goal                                             | Use                               |
| ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------- |
| remove variable from degrees of freedom at value | `fix(value)`                      |
| preserve variable object but restrict interval   | `setlb`, `setub`                  |
| enforce exact value through solver bounds        | `setlb(v); setub(v)`              |
| temporarily force incumbent binary choice        | `fix(0/1)`                        |
| warm-start without restricting                   | `.value = ...` / `set_value(...)` |

---

## 7.13 Bounds update patterns

### 7.13.1 Scalar update

```python id="83rb4f"
m.x.setlb(0.0)
m.x.setub(10.0)
```

### 7.13.2 Indexed update

```python id="1px3fm"
for i in m.I:
    m.x[i].setlb(lb[i])
    m.x[i].setub(ub[i])
```

### 7.13.3 Reset to unbounded side

```python id="7dq69u"
m.x.setlb(None)
m.x.setub(None)
```

### 7.13.4 Bound tightening from solution

```python id="rsvrri"
for i in m.I:
    val = pyo.value(m.x[i])
    m.x[i].setlb(max(m.x[i].lb or -float("inf"), val - tolerance))
    m.x[i].setub(min(m.x[i].ub or float("inf"), val + tolerance))
```

### 7.13.5 Bound audit

```python id="5ttq5o"
def unbounded_continuous_vars(m):
    out = []
    for v in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True):
        if v.is_continuous() and not v.fixed and v.lb is None and v.ub is None:
            out.append(v.name)
    return out
```

## 7.14 Warm starts / initial values

### 7.14.1 Simple warm-start assignment

```python id="0d3gpd"
for i, val in incumbent_x.items():
    m.x[i].value = val

results = opt.solve(m, warmstart=True)
```

`warmstart=True` is solver-interface dependent; Pyomo’s solver recipes include a section on warm starts, and solver option support differs across solver interfaces. ([Pyomo Documentation][5])

### 7.14.2 MIP incumbent warm start

```python id="vv4qhp"
for i in m.I:
    m.y[i].value = int(round(incumbent_y[i]))

results = opt.solve(m, warmstart=True)
```

### 7.14.3 NLP starting point

```python id="s9ye7a"
m.x = pyo.Var(initialize=1.0)
m.y = pyo.Var(initialize=1.0)

# or later
m.x.set_value(2.0)
m.y.set_value(-1.0)

results = pyo.SolverFactory("ipopt").solve(m)
```

### 7.14.4 Warm-start vs fix

```text id="5jjie2"
.value / initialize:
  suggest starting value
  solver may move variable

fix(value):
  force variable value
  solver cannot move variable

warmstart=True:
  ask solver interface to communicate incumbent/start data
  availability and semantics are solver-dependent
```

---

## 7.15 Nonlinear model initialization

### 7.15.1 Why it matters

```text id="6utayc"
NLP/MINLP solvers often use local iterative algorithms.
Initial values affect convergence, feasibility restoration, local optimum, and numerical stability.
Uninitialized variables may default poorly or fail in nonlinear expression evaluation.
```

Pyomo’s variable docs explicitly state that `initialize` is particularly important for nonlinear models. ([Pyomo Documentation][4])

### 7.15.2 Positive-domain nonlinear variables

Bad:

```python id="0idx2r"
m.x = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=pyo.log(m.x) >= 0)
```

Better:

```python id="wnkpcp"
m.x = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.PositiveReals, bounds=(1e-6, None), initialize=1.0)
m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=pyo.log(m.x) >= 0)
```

### 7.15.3 Division denominators

Bad:

```python id="oromya"
m.y = pyo.Var()
m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x / m.y <= 10)
```

Better:

```python id="ul6yvq"
m.y = pyo.Var(bounds=(1e-4, None), initialize=1.0)
m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x / m.y <= 10)
```

### 7.15.4 Square-root domain

```python id="09qw7o"
m.x = pyo.Var(bounds=(0, None), initialize=1.0)
m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=pyo.sqrt(m.x) <= 5)
```

### 7.15.5 Local multi-start loop

```python id="jidml6"
def solve_from_start(m, opt, start):
    for name, value in start.items():
        var = m.find_component(name)
        if var is None:
            raise KeyError(name)
        var.set_value(value)
    return opt.solve(m, load_solutions=False)

starts = [
    {"x": -2.0, "y": 2.0},
    {"x": 0.0, "y": 0.0},
    {"x": 2.0, "y": -2.0},
]
```

Agent rule:

```text id="h6dwgx"
For nonlinear expressions:
  initialize every variable in nonlinear terms
  bound domains away from singularities
  scale variable magnitudes
  test multiple initial points for nonconvex models
```

---

## 7.16 Variable values after solve

### 7.16.1 Safe extraction

```python id="jw0l4a"
x_val = pyo.value(m.x)
x_i_val = pyo.value(m.x[i])
```

### 7.16.2 Exception-safe extraction

```python id="2w3kyn"
x_val = pyo.value(m.x, exception=False)
```

### 7.16.3 Extract indexed values

```python id="xb4728"
values = m.x.extract_values()
# or:
values = m.x.get_values()
```

The `Var` API documents `extract_values(...)` and `get_values(...)` returning dictionaries of index-value pairs. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

### 7.16.4 Include/exclude fixed values

```python id="4h6zkp"
all_values = m.x.get_values(include_fixed_values=True)
free_values = m.x.get_values(include_fixed_values=False)
```

---

## 7.17 Stale values

```text id="vbt0u8"
stale:
  Pyomo marker indicating variable value may not reflect current solved state
  useful after model modifications / pre-solve states
```

API:

```python id="uc88w2"
m.x.flag_as_stale()
```

The `Var` API documents `flag_as_stale()` as setting the stale attribute on every variable data object. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

Deployment rule:

```text id="6eyibu"
Do not trust Var.value unless:
  solve completed acceptably
  solutions were loaded
  model has not since been materially changed without re-solve
```

---

## 7.18 Variable units

```python id="kd5icp"
from pyomo.environ import units as u

m.distance = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, units=u.m)
m.time = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.PositiveReals, units=u.s)
m.speed = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, units=u.m / u.s)
```

The stable `Var` API includes a `units` keyword and a `get_units()` method. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

Agent rule:

```text id="rg77cy"
Use units for physics/engineering models where dimensional errors are common.
Avoid units in very large models unless unit checking is part of the project’s QA workflow.
```

---

## 7.19 Domain-rule pattern

The `domain` keyword may be a Set or function returning Sets. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

Example:

```python id="yd9bbi"
def domain_rule(m, i):
    if i in integer_items:
        return pyo.NonNegativeIntegers
    return pyo.NonNegativeReals

m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, domain=domain_rule)
```

Caution:

```text id="5j5sig"
Mixed per-index domains can reduce clarity.
For large production models, prefer separate variables:
  m.x_cont = Var(CONTINUOUS_ITEMS)
  m.x_int  = Var(INTEGER_ITEMS, domain=NonNegativeIntegers)
```

---

## 7.20 Separate variables vs mixed domains

### 7.20.1 Mixed-domain variable

```python id="p7wzpj"
def domain_rule(m, i):
    return pyo.Binary if i in m.BINARY_ITEMS else pyo.NonNegativeReals

m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, domain=domain_rule)
```

### 7.20.2 Separate variable components

```python id="032g9f"
m.B = pyo.Set(initialize=binary_items)
m.C = pyo.Set(initialize=continuous_items)

m.y = pyo.Var(m.B, domain=pyo.Binary)
m.x = pyo.Var(m.C, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
```

Recommendation:

```text id="i283qp"
Separate variable components:
  clearer solver statistics
  clearer reporting
  less surprising domain behavior
  easier warm starts and bound audits
```

---

## 7.21 Sparse variables and structural sparsity

### 7.21.1 Bad dense construction

```python id="p9jm11"
m.flow = pyo.Var(m.NODES, m.NODES, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
```

### 7.21.2 Good sparse construction

```python id="uz5arl"
m.ARCS = pyo.Set(dimen=2, initialize=arcs, within=m.NODES * m.NODES)
m.flow = pyo.Var(m.ARCS, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
```

### 7.21.3 Sparse by time and arc

```python id="0g1bky"
m.TIME_ARCS = pyo.Set(dimen=3, initialize=time_arcs)
m.flow = pyo.Var(m.TIME_ARCS, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
```

Agent rule:

```text id="agk53w"
Structural sparsity belongs in the index set.
Do not create dense variable arrays and compensate with zero bounds unless there is a strong reason.
```

---

## 7.22 Variable initialization from heuristic

```python id="60cc37"
def initialize_from_heuristic(m, i):
    return min(pyo.value(m.demand[i]), pyo.value(m.capacity[i]))

m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, initialize=initialize_from_heuristic)
```

For mutable post-build starts:

```python id="0pdqie"
def apply_start(m, start: dict):
    for i, val in start.items():
        if i in m.x:
            m.x[i].set_value(val)
```

Validation:

```python id="kqxhod"
def apply_start_checked(var, values):
    valid = set(var.keys())
    extra = set(values) - valid
    if extra:
        raise KeyError(f"unknown variable start indices: {sorted(extra)[:10]}")

    for idx, val in values.items():
        var[idx].set_value(val)
```

---

## 7.23 Bounds from variable-dependent expressions: avoid

Bad:

```python id="6ccaa5"
def bounds_rule(m, i):
    return (0, m.y[i])  # y is a Var
```

Reason:

```text id="somwe7"
Variable bounds must be numeric / data-dependent at construction/export time.
Use constraints for variable-dependent limits.
```

Correct:

```python id="5ymmu5"
m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

def linking_rule(m, i):
    return m.x[i] <= m.y[i]

m.link = pyo.Constraint(m.I, rule=linking_rule)
```

---

## 7.24 Bounds and Big-M formulations

Good:

```python id="r3x03c"
m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=x_bounds)
m.y = pyo.Var(m.I, domain=pyo.Binary)

def on_off_rule(m, i):
    return m.x[i] <= m.x[i].ub * m.y[i]

m.on_off = pyo.Constraint(m.I, rule=on_off_rule)
```

Better if upper bounds are data:

```python id="gauxar"
m.ub_x = pyo.Param(m.I, initialize=ub_x, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=lambda m, i: (0, m.ub_x[i]))

def on_off_rule(m, i):
    return m.x[i] <= m.ub_x[i] * m.y[i]
```

Agent rule:

```text id="nbrz80"
Bound variables tightly before GDP/MIP transformations.
Use physical/data-derived upper bounds, not arbitrary huge M.
Variable bounds improve relaxations, presolve, scaling, and nonlinear convergence.
```

---

## 7.25 Fix/unfix workflows

### 7.25.1 Freeze incumbent solution

```python id="1z04vc"
def fix_solution(var):
    for idx in var:
        var[idx].fix(pyo.value(var[idx]))
```

### 7.25.2 Relax fixed variables

```python id="jbnnkm"
def unfix_all(var):
    for idx in var:
        var[idx].unfix()
```

### 7.25.3 Fix a subset

```python id="qa46ey"
for i in fixed_items:
    m.x[i].fix(fixed_value[i])
```

### 7.25.4 Rolling horizon

```python id="5e2ewg"
for t in m.T:
    if t <= frozen_period:
        m.dispatch[t].fix(previous_solution[t])
    else:
        m.dispatch[t].unfix()
```

---

## 7.26 Updating bounds in repeated solves

```python id="83xf35"
def update_capacity_bounds(m, capacity):
    for i, cap in capacity.items():
        m.production[i].setlb(0)
        m.production[i].setub(cap)
```

Solve loop:

```python id="gp0znu"
for scenario in scenarios:
    update_capacity_bounds(m, scenario.capacity)
    apply_start_checked(m.production, scenario.initial_production)
    results = opt.solve(m, load_solutions=False)
```

Persistent solver caveat:

```text id="uqekiy"
File-based solves:
  model is re-exported, changed bounds/values are seen on next solve

Persistent solver:
  update_var(...) or APPSI update behavior may be required
```

Pyomo’s persistent-solver docs state that persistent solvers maintain a live solver-side model and users are responsible for notifying the persistent solver interface when the Pyomo model changes. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

---

## 7.27 Auditing variable domains and bounds

### 7.27.1 Domain/type counts

```python id="b2uc04"
def variable_type_counts(m):
    vars_ = list(m.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True))
    return {
        "total": len(vars_),
        "binary": sum(v.is_binary() for v in vars_),
        "integer": sum(v.is_integer() for v in vars_),
        "continuous": sum(v.is_continuous() for v in vars_),
        "fixed": sum(v.fixed for v in vars_),
    }
```

### 7.27.2 Missing bounds audit

```python id="oyprqt"
def missing_bound_audit(m):
    out = []
    for v in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True):
        if v.fixed:
            continue
        if v.lb is None or v.ub is None:
            out.append({
                "name": v.name,
                "lb": v.lb,
                "ub": v.ub,
                "binary": v.is_binary(),
                "integer": v.is_integer(),
                "continuous": v.is_continuous(),
            })
    return out
```

### 7.27.3 Initialization audit

```python id="5rwh7a"
def uninitialized_vars(m):
    return [
        v.name
        for v in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True)
        if v.value is None and not v.fixed
    ]
```

### 7.27.4 NLP start audit

```python id="qxlzok"
def require_nlp_initialization(m):
    missing = uninitialized_vars(m)
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"uninitialized variables: {missing[:20]}")
```

## 7.28 Solver-class implications

| Model class                  | Variable domains                    | Initialization importance | Bounds importance |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------: | ----------------: |
| LP                           | continuous                          |                       low |       medium/high |
| MILP                         | continuous + integer/binary         | low/medium for MIP starts |              high |
| QP                           | continuous/integer depending solver |                    medium |              high |
| NLP                          | continuous                          |                 very high |         very high |
| MINLP                        | continuous + integer/binary         |                 very high |         very high |
| GDP transformed to MIP/MINLP | binary indicators + continuous      |               medium/high |         very high |
| DAE after discretization     | continuous                          |                 very high |         very high |

Agent deployment rule:

```text id="r9u947"
LP/MILP:
  prioritize valid domains, tight bounds, sparse variables.

NLP/MINLP:
  additionally provide high-quality initial values and avoid singular domains.

GDP/Big-M:
  bounds are formulation-critical, not optional.
```

---

## 7.29 Common variable-domain modeling patterns

### 7.29.1 Facility open/closed

```python id="scl029"
m.open = pyo.Var(m.FACILITIES, domain=pyo.Binary)
```

### 7.29.2 Production quantity

```python id="arx4vy"
m.prod = pyo.Var(m.PRODUCTS, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
```

### 7.29.3 Integer batch count

```python id="81z64d"
m.batches = pyo.Var(m.PRODUCTS, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers, bounds=(0, 100))
```

### 7.29.4 Signed deviation

```python id="ri90vv"
m.dev = pyo.Var(m.I, domain=pyo.Reals)
```

Alternative split:

```python id="8jd48f"
m.dev_pos = pyo.Var(m.I, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
m.dev_neg = pyo.Var(m.I, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
```

### 7.29.5 Semi-continuous variable via binary

```python id="ryzv9i"
m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, None))
m.y = pyo.Var(m.I, domain=pyo.Binary)

def semi_lb_rule(m, i):
    return m.x[i] >= min_level[i] * m.y[i]

def semi_ub_rule(m, i):
    return m.x[i] <= max_level[i] * m.y[i]

m.semi_lb = pyo.Constraint(m.I, rule=semi_lb_rule)
m.semi_ub = pyo.Constraint(m.I, rule=semi_ub_rule)
```
