## 7.30 Unit-test patterns

### 7.30.1 Variable count

```python id="6pgbvh"
def test_variable_count(model):
    assert len(model.x) == len(model.I)
```

### 7.30.2 Domain checks

```python id="qjo90c"
def test_binary_domain(model):
    assert all(model.y[i].is_binary() for i in model.I)
```

### 7.30.3 Bound checks

```python id="qkngie"
def test_bounds(model):
    for i in model.I:
        assert model.x[i].lb == 0
        assert model.x[i].ub == model.capacity[i]
```

### 7.30.4 Initialization checks

```python id="wy3sji"
def test_initialization(model):
    for i in model.I:
        assert model.x[i].value is not None
```

### 7.30.5 Fixing semantics

```python id="motlq5"
def test_fix_unfix(model):
    model.x["A"].fix(1.0)
    assert model.x["A"].fixed
    assert model.x["A"].value == 1.0

    model.x["A"].unfix()
    assert not model.x["A"].fixed
```

---

## 7.31 Production deployment advisory

### 7.31.1 Minimum variable policy

```text id="xhrsvu"
[ ] Every Var has an intentional domain.
[ ] Every continuous physical Var has finite bounds where possible.
[ ] Every integer Var has finite bounds where practical.
[ ] Every binary decision uses domain=Binary, not bounds=(0,1).
[ ] Every NLP variable has an initial value.
[ ] Variables inside log/sqrt/division/power expressions are bounded away from invalid regions.
[ ] Sparse decisions are indexed over sparse Sets.
[ ] Warm-start data is validated against variable index sets.
[ ] Fixing is never confused with initialization.
[ ] Bound updates are applied to instantiated ConcreteModel / AbstractModel instance.
```

### 7.31.2 Model manifest

```python id="1us7uh"
def variable_manifest(m):
    vars_ = list(m.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True))
    return {
        "n_vars": len(vars_),
        "n_binary": sum(v.is_binary() for v in vars_),
        "n_integer": sum(v.is_integer() for v in vars_),
        "n_continuous": sum(v.is_continuous() for v in vars_),
        "n_fixed": sum(v.fixed for v in vars_),
        "n_uninitialized": sum(v.value is None for v in vars_),
        "n_missing_lb": sum(v.lb is None and not v.fixed for v in vars_),
        "n_missing_ub": sum(v.ub is None and not v.fixed for v in vars_),
    }
```

### 7.31.3 Service policy

```text id="wm3tjm"
Request payload:
  may set bounds/starts only through validated schema
  cannot arbitrarily fix variables unless authorized
  cannot create structural variable explosion
  must respect model-size limits
```

### 7.31.4 Batch/scenario policy

```text id="333oh8"
Changing numeric limits:
  update bounds / mutable Params

Changing starts:
  set Var.value

Changing fixed decisions:
  fix/unfix

Changing index structure:
  rebuild model or use controlled add(index) lifecycle
```

---

## 7.32 Anti-pattern table

| Anti-pattern                                   | Failure mode                             | Replacement                               |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `Var(bounds=(0, 1))` for binary decision       | continuous relaxation, wrong MILP        | `Var(domain=Binary)`                      |
| Unbounded physical continuous variables        | weak relaxation / nonlinear instability  | data-derived finite bounds                |
| No NLP initial values                          | convergence failure / bad local solution | `initialize=` for all nonlinear variables |
| `log(x)` with `x` initialized at 0             | invalid evaluation                       | `bounds=(eps, None), initialize=1`        |
| Fixing when intending warm start               | variable cannot move                     | set `.value` only                         |
| Setting equal bounds when intending fixed flag | `fixed` remains false                    | use `fix(value)`                          |
| Using variable-dependent bounds                | invalid bound semantics                  | use `Constraint`                          |
| Dense variable over huge Cartesian product     | memory explosion                         | sparse tuple set                          |
| Mixed domains in one Var without documentation | audit/report confusion                   | separate Var components                   |
| Trusting `.value` after failed solve           | stale/unloaded result                    | gate solve status and load                |
| Mutating AbstractModel template variable       | instance unchanged                       | mutate instance                           |
| Persistent solver bound updates without sync   | solver-side stale model                  | update persistent/APPSI interface         |

---

## 7.33 Agent-ready production template

```python id="rx4t9f"
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

import pyomo.environ as pyo


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class UnitCommitmentData:
    units: tuple[str, ...]
    periods: tuple[int, ...]
    p_min: dict[str, float]
    p_max: dict[str, float]
    variable_cost: dict[str, float]
    demand: dict[int, float]
    initial_dispatch: dict[tuple[str, int], float]


def validate_data(data: UnitCommitmentData) -> None:
    units = set(data.units)
    periods = set(data.periods)

    for name, mapping in {
        "p_min": data.p_min,
        "p_max": data.p_max,
        "variable_cost": data.variable_cost,
    }.items():
        missing = units - set(mapping)
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} missing units: {sorted(missing)}")

    missing_demand = periods - set(data.demand)
    if missing_demand:
        raise ValueError(f"demand missing periods: {sorted(missing_demand)}")

    for u in data.units:
        if data.p_min[u] < 0:
            raise ValueError(f"p_min[{u}] must be nonnegative")
        if data.p_max[u] < data.p_min[u]:
            raise ValueError(f"p_max[{u}] must be >= p_min[{u}]")


def build_model(data: UnitCommitmentData) -> pyo.ConcreteModel:
    validate_data(data)

    m = pyo.ConcreteModel(name="variable_contract_demo")

    m.U = pyo.Set(initialize=data.units, ordered=True)
    m.T = pyo.Set(initialize=data.periods, ordered=True)

    m.p_min = pyo.Param(m.U, initialize=data.p_min, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    m.p_max = pyo.Param(m.U, initialize=data.p_max, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    m.variable_cost = pyo.Param(m.U, initialize=data.variable_cost)
    m.demand = pyo.Param(m.T, initialize=data.demand, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    def dispatch_bounds(m, u, t):
        return (0, m.p_max[u])

    def dispatch_init(m, u, t):
        return data.initial_dispatch.get((u, t), 0.0)

    m.dispatch = pyo.Var(
        m.U,
        m.T,
        domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
        bounds=dispatch_bounds,
        initialize=dispatch_init,
        doc="Power generated by unit u in period t.",
    )

    m.on = pyo.Var(
        m.U,
        m.T,
        domain=pyo.Binary,
        initialize=0,
        doc="Binary commitment status.",
    )

    def min_output_rule(m, u, t):
        return m.dispatch[u, t] >= m.p_min[u] * m.on[u, t]

    def max_output_rule(m, u, t):
        return m.dispatch[u, t] <= m.p_max[u] * m.on[u, t]

    def balance_rule(m, t):
        return sum(m.dispatch[u, t] for u in m.U) >= m.demand[t]

    m.min_output = pyo.Constraint(m.U, m.T, rule=min_output_rule)
    m.max_output = pyo.Constraint(m.U, m.T, rule=max_output_rule)
    m.balance = pyo.Constraint(m.T, rule=balance_rule)

    m.obj = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(m.variable_cost[u] * m.dispatch[u, t] for u in m.U for t in m.T),
        sense=pyo.minimize,
    )

    return m


def apply_warm_start(m: pyo.ConcreteModel, start: dict[tuple[str, int], float]) -> None:
    valid = set(m.dispatch.keys())
    extra = set(start) - valid
    if extra:
        raise KeyError(f"unknown dispatch start indices: {sorted(extra)[:10]}")

    for idx, value in start.items():
        m.dispatch[idx].set_value(value)


def fix_commitments(m: pyo.ConcreteModel, commitment: dict[tuple[str, int], int]) -> None:
    valid = set(m.on.keys())
    extra = set(commitment) - valid
    if extra:
        raise KeyError(f"unknown commitment indices: {sorted(extra)[:10]}")

    for idx, value in commitment.items():
        if value not in (0, 1):
            raise ValueError(f"commitment[{idx}] must be 0 or 1")
        m.on[idx].fix(value)


def unfix_commitments(m: pyo.ConcreteModel) -> None:
    for idx in m.on:
        m.on[idx].unfix()
```

---

## 7.34 Final checklist

```text id="p7boap"
[ ] Use Var for numeric decision variables.
[ ] Use domain= or within= intentionally; prefer domain= in generated code.
[ ] Use Binary for algebraic 0/1 decisions.
[ ] Use BooleanVar, not Var(Boolean), for logical propositions.
[ ] Use bounds= for physical/numerical lower/upper limits.
[ ] Use rule-based bounds when bounds vary by index.
[ ] Use initialize= for starts, especially NLP/MINLP.
[ ] Use sparse tuple sets for sparse variables.
[ ] Avoid dense Cartesian products for sparse decisions.
[ ] Use fix(value) to force a variable.
[ ] Use .value / set_value only for start/incumbent values.
[ ] Use setlb/setub for bound updates.
[ ] Do not use variable-dependent bounds; use constraints.
[ ] Do not confuse equal bounds with fixed=True.
[ ] Validate warm-start dictionaries against variable keys.
[ ] Audit unbounded variables before solve.
[ ] Audit uninitialized nonlinear variables before solve.
[ ] Gate solution extraction on solver status and loaded results.
[ ] For persistent solvers, synchronize variable bound/value/fix changes according to interface rules.
```

[1]: https://pyomo.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/pyomo.core.base.var.Var.html "Var — Pyomo 6.10.0 documentation"
[2]: https://pyomo.readthedocs.io/en/6.8.2/howto/manipulating.html "Manipulating Pyomo Models — Pyomo 6.8.2 documentation"
[3]: https://pyomo.readthedocs.io/en/6.4.1/modeling_extensions/gdp/modeling.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com "Modeling in Pyomo.GDP — Pyomo 6.4.1 documentation"
[4]: https://pyomo.readthedocs.io/en/6.8.0/pyomo_modeling_components/Variables.html "Variables — Pyomo 6.8.0 documentation"
[5]: https://pyomo.readthedocs.io/en/stable/howto/solver_recipes.html "Solver Recipes — Pyomo 6.10.0 documentation"

# 8) Expressions and expression construction — Pyomo deep dive

Style target: uploaded advanced technical-doc plan. 

Pyomo expressions are **symbolic expression trees** representing objectives, constraints, and other modeling components. Pyomo builds these trees through Python operator overloading / magic methods: for `e = M.v * 2`, Python calls `M.v.__mul__(2)` and Pyomo returns a `ProductExpression` with operands `M.v` and `2`; leaves are operands such as constants, variables, and parameters, and interior nodes are operators. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

---

## 8.0 Mental model

```text id="i1gm66"
Pyomo expression:
  symbolic tree
  not a numeric value
  constructed by overloaded Python operators
  consumed by Objective / Constraint / Expression / Piecewise / transformations / solver writers

Numeric evaluation:
  pyo.value(expr)
  requires all variable/parameter leaves needed for evaluation to have numeric values

Solver export:
  expression tree -> representation classification -> solver writer / direct interface
  linear / quadratic / nonlinear classification affects solver compatibility and performance
```

Core distinction:

```text id="uo12gu"
Python expression:
  evaluates immediately to Python object

Pyomo algebraic expression:
  builds symbolic object; evaluated later by solver or pyo.value(...)
```

Example:

```python id="xv5zxh"
import pyomo.environ as pyo

m = pyo.ConcreteModel()
m.x = pyo.Var()

e = 2 * m.x + 1
# e is symbolic, not float
```

---

## 8.1 Expression construction by operator overloading

### 8.1.1 Arithmetic operators

```python id="eumfkq"
e1 = m.x + m.y
e2 = m.x - 3
e3 = 2 * m.x
e4 = m.x / (m.y + 1)
e5 = m.x ** 2
e6 = -m.x
```

Generated object classes may include sum/product/power/negation/division expression nodes. Do not depend on internal class names in application code.

### 8.1.2 Relational operators

```python id="xlyovf"
c1_expr = m.x <= 10
c2_expr = m.x >= m.y
c3_expr = m.x + m.y == 1
```

Relational expressions are normally passed to `Constraint`.

```python id="ie7xrw"
m.c1 = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x <= 10)
m.c2 = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= m.y)
m.c3 = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x + m.y == 1)
```

### 8.1.3 Chained inequality warning

Avoid Python chained comparisons:

```python id="2muh2j"
# Avoid
m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=0 <= m.x <= 10)
```

Use Pyomo ranged-expression tuple form:

```python id="klolsy"
m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=(0, m.x, 10))
```

or two constraints:

```python id="97bchh"
m.lb = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= 0)
m.ub = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x <= 10)
```

Agent rule:

```text id="ikqeur"
Do not rely on Python chained comparison semantics for symbolic algebra.
Use tuple ranged constraints or explicit lower/upper constraints.
```

---

## 8.2 Expression classes recognized by Pyomo

Pyomo recognizes broad expression classes: **linear polynomials**, **quadratic polynomials**, and **general nonlinear expressions**, including higher-order polynomials and intrinsic functions. Pyomo uses these classes to generate compact expression representations and to transform expression trees into solver-facing standard forms; not every quadratic-looking expression is immediately recognized as quadratic unless processed for that purpose. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

| Class                | Example                                         | Solver implication                                        |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| linear               | `3*x + 2*y - p`                                 | LP/MILP-compatible if domains fit                         |
| quadratic            | `x*x + x*y`                                     | QP/MIQP/QCP solver needed                                 |
| nonlinear polynomial | `x**3`, `(sum(x[i]))**2` when treated generally | NLP/MINLP-compatible path                                 |
| nonlinear intrinsic  | `sin(x)`, `exp(x)`, `log(x)`, `sqrt(x)`         | nonlinear solver; domain/initialization critical          |
| rational             | `x / y`                                         | nonlinear; denominator bounds required                    |
| external             | `m.f(x)`                                        | solver-interface-specific; not accepted by linear solvers |

---

## 8.3 Native algebraic syntax

### 8.3.1 Objective expression

```python id="ndgjey"
m.obj = pyo.Objective(
    expr=sum(m.cost[i] * m.x[i] for i in m.I),
    sense=pyo.minimize,
)
```

### 8.3.2 Constraint expression

```python id="u8m9sg"
m.capacity = pyo.Constraint(
    expr=sum(m.weight[i] * m.x[i] for i in m.I) <= m.capacity_limit
)
```

### 8.3.3 Indexed constraint expression rule

```python id="f3372k"
def demand_rule(m, j):
    return sum(m.ship[i, j] for i in m.I if (i, j) in m.ARCS) >= m.demand[j]

m.demand_con = pyo.Constraint(m.J, rule=demand_rule)
```

Constraint constructor docs state that `expr` is a Pyomo expression and `rule` is a function used to construct constraint expressions; the component defines constraint expressions using that rule function. ([Pyomo Documentation][3])

---

## 8.4 Rule-generated expressions

### 8.4.1 Rule contract

```text id="ij0c9n"
Objective(rule=f):
  f(model) -> numeric Pyomo expression

Constraint(rule=f):
  f(model) -> relational Pyomo expression

Constraint(index_set, rule=f):
  f(model, *index_tuple) -> relational Pyomo expression / tuple / Constraint.Skip
```

Pyomo docs state that objectives and constraints both use rules to generate expressions; these are first-class Python functions that return appropriate expressions and can access global data and model data. ([Pyomo Documentation][4])

### 8.4.2 Objective rule

```python id="yvynw0"
def obj_rule(m):
    return sum(m.cost[i] * m.x[i] for i in m.I)

m.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)
```

### 8.4.3 Constraint rule

```python id="0xbwsa"
def capacity_rule(m):
    return sum(m.weight[i] * m.x[i] for i in m.I) <= m.capacity

m.capacity_con = pyo.Constraint(rule=capacity_rule)
```

### 8.4.4 Indexed constraint rule

```python id="e8w9cn"
def flow_balance_rule(m, n):
    return (
        m.supply[n]
        + sum(m.flow[i, n] for i in m.NODES_IN[n])
        - m.demand[n]
        - sum(m.flow[n, j] for j in m.NODES_OUT[n])
        == 0
    )

m.balance = pyo.Constraint(m.NODES, rule=flow_balance_rule)
```

### 8.4.5 Conditional expression construction using Python data

```python id="15j2pw"
include_penalty = True

def obj_rule(m):
    expr = sum(m.cost[i] * m.x[i] for i in m.I)
    if include_penalty:
        expr += m.penalty * sum(m.slack[i] for i in m.I)
    return expr
```

This is valid because `include_penalty` is a Python boolean known at construction time.

### 8.4.6 Conditional construction using Pyomo data

Wrong in abstract/symbolic contexts:

```python id="cfzqc5"
def c_rule(m):
    expr = sum(m.x[i] for i in m.I)
    if m.threshold >= 2:  # creates symbolic expression, not Python bool
        expr -= m.y
    return expr >= 0
```

Correct:

```python id="hq5gkz"
def c_rule(m):
    expr = sum(m.x[i] for i in m.I)
    if pyo.value(m.threshold) >= 2:
        expr -= m.y
    return expr >= 0
```

Pyomo docs explicitly warn that `model.d >= 2` creates an expression rather than an evaluated value in an abstract model, and advise using `value(model.d)` when a construction-time Python conditional needs the numeric value. ([Pyomo Documentation][4])

Agent rule:

```text id="p40zcy"
Use Python if only on Python data or pyo.value(...) of initialized fixed data.
Never use Python if on unfixed Vars or symbolic relational expressions.
If the condition is a decision, model it with binaries, GDP, complementarity, or disjunctions.
```

---

## 8.5 Expression components vs Python helper functions

### 8.5.1 Python helper function

```python id="m7ckhi"
def shipping_cost(m):
    return sum(m.cost[i, j] * m.ship[i, j] for (i, j) in m.ARCS)

m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=shipping_cost(m))
```

Properties:

```text id="9jlr98"
no Pyomo component created
expression tree inserted where function is called
good for one-time expression construction
may duplicate tree if called repeatedly
```

### 8.5.2 Pyomo `Expression` component

```python id="38ho50"
def shipping_cost_rule(m):
    return sum(m.cost[i, j] * m.ship[i, j] for (i, j) in m.ARCS)

m.shipping_cost = pyo.Expression(rule=shipping_cost_rule)
m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.shipping_cost)
```

Properties:

```text id="756exc"
named Pyomo component
reusable in multiple constraints/objectives
introspectable
set_value(...) mutable expression body
can reduce duplicated model code
does not create an additional solver variable by itself
```

Pyomo docs describe `Expression` objects as similar to mutable `Param` components except that their underlying values can be numeric constants or Pyomo expressions; the example shows indexed `Expression` objects, evaluation with `value(instance.e[1])`, and updating the underlying expression with `.value = instance.x**2`. ([Pyomo Documentation][4])

### 8.5.3 Indexed `Expression`

```python id="e1i4qm"
def revenue_rule(m, p):
    return m.price[p] * m.sales[p]

m.revenue = pyo.Expression(m.P, rule=revenue_rule)

m.total_revenue = pyo.Expression(
    expr=sum(m.revenue[p] for p in m.P)
)
```

### 8.5.4 Expression update

```python id="i18ehx"
m.total_cost = pyo.Expression(expr=sum(m.cost[i] * m.x[i] for i in m.I))

# later, replace expression body
m.total_cost.set_value(
    sum(m.cost[i] * m.x[i] for i in m.I) + m.fixed_charge
)
```

or:

```python id="5goe8r"
m.total_cost.value = new_expr
```

The `SimpleExpression`/`ExpressionData` API exposes `.expr`, `.set_value(expr)`, `.to_string(...)`, `.is_fixed()`, `.is_potentially_variable()`, and `.polynomial_degree()`, supporting named-expression mutation and inspection. ([Pyomo Documentation][5])

---

## 8.6 When to use `Expression`

| Need                                      |            Use Python helper |       Use `pyo.Expression` |
| ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------: | -------------------------: |
| one-time objective body                   |                          yes |                   optional |
| reused expression in many constraints     | possible but duplicates tree |                        yes |
| named reporting expression                |                           no |                        yes |
| expression body changes between solves    |                      awkward |                        yes |
| decomposition / block-local metric        |                     possible |                        yes |
| avoid adding algebraic variable           |                          yes |                        yes |
| need solver variable for expression value |                           no | no; use `Var + Constraint` |

Key distinction:

```text id="pbtnpa"
Expression:
  alias / named formula

Var + Constraint:
  actual decision variable linked to formula
```

Example: named cost only

```python id="yg3mnp"
m.total_cost = pyo.Expression(expr=sum(m.c[i] * m.x[i] for i in m.I))
m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.total_cost)
```

Example: cost variable needed in other model logic

```python id="rd4reg"
m.total_cost_var = pyo.Var()

m.total_cost_def = pyo.Constraint(
    expr=m.total_cost_var == sum(m.c[i] * m.x[i] for i in m.I)
)
```

---

## 8.7 `pyo.value(...)` and expression evaluation

### 8.7.1 Basic evaluation

```python id="xs1yw9"
val = pyo.value(m.obj)
x_val = pyo.value(m.x[i])
expr_val = pyo.value(m.total_cost)
```

`pyo.value(obj, exception=True)` returns the value of a Pyomo object or expression; for primitive numeric values it returns the argument, and for Pyomo numeric objects it executes the object’s `__call__`; if evaluation fails because variables are uninitialized, `exception=True` raises, while `exception=False` returns `None`. ([Pyomo Documentation][6])

### 8.7.2 Exception-safe evaluation

```python id="kzsfh7"
maybe_val = pyo.value(m.x[i], exception=False)
```

### 8.7.3 Evaluation after solve

```python id="lsfslj"
results = opt.solve(m, load_solutions=False)

if results.solver.termination_condition == pyo.TerminationCondition.optimal:
    m.solutions.load_from(results)
    print(pyo.value(m.obj))
```

### 8.7.4 Do not evaluate symbolic expressions during construction unless intended

Bad for mutable parameters:

```python id="4bs1mx"
m.rhs = pyo.Param(initialize=10, mutable=True)
m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= pyo.value(m.rhs))  # freezes current value
```

Correct:

```python id="mfj827"
m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= m.rhs)
```

### 8.7.5 Do not evaluate uninitialized variables

```python id="0tzbk6"
# before solve or initialization:
pyo.value(m.x)  # likely error
```

Safe:

```python id="updejr"
pyo.value(m.x, exception=False)
```

---

## 8.8 Expression cloning and replacement

### 8.8.1 Component clone

```python id="dr3tuy"
m2 = m.clone()
```

Model/block clone copies expression trees owned by the cloned scope.

### 8.8.2 Expression object clone/no-op nuance

`ExpressionData` is a named expression object whose `clone()` method is documented as returning a clone no-op; `NamedExpressionData` exists as a base for `ExpressionData` and `ObjectiveData`, so application code should avoid assuming `expr.clone()` deep-copies referenced model components. ([Pyomo Documentation][7])

Agent rule:

```text id="bv23ph"
Clone whole model/block for independent model copies.
Do not rely on low-level expression clone behavior for model duplication.
Use expression visitors only for advanced transformations.
```

### 8.8.3 Identify variables in expression

```python id="ur4asd"
import pyomo.core.expr as EXPR

vars_in_expr = list(EXPR.identify_variables(m.obj.expr, include_fixed=True))
free_vars = list(EXPR.identify_variables(m.obj.expr, include_fixed=False))
```

Pyomo provides `identify_components` to yield nodes of specified types and `identify_variables` to yield variable nodes in an expression tree; `include_fixed=False` omits fixed variables. ([Pyomo Documentation][8])

### 8.8.4 Identify mutable Params in expression

```python id="oxalnh"
import pyomo.core.expr as EXPR

param_type = type(m.mutable_param)
params = list(EXPR.identify_components(m.expr.expr, {param_type}))
```

### 8.8.5 Advanced visitor classes

Use only for transformations/reformulations:

```text id="d9h5cs"
StreamBasedExpressionVisitor
SimpleExpressionVisitor
ExpressionValueVisitor
ExpressionReplacementVisitor
```

Pyomo documents visitor classes for walking expression trees, including value visitors and replacement visitors, but notes expression-tree walking requires intimate knowledge of expression-system design. ([Pyomo Documentation][8])

### 8.9.1 Polynomial degree

deg = m.obj.expr.polynomial_degree()
```

linear expression       -> 1

### 8.9.2 Fixed / constant / potentially variable

expr = m.total_cost.expr

expr.is_fixed()
expr.is_constant()
expr.is_potentially_variable()
```

Expression APIs document methods such as `is_fixed`, `is_constant`, `is_potentially_variable`, `is_expression_type`, and `polynomial_degree`, allowing agents to inspect expression character and solver compatibility. ([Pyomo Documentation][5])

### 8.9.3 String rendering

```python id="2btulc"
print(m.obj.expr.to_string())
print(m.total_cost.to_string())
```

### 8.9.4 Constraint body/lower/upper

```python id="d3fsgc"
c = m.capacity
body = c.body
lb = c.lower
ub = c.upper
```

Useful for diagnostics and persistent-solver update checks.

## 8.10 Expression performance

### 8.10.1 Prefer generator `sum(...)` over manual incremental `s = s + term`

Slower/manual:

```python id="idsjmk"
s = 0
for i in m.I:
    s = s + m.x[i]
```

Better:

```python id="ubh3h0"
s = sum(m.x[i] for i in m.I)
```

Pyomo performance docs state expressions can be built with native binary operators, but Python `sum()` is more compact and more efficient than manual accumulation because it avoids temporary variables and executes summation logic inside the Python interpreter. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 8.10.2 Use `pyo.quicksum(...)` for compact Pyomo expression representation

```python id="klgl7h"
s = pyo.quicksum(m.x[i] for i in m.I)
```

Linear hint:

```python id="cuvf9j"
s = pyo.quicksum((m.c[i] * m.x[i] for i in m.I), linear=True)
```

Nonlinear hint:

```python id="sfmmxp"
s = pyo.quicksum((m.x[i] ** 2 for i in m.I), linear=False)
```

`quicksum` often generates a more compact Pyomo expression; it can be slower than built-in `sum()` during expression creation, but the compact representation can make problem representation generation faster. Its `linear` argument controls processing assumptions, where `True` assumes linear terms, `False` assumes nonlinear terms, and `None` analyzes the first term. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 8.10.3 Use `pyo.sum_product(...)` for dot products

```python id="u1v3a6"
m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=pyo.sum_product(m.c, m.x))
```

With index:

```python id="66jm2b"
expr = pyo.sum_product(m.c, m.x, index=m.I)
```

Denominator form:

```python id="ry6b74"
expr = pyo.sum_product(m.x, denom=m.y)
```

`sum_product` supports generalized dot products and explicitly specified terms, allowing Pyomo to identify whether the resulting expression is linear, quadratic, or nonlinear; docs state it is typically faster than simple loops and generates compact representations. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 8.10.4 Use `pyo.prod(...)` for products

```python id="arhl4i"
expr = pyo.prod(m.x[i] for i in m.I)
```

### 8.10.5 Avoid repeated expression helper calls

Bad:

```python id="u6h3zk"
def total_flow(m):
    return sum(m.flow[a] for a in m.ARCS)

m.c1 = pyo.Constraint(expr=total_flow(m) <= m.cap)
m.c2 = pyo.Constraint(expr=total_flow(m) >= m.min_flow)
m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.cost * total_flow(m))
```

Better:

```python id="e4ovlf"
m.total_flow = pyo.Expression(expr=sum(m.flow[a] for a in m.ARCS))

m.c1 = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.total_flow <= m.cap)
m.c2 = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.total_flow >= m.min_flow)
m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.cost * m.total_flow)
```

### 8.10.6 Avoid dense sums over sparse structures

Bad:

```python id="61g21j"
def balance_rule(m, n):
    return (
        sum(m.flow[i, n] for i in m.NODES if (i, n) in m.ARCS)
        - sum(m.flow[n, j] for j in m.NODES if (n, j) in m.ARCS)
        == 0
    )
```

Better:

```python id="azagtw"
def balance_rule(m, n):
    return (
        sum(m.flow[i, n] for i in m.NODES_IN[n])
        - sum(m.flow[n, j] for j in m.NODES_OUT[n])
        == 0
    )
```

Performance rule:

```text id="m060w1"
Expression performance is dominated by:
  Python loop count
  expression tree size
  repeated tree construction
  dense index products
  repeated membership checks
  solver-representation generation cost
```

---

## 8.11 Linear expression construction patterns

### 8.11.1 Objective dot product

```python id="p5k73a"
m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=pyo.sum_product(m.c, m.x))
```

### 8.11.2 Sparse objective

```python id="rxzq3t"
m.obj = pyo.Objective(
    expr=sum(m.c[a] * m.flow[a] for a in m.ARCS)
)
```

### 8.11.3 Large linear objective with `quicksum`

```python id="ek0oqn"
m.obj = pyo.Objective(
    expr=pyo.quicksum((m.c[a] * m.flow[a] for a in m.ARCS), linear=True)
)
```

### 8.11.4 Avoid Python list materialization

Bad:

```python id="q1wjf2"
expr = sum([m.c[i] * m.x[i] for i in m.I])
```

Better:

```python id="ufz9cw"
expr = sum(m.c[i] * m.x[i] for i in m.I)
```

Reason:

```text id="5w5di0"
list comprehension stores all term objects
generator expression streams terms to sum/quicksum
```

## 8.12 Nonlinear expressions

### 8.12.1 Intrinsic functions

```python id="upgi0y"
m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=pyo.log(m.x) + pyo.exp(m.y) <= 10)
m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=(m.x - 1) ** 2 + pyo.sin(m.y))
```

### 8.12.2 Domain-safe variables

```python id="pfqqyb"
m.x = pyo.Var(bounds=(1e-6, None), initialize=1.0)  # for log/sqrt/denominator
m.y = pyo.Var(initialize=0.0)
```

### 8.12.3 Nonlinear solver path

```python id="1jgxcm"
opt = pyo.SolverFactory("ipopt")
results = opt.solve(m)
```

Pyomo modeling docs note that Pyomo supports nonlinear expressions and can call nonlinear solvers such as Ipopt. ([Pyomo Documentation][4])

### 8.12.4 MINLP path

```python id="v0h4by"
m.y = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.Binary)
m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.y * (m.x - 1) ** 2)
```

Requires:

```text id="eq9psc"
MINLP-capable solver or decomposition meta-solver
valid bounds
good starts for continuous variables
integer domains intentionally declared
```

### 8.12.5 Fixed variables in nonlinear-looking expressions

```python id="8yd2ae"
m.y.fix(2.0)
m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.z == m.x * m.y)
```

Some solver interfaces may treat fixed variables like parameters; APPSI/new-solver-interface docs note an option `treat_fixed_vars_as_params`, where fixed variables can make expressions such as `z == x*y` linear for LP export, but changing fixed variable values may require reprocessing constraints. ([Pyomo Documentation][9])

---

## 8.13 Solver compatibility

| Expression type             | Variable domains          | Compatible solver family           | Agent action                          |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| linear                      | continuous                | LP                                 | `glpk`, `highs`, `cbc`, commercial LP |
| linear                      | binary/integer present    | MILP                               | MILP solver                           |
| quadratic convex            | continuous                | QP                                 | QP-capable solver                     |
| quadratic + integer         | mixed-integer             | MIQP/MIQCP                         | compatible commercial/open solver     |
| general nonlinear           | continuous                | NLP                                | Ipopt/Knitro/etc.                     |
| general nonlinear + integer | mixed-integer             | MINLP                              | MindtPy/SCIP/Knitro/etc.              |
| external function           | continuous/nonlinear      | interface-specific NLP only        | avoid unless solver supports it       |
| piecewise                   | depends on representation | MILP/SOS/NLP depending formulation | choose `pw_repn` deliberately         |

`ExternalFunction` can embed user-provided functions in Pyomo expressions, but Pyomo docs warn that expressibility does not imply solvability: linear solvers do not accept external functions, and ASL external-function support is limited to nonlinear solvers compiled against ASL and compiled-library AMPL external functions. ([Pyomo Documentation][10])

---

## 8.14 Piecewise expression boundary

### 8.14.1 Piecewise declaration

```python id="nhbsfq"
m.pw = pyo.Piecewise(
    m.J,
    m.y,
    m.x,
    pw_pts=bpts,
    pw_constr_type="EQ",
    f_rule=f_rule,
    pw_repn="SOS2",
)
```

### 8.14.2 Required bound coverage

Piecewise docs state that `pw_pts` are always required and expected to span the bounds of the independent variables; they also state that variables appearing as independent variables in piecewise constraints must have bounds. ([Pyomo Documentation][4])

Agent rule:

```text id="cf9v9n"
Piecewise is not just expression syntax.
It creates constraints / auxiliary variables according to representation.
Set x variable bounds before Piecewise.
Pick pw_repn based on solver support and formulation size.
```

## 8.15 Python helper functions that work with Pyomo objects

### 8.15.1 Helper returns numeric when given numerics

```python id="aidutt"
def affine(x, a, b):
    return a * x + b

affine(2, 3, 4)  # 10
```

### 8.15.2 Same helper returns Pyomo expression when given Pyomo objects

```python id="9fczc2"
m.y_expr = affine(m.x, m.a, m.b)
```

Pyomo docs show this exact general idea: a Python function like `f(x, p): return x + p` returns a number for numeric inputs and a Pyomo expression for Pyomo component inputs due to operator overloading. ([Pyomo Documentation][4])

### 8.15.3 Good helper function style

```python id="uqskf7"
def weighted_sum(var, coeff, index):
    return sum(coeff[i] * var[i] for i in index)
```

Use:

```python id="ukx1zb"
m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=weighted_sum(m.x, m.c, m.I))
```

### 8.15.4 Bad helper function style

```python id="2wkr1t"
def weighted_sum_value(var, coeff, index):
    return sum(pyo.value(coeff[i] * var[i]) for i in index)
```

Reason:

```text id="rxwfp7"
forces numeric evaluation
fails before solve if variables uninitialized
destroys symbolic algebra
```

## 8.16 Expression mutation in repeated solves

### 8.16.1 Replace objective expression

```python id="on44lu"
m.obj.set_value(sum(m.new_cost[i] * m.x[i] for i in m.I))
```

or reconstruct objective:

```python id="2zfr6s"
m.obj.expr = sum(m.new_cost[i] * m.x[i] for i in m.I)
```

### 8.16.2 Replace named expression body

```python id="b5kgqv"
m.penalty_expr.set_value(m.penalty_weight * sum(m.slack[i] for i in m.I))
```

### 8.16.3 Persistent/APPSI caveat

Solver-interface update configs may need to detect changed objectives, constraints, parameters, variables, and named expressions. The new-solver-interface docs expose update flags such as `update_constraints`, `update_parameters`, `update_named_expressions`, and `update_objective`, and warn that disabling them is only safe if manually updating the solver or if components are not modified. ([Pyomo Documentation][9])

Deployment rule:

```text id="342psa"
File-based solve:
  expression changes visible on next export/solve

Persistent/APPSI solve:
  verify interface update detection or call explicit update APIs
```

## 8.17 Expression evaluation audit utilities

### 8.17.1 Safe objective value

```python id="aeq5o1"
def objective_value(m):
    return pyo.value(m.obj, exception=False)
```

### 8.17.2 Evaluate all named expressions

```python id="89kdar"
def expression_values(m):
    out = {}
    for e in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Expression, active=True, descend_into=True):
        out[e.name] = pyo.value(e, exception=False)
    return out
```

### 8.17.3 Identify variables in a constraint

```python id="e0vj4q"
import pyomo.core.expr as EXPR

def vars_in_constraint(c):
    return list(EXPR.identify_variables(c.body, include_fixed=True))
```

### 8.17.4 Expression degree audit

```python id="dbpizv"
def nonlinear_constraints(m):
    out = []
    for c in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Constraint, active=True, descend_into=True):
        deg = c.body.polynomial_degree()
        if deg is None or deg > 1:
            out.append((c.name, deg))
    return out
```

## 8.18 Large-model expression performance patterns

### 8.18.1 Precompute adjacency once

```python id="pdrfqp"
nodes_in = {n: [] for n in nodes}
nodes_out = {n: [] for n in nodes}
for i, j in arcs:
    nodes_out[i].append(j)
    nodes_in[j].append(i)
```

Then use indexed sets / dictionaries rather than filtering dense sets inside rules.

### 8.18.2 Reuse subexpressions with `Expression`

```python id="zwngb6"
m.unit_cost = pyo.Expression(m.U, rule=lambda m, u: m.fixed[u] * m.open[u] + m.var[u] * m.prod[u])

m.total_cost = pyo.Expression(expr=sum(m.unit_cost[u] for u in m.U))
m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.total_cost)
```

### 8.18.3 Avoid nested expression helper rebuilding

Bad:

```python id="7dknug"
def unit_cost(m, u):
    return m.fixed[u] * m.open[u] + m.var[u] * m.prod[u]

m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=sum(unit_cost(m, u) for u in m.U))
m.budget = pyo.Constraint(expr=sum(unit_cost(m, u) for u in m.U) <= m.budget_cap)
```

Better:

```python id="yxagsq"
m.unit_cost = pyo.Expression(m.U, rule=lambda m, u: m.fixed[u] * m.open[u] + m.var[u] * m.prod[u])
m.total_cost = pyo.Expression(expr=sum(m.unit_cost[u] for u in m.U))

m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.total_cost)
m.budget = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.total_cost <= m.budget_cap)
```

### 8.18.4 Avoid unnecessary nonlinear expressions

Bad:

```python id="vqqql3"
m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=(sum(m.x[i] for i in m.I)) ** 2)
```

If intended quadratic expansion:

```python id="1t1o4g"
s = sum(m.x[i] for i in m.I)
m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=s * s)
```

Still nonlinear/quadratic; ensure QP/NLP solver path.

If intended linear penalty:

```python id="mqvdjf"
m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=sum(m.penalty[i] * m.x[i] for i in m.I))
```

## 8.20 Expression safety rules

### 8.20.1 Symbolic construction only

Good:

```python id="u2gfn1"
m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x + m.y >= m.rhs)
```

Bad:

```python id="y2p6qn"
m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=pyo.value(m.x + m.y) >= m.rhs)
```

### 8.20.2 Python `math` vs Pyomo functions

Bad:

```python id="flgyvj"
import math
m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=math.log(m.x) <= 1)
```

Correct:

```python id="jutq40"
m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=pyo.log(m.x) <= 1)
```

Agent rule:

```text id="xqro18"
Use Pyomo math functions for symbolic expressions.
Use Python math only on plain numeric data.
```

### 8.20.3 NumPy operations

Risky:

```python id="h0gl6o"
expr = numpy.dot(coeff_array, [m.x[i] for i in m.I])
```

Better:

```python id="jhgqj1"
expr = sum(float(c[i]) * m.x[i] for i in m.I)
```

Reason:

```text id="b5hiy0"
NumPy may coerce objects or create object arrays.
Solver writers often expect native numeric/Pyomo expression objects.
Keep Pyomo expression construction explicit.
```

### 8.20.4 Avoid evaluating variables in rule conditions

Bad:

```python id="3zturk"
def rule(m, i):
    if m.x[i] >= 0:
        return m.y[i] >= 1
    return pyo.Constraint.Skip
```

Correct modeling options:

```text id="kqz3j2"
construction-time condition on data:
  if pyo.value(m.param[i]) >= 0

decision-dependent condition:
  binary indicator + big-M
  GDP disjunction
  complementarity
  logical constraint
```

---

## 8.21 External functions and solver compatibility

### 8.21.1 Declaration

```python id="4i0l7t"
def f(x):
    return x**2 + 1

m.f = pyo.ExternalFunction(function=f)
m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.f(m.x) <= 10)
```

### 8.21.2 Deployment checklist

```text id="zgnnct"
[ ] nonlinear solver path only
[ ] no LP/MILP solver
[ ] deterministic function
[ ] no file/network side effects
[ ] derivative availability documented
[ ] callback tested outside Pyomo
[ ] solver interface supports callback/external function path
```

Pyomo’s AML reference states `ExternalFunction` embeds user-provided functions in Pyomo expressions but warns linear solvers do not accept them; ASL support is limited and interface-specific. ([Pyomo Documentation][10])

## 8.22 Production expression contract

### 8.22.1 Model factory

```python id="q8o1l2"
def build_model(data):
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=data.items)
    m.cost = pyo.Param(m.I, initialize=data.cost)
    m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    m.total_cost = pyo.Expression(
        expr=sum(m.cost[i] * m.x[i] for i in m.I)
    )

    m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.total_cost)

    return m
```

### 8.22.2 Expression audit before solve

```python id="g5ahtd"
def expression_audit(m):
    constraints = list(m.component_data_objects(pyo.Constraint, active=True, descend_into=True))
    objectives = list(m.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=True, descend_into=True))

    return {
        "n_constraints": len(constraints),
        "n_objectives": len(objectives),
        "constraint_degrees": {
            c.name: c.body.polynomial_degree()
            for c in constraints
        },
        "objective_degrees": {
            o.name: o.expr.polynomial_degree()
            for o in objectives
        },
    }
```

### 8.22.3 Solver selection from expression degree

```python id="2h1n9t"
def infer_required_solver_family(m):
    max_degree = 0
    general_nonlinear = False
    integer = any(v.is_integer() for v in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True))

    for obj in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=True, descend_into=True):
        deg = obj.expr.polynomial_degree()
        if deg is None:
            general_nonlinear = True
        else:
            max_degree = max(max_degree, deg)

    for con in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Constraint, active=True, descend_into=True):
        deg = con.body.polynomial_degree()
        if deg is None:
            general_nonlinear = True
        else:
            max_degree = max(max_degree, deg)

    if general_nonlinear:
        return "MINLP" if integer else "NLP"
    if max_degree > 2:
        return "MINLP" if integer else "NLP"
    if max_degree == 2:
        return "MIQP/QCP" if integer else "QP/QCP"
    return "MILP" if integer else "LP"
```

## 8.23 Testing patterns

### 8.23.1 Expression value after solution

```python id="dbmwly"
def test_total_cost_value(model, solved_model):
    assert pyo.value(solved_model.total_cost) >= 0
```

### 8.23.2 Expression degree

```python id="96os12"
def test_objective_is_linear(model):
    assert model.obj.expr.polynomial_degree() == 1
```

### 8.23.3 No uninitialized variables in nonlinear starts

```python id="4gqs2h"
def test_all_nlp_vars_initialized(model):
    missing = [
        v.name
        for v in model.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True)
        if v.value is None and not v.fixed
    ]
    assert not missing
```

### 8.23.4 No accidental dense expression size

```python id="ztx44z"
def test_sparse_objective_uses_arcs(model):
    vars_in_obj = list(EXPR.identify_variables(model.obj.expr))
    assert len(vars_in_obj) == len(model.ARCS)
```

### 8.23.5 No nonlinear constraints for LP model

```python id="if71i4"
def test_lp_constraints_linear(model):
    nonlinear = [
        (c.name, c.body.polynomial_degree())
        for c in model.component_data_objects(pyo.Constraint, active=True, descend_into=True)
        if c.body.polynomial_degree() != 1
    ]
    assert not nonlinear
```

## 8.24 Deployment advisory

```text id="b9fgid"
[ ] Use symbolic Pyomo expressions in Objective / Constraint / Expression.
[ ] Use pyo.value(...) only for numeric extraction or construction-time data conditions.
[ ] Use Pyomo math functions, not Python math, for symbolic expressions.
[ ] Use pyo.sum_product for dot products.
[ ] Use pyo.quicksum for large sums where compact representation helps.
[ ] Use generator expressions, not list comprehensions, for large sums.
[ ] Use Expression components for reused named formulas.
[ ] Avoid repeated helper calls that clone/rebuild large expression trees.
[ ] Avoid dense sums over sparse structures.
[ ] Audit polynomial_degree() before selecting solver family.
[ ] Bound and initialize variables in nonlinear expressions.
[ ] Avoid ExternalFunction unless solver path explicitly supports it.
[ ] For persistent/APPSI solvers, verify named-expression/objective/constraint update detection.
```

---

## 8.25 Anti-pattern table

| Anti-pattern                                                       | Failure mode                                       | Replacement                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `math.log(m.x)`                                                    | TypeError / numeric evaluation attempt             | `pyo.log(m.x)`                                         |
| `if m.x >= 0:`                                                     | symbolic relational expression used as Python bool | binary/GDP model or `pyo.value` on fixed data          |
| `pyo.value(m.x)` inside constraint                                 | uninitialized error / frozen numeric value         | symbolic `m.x`                                         |
| repeated helper expression calls                                   | duplicated trees / slow construction               | `pyo.Expression`                                       |
| dense loops with membership tests                                  | slow expression generation                         | sparse sets / adjacency sets                           |
| list comprehensions inside large sums                              | memory overhead                                    | generator expressions                                  |
| manual `s = s + term` loops                                        | temporary expression churn                         | `sum`, `quicksum`, `sum_product`                       |
| assuming nonlinear expression works with MILP solver               | solver export failure                              | NLP/MINLP solver or reformulation                      |
| external function with linear solver                               | unsupported model                                  | algebraic expression or nonlinear-compatible interface |
| replacing `Expression` body under persistent solver without update | stale solver-side representation                   | update/check APPSI/persistent settings                 |
| using `Expression` when solver variable is required                | no actual variable in solver                       | `Var + Constraint` definition                          |

---

## 8.26 Agent-ready production template

```python id="nyjxim"
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

import pyomo.environ as pyo
import pyomo.core.expr as EXPR


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NetworkCostData:
    nodes: tuple[str, ...]
    arcs: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]
    cost: dict[tuple[str, str], float]
    capacity: dict[tuple[str, str], float]
    supply: dict[str, float]
    demand: dict[str, float]


def build_model(data: NetworkCostData) -> pyo.ConcreteModel:
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel(name="expression_contract_demo")

    m.N = pyo.Set(initialize=data.nodes, ordered=True)
    m.A = pyo.Set(dimen=2, within=m.N * m.N, initialize=data.arcs, ordered=True)

    # Precompute adjacency outside expression rules.
    nodes_in = {n: [] for n in data.nodes}
    nodes_out = {n: [] for n in data.nodes}
    for i, j in data.arcs:
        nodes_out[i].append(j)
        nodes_in[j].append(i)

    m.N_IN = pyo.Set(m.N, initialize=lambda m, n: nodes_in[n], within=m.N)
    m.N_OUT = pyo.Set(m.N, initialize=lambda m, n: nodes_out[n], within=m.N)

    m.cost = pyo.Param(m.A, initialize=data.cost, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    m.capacity = pyo.Param(m.A, initialize=data.capacity, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    m.supply = pyo.Param(m.N, initialize=data.supply)
    m.demand = pyo.Param(m.N, initialize=data.demand)

    m.flow = pyo.Var(m.A, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Named reusable expression.
    m.arc_cost = pyo.Expression(
        m.A,
        rule=lambda m, i, j: m.cost[i, j] * m.flow[i, j],
    )

    m.total_cost = pyo.Expression(
        expr=pyo.quicksum((m.arc_cost[i, j] for (i, j) in m.A), linear=True)
    )

    def capacity_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.flow[i, j] <= m.capacity[i, j]

    m.capacity_con = pyo.Constraint(m.A, rule=capacity_rule)

    def balance_rule(m, n):
        return (
            m.supply[n]
            + sum(m.flow[i, n] for i in m.N_IN[n])
            - m.demand[n]
            - sum(m.flow[n, j] for j in m.N_OUT[n])
            == 0
        )

    m.balance = pyo.Constraint(m.N, rule=balance_rule)
    m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.total_cost, sense=pyo.minimize)

    return m


def expression_manifest(m: pyo.ConcreteModel) -> dict:
    constraints = list(m.component_data_objects(pyo.Constraint, active=True, descend_into=True))
    objectives = list(m.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=True, descend_into=True))

    return {
        "objectives": {
            obj.name: {
                "degree": obj.expr.polynomial_degree(),
                "variables": len(list(EXPR.identify_variables(obj.expr))),
            }
            for obj in objectives
        },
        "constraints": {
            con.name: {
                "degree": con.body.polynomial_degree(),
                "variables": len(list(EXPR.identify_variables(con.body))),
            }
            for con in constraints
        },
    }


def extract_expression_values(m: pyo.ConcreteModel) -> dict:
    return {
        expr.name: pyo.value(expr, exception=False)
        for expr in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Expression, active=True, descend_into=True)
    }
```

---

## 8.27 Final checklist

```text id="k2j92w"
[ ] Treat Pyomo algebra as symbolic tree construction.
[ ] Use pyo.value only when numeric evaluation is explicitly intended.
[ ] Use Constraint(expr=...) / Objective(expr=...) for scalar expressions.
[ ] Use rule functions for indexed expressions.
[ ] Use Python conditionals only on Python data or pyo.value(initialized data).
[ ] Use binary/GDP/logical modeling for decision-dependent conditions.
[ ] Use pyo.Expression for reused named formulas.
[ ] Use Var + Constraint when the formula value must be an actual solver variable.
[ ] Use sum/generator, quicksum, sum_product, prod appropriately.
[ ] Avoid manual incremental expression loops for large sums.
[ ] Avoid dense sums and repeated membership filters.
[ ] Precompute sparse adjacency/index supports.
[ ] Use Pyomo math functions for symbolic nonlinear expressions.
[ ] Bound and initialize variables in nonlinear domains.
[ ] Audit polynomial_degree for solver-family compatibility.
[ ] Avoid ExternalFunction unless solver compatibility is explicitly verified.
[ ] For persistent solvers, verify expression/objective/constraint update behavior.
[ ] Unit-test expression degree, value extraction, and variable participation.
```
