## 19.17 GDP transformation wrapper

```python id="o94d4m"
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GDPTransformConfig:
    method: str = "bigm"  # bigm | hull | cuttingplane | mbigm
    bigM: Any | None = None
    mode: str = "apply_to"


def transform_gdp(model: pyo.ConcreteModel, cfg: GDPTransformConfig):
    names = {
        "bigm": "gdp.bigm",
        "mbigm": "gdp.mbigm",
        "hull": "gdp.hull",
        "cuttingplane": "gdp.cuttingplane",
    }

    name = names[cfg.method]
    xfrm = pyo.TransformationFactory(name)

    options = {}
    if cfg.bigM is not None and cfg.method in {"bigm", "mbigm"}:
        options["bigM"] = cfg.bigM

    if cfg.mode == "apply_to":
        xfrm.apply_to(model, **options)
        return model

    if cfg.mode == "create_using":
        return xfrm.create_using(model, **options)

    raise ValueError(cfg.mode)
```

Pre-check for hull:

```python id="yhas4b"
def require_bounds_for_hull(model: pyo.Block):
    missing = []
    for v in model.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True):
        if v.lb is None or v.ub is None:
            missing.append(v.name)

    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"hull transformation requires bounded variables; examples={missing[:20]}")
```

GDP docs specifically note hull requires upper and lower bounds for all variables appearing in disjuncts. ([Pyomo Documentation][3])

## 19.18 DAE transformation wrapper

```python id="k44e4z"
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DAETransformConfig:
    method: str = "finite_difference"  # finite_difference | collocation
    wrt_name: str = "time"
    nfe: int = 20
    ncp: int | None = None
    scheme: str | None = None


def transform_dae(model: pyo.ConcreteModel, cfg: DAETransformConfig):
    contset = model.find_component(cfg.wrt_name)
    if contset is None:
        raise KeyError(f"ContinuousSet not found: {cfg.wrt_name}")

    if cfg.method == "finite_difference":
        opts = {"wrt": contset, "nfe": cfg.nfe}
        if cfg.scheme is not None:
            opts["scheme"] = cfg.scheme
        pyo.TransformationFactory("dae.finite_difference").apply_to(model, **opts)
        return model

    if cfg.method == "collocation":
        opts = {"wrt": contset, "nfe": cfg.nfe}
        if cfg.ncp is not None:
            opts["ncp"] = cfg.ncp
        if cfg.scheme is not None:
            opts["scheme"] = cfg.scheme
        pyo.TransformationFactory("dae.collocation").apply_to(model, **opts)
        return model

    raise ValueError(cfg.method)
```

Post-check:

```python id="7o1kjg"
def dae_grid_manifest(model, contset_name: str) -> dict:
    cs = model.find_component(contset_name)
    return {
        "name": cs.name,
        "points": list(cs),
        "finite_elements": list(cs.get_finite_elements()),
        "discretization_info": cs.get_discretization_info(),
    }
```

`ContinuousSet` exposes `get_discretization_info()` and `get_finite_elements()`, where finite-element behavior differs for collocation versus finite difference. ([Pyomo Documentation][4])

## 19.20 Scaling wrapper

```python id="u8ng9i"
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ScalingConfig:
    mode: str = "create_using"  # apply_to | create_using
    rename: bool = True


def scale_model(model: pyo.ConcreteModel, cfg: ScalingConfig):
    xfrm = pyo.TransformationFactory("core.scale_model")

    if cfg.mode == "apply_to":
        xfrm.apply_to(model, rename=cfg.rename)
        return model, None

    if cfg.mode == "create_using":
        scaled = xfrm.create_using(model, rename=cfg.rename)
        return scaled, xfrm

    raise ValueError(cfg.mode)
```

Solution propagation:

```python id="mpa7hv"

solve_checked(scaled, solver_name="ipopt")
scaling_xfrm.propagate_solution(scaled, model)
```

## 19.21 Solution interpretation after transformations

### 19.21.1 In-place GDP

```text id="eu8ljb"
Original disjunct/disjunction components may be deactivated.
Auxiliary binary variables encode logical selections.
Report original business Vars plus BooleanVars updated from binaries if needed.
Generated constraints/vars should be considered formulation artifacts.
```

### 19.21.2 DAE discretization

```text id="lgaoi6"
Var indexed by ContinuousSet becomes values on discretization grid.
DerivativeVar is represented through discretization equations.
Report trajectories over list(model.time).
If using collocation, distinguish finite element points vs collocation points.
```

### 19.21.3 Network expansion

```text id="hcbq4w"
Arcs are high-level connection declarations.
Expanded blocks contain solver-facing connection constraints.
Report original port/member variables, not generated equality rows.
```

### 19.21.4 Scaling

```text id="ckdh5j"
If scaled clone:
  solve scaled model
  propagate solution to original
  report original model

If in-place scaled:
  report carefully; names/components may be scaled versions
```

### 19.21.5 Preprocessing

```text id="lg79re"
Aggregated/eliminated/transformed variables may need update hooks.
Dual/reduced-cost interpretation may refer to transformed model rows/columns.
Always report transformation chain.
```

`VariableAggregator` exposes `update_variables(model)` to update variables replaced by aggregate variables, and its docs explicitly flag reduced-cost behavior as a TODO; this is a warning that dual/reduced-cost interpretation after preprocessing transformations can be nontrivial. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

## 19.23 Deployment advisory

```text id="mg8q1g"
[ ] Record every transformation name, mode, and options.
[ ] Use apply_to for one-way low-memory workflows.
[ ] Use create_using when original model must remain available.
[ ] For GDP Big-M, require bounded variables or explicit Big-M values.
[ ] For GDP hull, require bounds on all variables in disjuncts.
[ ] For DAE, discretize before solver export.
[ ] Avoid building ContinuousSet-dependent sums before discretization if new points will be added.
[ ] For network models, call network.expand_arcs before solve.
[ ] For scaling, use scaling_factor suffix and prefer create_using + propagate_solution for clean reporting.
[ ] For preprocessing, test transformed solution equivalence and reporting implications.
[ ] Treat generated variables/constraints as formulation artifacts.
[ ] Do not assume dual/reduced-cost economics map to original high-level constructs.
[ ] Validate transformation chain in CI with before/after stats and solver smoke tests.
```

---

## 19.24 Anti-pattern table

| Anti-pattern                                                             | Failure mode                                                      | Replacement                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| solve GDP without reformulation/GDPopt                                   | solver cannot consume disjunctions                                | `gdp.bigm`, `gdp.hull`, or GDPopt                          |
| arbitrary huge Big-M                                                     | weak relaxation / numerical failure                               | bounded variables + data-derived M                         |
| hull with unbounded disjunct variables                                   | transformation error                                              | finite lower/upper bounds                                  |
| manually call `core.logical_to_linear` before GDP reformulation by habit | mathematically/algorithmically unnecessary in normal GDP workflow | pass mixed logical/algebraic model to reformulation/GDPopt |
| solve DAE before discretization                                          | solver cannot handle `DerivativeVar`/`Integral`                   | `dae.finite_difference` or `dae.collocation`               |
| sum over `ContinuousSet` before discretization adds points               | expression misses later grid points                               | build grid-dependent expressions after discretization      |
| forget `network.expand_arcs`                                             | solver misses port connection equations                           | apply network transform                                    |
| in-place scaling then report as original units                           | wrong interpretation                                              | scaled clone + `propagate_solution`                        |
| assume transformed duals equal original economic duals                   | invalid analysis                                                  | report transformed duals separately or derive mapping      |
| clone huge model for every transform variant                             | memory blowup                                                     | in-place transforms or smaller benchmarks                  |
| disable preprocessing validation                                         | silent model change                                               | before/after stats + equivalence tests                     |

---

## 19.25 Agent-ready production template

```python id="epwp2u"
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field, asdict
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any
import json

import pyomo.environ as pyo


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TransformSpec:
    name: str
    mode: str = "apply_to"
    options: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TransformRun:
    steps: list[dict]


def model_stats(m: pyo.Block) -> dict:
    vars_ = list(m.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True))
    cons = list(m.component_data_objects(pyo.Constraint, active=True, descend_into=True))
    objs = list(m.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=True, descend_into=True))

    return {
        "n_vars": len(vars_),
        "n_binary": sum(v.is_binary() for v in vars_),
        "n_integer": sum(v.is_integer() for v in vars_),
        "n_continuous": sum(v.is_continuous() for v in vars_),
        "n_constraints": len(cons),
        "n_objectives": len(objs),
    }


def stringify_options(options: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, str]:
    return {k: str(v) for k, v in options.items()}


def apply_transform_chain(model: pyo.ConcreteModel, specs: list[TransformSpec]):
    current = model
    steps = []
    propagation_hooks = []

    for spec in specs:
        xfrm = pyo.TransformationFactory(spec.name)
        if xfrm is None:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Transformation unavailable: {spec.name}")

        before = model_stats(current)

        if spec.mode == "apply_to":
            xfrm.apply_to(current, **spec.options)
            after_model = current
        elif spec.mode == "create_using":
            after_model = xfrm.create_using(current, **spec.options)
            propagation_hooks.append((spec.name, xfrm, after_model, current))
            current = after_model
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"invalid transform mode: {spec.mode}")

        after = model_stats(current)

        steps.append({
            "name": spec.name,
            "mode": spec.mode,
            "options": stringify_options(spec.options),
            "before": before,
            "after": after,
        })

    return current, TransformRun(steps=steps), propagation_hooks


def write_transform_manifest(path: Path, run: TransformRun) -> None:
    path.write_text(json.dumps(asdict(run), indent=2, sort_keys=True))


def require_bounded_vars(model: pyo.Block, vars_iter=None, label="model") -> None:
    if vars_iter is None:
        vars_iter = model.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True)

    missing = [
        v.name
        for v in vars_iter
        if v.lb is None or v.ub is None
    ]

    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"{label} has variables missing bounds: {missing[:20]}")


def transform_gdp_bigm(model: pyo.ConcreteModel, bigM=None):
    options = {}
    if bigM is not None:
        options["bigM"] = bigM
    pyo.TransformationFactory("gdp.bigm").apply_to(model, **options)
    return model


def transform_gdp_hull(model: pyo.ConcreteModel):
    require_bounded_vars(model, label="GDP hull candidate")
    pyo.TransformationFactory("gdp.hull").apply_to(model)
    return model


def transform_dae_finite_difference(model, contset, nfe=20, scheme="BACKWARD"):
    pyo.TransformationFactory("dae.finite_difference").apply_to(
        model,
        wrt=contset,
        nfe=nfe,
        scheme=scheme,
    )
    return model


def transform_dae_collocation(model, contset, nfe=20, ncp=3, scheme="LAGRANGE-RADAU"):
    pyo.TransformationFactory("dae.collocation").apply_to(
        model,
        wrt=contset,
        nfe=nfe,
        ncp=ncp,
        scheme=scheme,
    )
    return model


def expand_network_arcs(model):
    pyo.TransformationFactory("network.expand_arcs").apply_to(model)
    return model


def scale_clone(model):
    xfrm = pyo.TransformationFactory("core.scale_model")
    scaled = xfrm.create_using(model)
    return scaled, xfrm


def solve_checked(model, solver_name="highs", options=None):
    from pyomo.opt import SolverStatus, TerminationCondition

    opt = pyo.SolverFactory(solver_name)
    if opt is None or not opt.available(exception_flag=False):
        raise RuntimeError(f"solver unavailable: {solver_name}")

    results = opt.solve(model, options=options or {}, load_solutions=False)

    if (
        results.solver.status == SolverStatus.ok
        and results.solver.termination_condition == TerminationCondition.optimal
    ):
        model.solutions.load_from(results)
        return results

    raise RuntimeError(
        f"solve failed: status={results.solver.status}, "
        f"termination={results.solver.termination_condition}"
    )


def solve_scaled_and_propagate(original, solver_name="ipopt"):
    scaled, xfrm = scale_clone(original)
    results = solve_checked(scaled, solver_name=solver_name)
    xfrm.propagate_solution(scaled, original)
    return results, scaled
```

[ ] Use pyo.TransformationFactory("name").
[ ] Use apply_to(model) for in-place transformation.
[ ] Use create_using(model) for transformed copy.
[ ] Avoid deprecated apply(model).

[ ] Use scaling_factor suffix for core.scale_model.
[ ] Prefer scale create_using + propagate_solution for clean reporting.
[ ] Treat generated variables/constraints as formulation artifacts.
[ ] Do not assume transformed duals map to original economics.

# 20) Generalized Disjunctive Programming: `pyomo.gdp` — Pyomo deep dive

Style target: uploaded advanced technical-doc plan. 

Pyomo.GDP = Pyomo’s modeling layer for **logic-based algebraic optimization**: Boolean decisions, logical propositions, disjunctive alternatives, and reformulation/direct-solver workflows. GDP bridges propositional logic and algebraic constraints; `Disjunct` groups relational expressions under a Boolean indicator, while `Disjunction` expresses logical-OR relationships between those groups. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

---

## 20.0 Mental model

```text id="c4dzvk"
GDP model:
  continuous/integer algebraic model
  + Boolean decisions
  + logical propositions over Boolean decisions
  + disjunctive alternatives containing algebraic constraints

Disjunct:
  conditional block of constraints
  "if indicator_var is True, these constraints must hold"

Disjunction:
  logical OR over Disjuncts
  default semantics: exactly one disjunct active

LogicalConstraint:
  Boolean proposition over BooleanVar / Disjunct.indicator_var

Solve path:
  GDP model
    -> direct GDP solver, e.g. GDPopt
    OR
    -> reformulate to MILP/MINLP via Big-M / hull / related transformations
    -> solve with standard solver
```

Core warning:

```text id="s0ttbv"
BooleanVar is not numeric.
Do not write algebraic expressions like x == 3 * Y.
Use disjunctions, logical constraints, or associated binary variables only after transformation.
```

Pyomo’s GDP concepts page explicitly says Boolean variables are not intended to participate in algebraic expressions; instead of writing numeric algebra with a Boolean, the GDP formulation should express the alternative logic through disjunctions. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

---

## 20.1 Imports

### 20.1.1 Canonical GDP imports

```python id="4m6ycc"
import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.gdp import Disjunct, Disjunction
```

### 20.1.2 Logical components

```python id="qsewai"
m.Y = pyo.BooleanVar(m.I)
m.logic = pyo.LogicalConstraint(expr=pyo.exactly(1, m.Y))
```

### 20.1.3 Boolean operators

```python id="rh0bvp"
expr = m.Y[1].implies(m.Y[2] & ~m.Y[3])
expr = pyo.atleast(2, m.Y)
expr = pyo.atmost(1, m.Y[1], m.Y[2], m.Y[3])
expr = pyo.exactly(1, m.Y)
```

Pyomo’s current GDP docs show `BooleanVar`, `LogicalConstraint`, Boolean operators such as `~`, `&`, `|`, `^`, `.implies(...)`, and CP-style predicates `exactly`, `atmost`, and `atleast`. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

---

## 20.2 Core component taxonomy

| Component              | Role                                               | Example                                                  |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `BooleanVar`           | Boolean decision variable                          | `m.Y = pyo.BooleanVar(m.I)`                              |
| `LogicalConstraint`    | proposition over Boolean expressions               | `m.lc = pyo.LogicalConstraint(expr=pyo.atleast(2, m.Y))` |
| `Disjunct`             | conditional constraint block                       | `m.d1 = Disjunct()`                                      |
| `Disjunction`          | OR/XOR collection of disjuncts                     | `m.djn = Disjunction(expr=[m.d1, m.d2])`                 |
| `indicator_var`        | Boolean indicator on each disjunct                 | `m.d1.indicator_var`                                     |
| `binary_indicator_var` | associated binary for reformulated algebraic model | `m.d1.binary_indicator_var`                              |

Historically, `Disjunct.indicator_var` was binary; since Pyomo 6.0 it is a mathematically correct `BooleanVar`, with the associated binary variable available through `binary_indicator_var`. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

---

## 20.3 `Disjunct`: conditional algebraic block

### 20.3.1 Scalar explicit disjuncts

```python id="u8i4eh"
m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

m.x = pyo.Var(bounds=(0, 10))
m.y = pyo.Var(bounds=(0, 10))

m.low_mode = Disjunct()
m.low_mode.x_limit = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x <= 3)
m.low_mode.y_def = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.y == 2 * m.x)

m.high_mode = Disjunct()
m.high_mode.x_limit = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= 5)
m.high_mode.y_def = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.y == m.x + 7)

m.mode_choice = Disjunction(expr=[m.low_mode, m.high_mode])
```

Semantics:

```text id="symkd1"
if low_mode.indicator_var == True:
  x <= 3
  y == 2*x

if high_mode.indicator_var == True:
  x >= 5
  y == x + 7

mode_choice default:
  exactly one of low_mode/high_mode is active
```

Pyomo.GDP docs describe disjuncts as groupings of algebraic constraints summarized by a Boolean indicator: if the indicator is true, the constraints must be satisfied; if false, those constraints are ignored, and false does not imply violation. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

### 20.3.2 Indexed disjuncts with rule

```python id="r1zud2"
m.K = pyo.Set(initialize=["small", "medium", "large"])
m.x = pyo.Var(bounds=(0, 100))

def size_disjunct_rule(d, k):
    m = d.model()

    if k == "small":
        d.lb = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= 0)
        d.ub = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x <= 10)
    elif k == "medium":
        d.lb = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= 10)
        d.ub = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x <= 50)
    elif k == "large":
        d.lb = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= 50)
        d.ub = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x <= 100)
    else:
        raise KeyError(k)

m.size_disjunct = Disjunct(m.K, rule=size_disjunct_rule)
m.size_choice = Disjunction(expr=[m.size_disjunct[k] for k in m.K])
```

Rule signature:

```text id="i6npgo"
Disjunct(m.K, rule=f):
  f(disjunct_data, k)
```

### 20.3.3 Disjunct as submodel

```python id="fof2np"
def build_unit_on_disjunct(d, unit):
    m = d.model()
    d.capacity = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.output[unit] <= m.max_cap[unit])
    d.min_load = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.output[unit] >= m.min_cap[unit])

m.on = Disjunct(m.UNITS, rule=build_unit_on_disjunct)
```

Best practice:

```text id="kgx0rc"
Disjuncts should contain local conditional constraints.
Global constraints should remain outside disjuncts unless truly conditional.
```

---

## 20.4 `Disjunction`: OR/XOR over disjuncts

### 20.4.1 Default XOR disjunction

```python id="ba28gh"
m.choice = Disjunction(expr=[m.low_mode, m.high_mode])
```

Default semantics:

```text id="l8iz2e"
exactly one disjunct indicator_var is True
```

Pyomo.GDP docs state that `Disjunction` objects enforce an implicit “exactly one” relationship by default, generalizing exclusive-OR: exactly one `Disjunct` indicator variable should be `True`. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 20.4.2 Inclusive OR disjunction

```python id="tg3uic"
m.choice = Disjunction(expr=[m.a, m.b, m.c], xor=False)
```

Semantics:

```text id="fdlwq2"
at least one disjunct active
multiple disjuncts may be active
```

### 20.4.3 Indexed disjunctions

```python id="f23zqs"
m.T = pyo.RangeSet(1, 24)
m.mode = pyo.Set(initialize=["off", "low", "high"])

m.d = Disjunct(m.T, m.mode)

def off_rule(d, t):
    m = d.model()
    d.output_zero = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.output[t] == 0)

def low_rule(d, t):
    m = d.model()
    d.lb = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.output[t] >= m.low_min)
    d.ub = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.output[t] <= m.low_max)

def high_rule(d, t):
    m = d.model()
    d.lb = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.output[t] >= m.high_min)
    d.ub = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.output[t] <= m.high_max)

for t in m.T:
    off_rule(m.d[t, "off"], t)
    low_rule(m.d[t, "low"], t)
    high_rule(m.d[t, "high"], t)

def mode_disjunction_rule(m, t):
    return [m.d[t, k] for k in m.mode]

m.mode_choice = Disjunction(m.T, rule=mode_disjunction_rule)
```

### 20.4.4 Compact implicit disjunct syntax

```python id="fvx7ph"
m.c = Disjunction(expr=[
    [m.x == 0],
    [m.y == 0],
])
```

Pyomo’s GDP modeling docs show compact syntax where `Disjunction(expr=[...])` receives lists of constraint expressions; the outer list defines disjuncts, and inner lists define the constraints within each disjunct. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

Agent recommendation:

```text id="a37hm4"
Use explicit named Disjuncts in production.
Use compact implicit Disjunction syntax only for small examples/tests.
```

---

## 20.5 `BooleanVar`

### 20.5.1 Scalar Boolean variable

```python id="avbqtq"
m.Y = pyo.BooleanVar()
```

### 20.5.2 Indexed Boolean variable

```python id="4djc6d"
m.I = pyo.RangeSet(4)
m.Y = pyo.BooleanVar(m.I)
```

### 20.5.3 Fixing Boolean values

```python id="nfntfe"
m.Y[1].fix(True)
m.Y[2].fix(False)
m.Y[2].unfix()
```

### 20.5.4 Boolean value after solve

```python id="fag2lb"
val = pyo.value(m.Y[1])
```

Before transformation/solve, Boolean values may be `None`; after solving a transformed model, associated binary values may need to be propagated back to Boolean variables depending on the transformation/solver path. Pyomo’s logical-to-linear docs expose `update_boolean_vars_from_binary(model, integer_tolerance=...)` for this purpose. ([Pyomo Documentation][3])

## 20.6 `LogicalConstraint`

### 20.6.1 Scalar logical constraint

```python id="0y0yau"
m.Y = pyo.BooleanVar([1, 2, 3, 4])

m.logic = pyo.LogicalConstraint(
    expr=m.Y[1].implies(m.Y[2] & m.Y[3]) | m.Y[4]
)
```

Pyomo docs show `LogicalConstraint` as the Boolean analogue of algebraic `Constraint`. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 20.6.2 Indexed logical constraint

```python id="y439ic"
m.I = pyo.RangeSet(5)
m.Y = pyo.BooleanVar(m.I)

def monotone_logic_rule(m, i):
    if i == m.I.last():
        return pyo.Constraint.Skip
    return m.Y[i + 1].implies(m.Y[i])

m.monotone = pyo.LogicalConstraint(m.I, rule=monotone_logic_rule)
```

Pyomo’s GDP docs show indexed logical constraints with a rule returning implication expressions and `Constraint.Skip` for omitted indices. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 20.6.3 Logical proposition operators

```python id="7bibfe"
m.l1 = pyo.LogicalConstraint(expr=~m.Y[1])
m.l2 = pyo.LogicalConstraint(expr=m.Y[1] & m.Y[2])
m.l3 = pyo.LogicalConstraint(expr=m.Y[1] | m.Y[2])
m.l4 = pyo.LogicalConstraint(expr=m.Y[1] ^ m.Y[2])
m.l5 = pyo.LogicalConstraint(expr=m.Y[1].implies(m.Y[2]))
m.l6 = pyo.LogicalConstraint(expr=m.Y[1].equivalent_to(m.Y[2]))
```

Supported logical operators in Pyomo.GDP include negation, conjunction, disjunction, exclusive OR, implication, and equivalence, with both operator/method/function forms documented. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 20.6.4 CP-style logical predicates

```python id="z034qq"
m.at_least_two = pyo.LogicalConstraint(expr=pyo.atleast(2, m.Y))
m.at_most_one = pyo.LogicalConstraint(expr=pyo.atmost(1, m.Y))
m.exactly_one = pyo.LogicalConstraint(expr=pyo.exactly(1, m.Y))
```

`exactly`, `atmost`, and `atleast` enforce that exactly, at most, or at least `N` Boolean arguments are true. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

---

## 20.7 Logical propositions with disjunct indicators

### 20.7.1 Indicator implication

```python id="4o5zzn"
m.d1 = Disjunct()
m.d2 = Disjunct()
m.d3 = Disjunct()

m.d1.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= 1)
m.d2.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= 2)
m.d3.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= 3)

m.choice = Disjunction(expr=[m.d1, m.d2, m.d3])

m.logic = pyo.LogicalConstraint(
    expr=m.d1.indicator_var.implies(m.d3.indicator_var)
)
```

Pyomo docs show `Disjunct.indicator_var` can be used directly in logical propositions, including implications between disjunct indicators. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 20.7.2 Exactly one across disjunct indicators

```python id="20k07f"
m.exactly_one = pyo.LogicalConstraint(
    expr=pyo.exactly(1, [m.d1.indicator_var, m.d2.indicator_var, m.d3.indicator_var])
)
```

Usually redundant for default `Disjunction`, but useful for GDPopt LD-SDA workflows or separately modeled Boolean controls.

---

## 20.8 Modeling if/then/else decisions as disjunctions

### 20.8.1 If/else on algebraic constraints

Mathematical rule:

```text id="dcjqdl"
if mode == A:
  x >= 2
  cost == 5*x
else:
  x <= 1
  cost == 3*x + 10
```

GDP model:

```python id="epz9g0"
m = pyo.ConcreteModel()
m.x = pyo.Var(bounds=(0, 10))
m.cost = pyo.Var(bounds=(0, 100))

m.mode_a = Disjunct()
m.mode_a.x_lb = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= 2)
m.mode_a.cost_def = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.cost == 5 * m.x)

m.mode_b = Disjunct()
m.mode_b.x_ub = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x <= 1)
m.mode_b.cost_def = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.cost == 3 * m.x + 10)

m.mode = Disjunction(expr=[m.mode_a, m.mode_b])
m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.cost)
```

### 20.8.2 Semi-continuous variable as GDP

```python id="cyeoab"
m.x = pyo.Var(bounds=(0, 100))

m.off = Disjunct()
m.off.zero = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x == 0)

m.on = Disjunct()
m.on.lb = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= 10)
m.on.ub = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x <= 100)

m.on_or_off = Disjunction(expr=[m.off, m.on])
```

Alternative MIP formulation:

```python id="cnh111"
m.y = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.Binary)
m.x = pyo.Var(bounds=(0, 100))

m.lb = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= 10 * m.y)
m.ub = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x <= 100 * m.y)
```

GDP value:

```text id="223t3g"
clearer logical structure
can switch between big-M/hull/GDPopt
avoids manually coding each binary implication
```

### 20.8.3 Mutually exclusive process modes

```python id="idk9z4"
m.MODES = pyo.Set(initialize=["unit1", "unit2"])

m.unit = Disjunct(m.MODES)

m.unit["unit1"].io = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.out1 == pyo.exp(m.in1) - 1)
m.unit["unit1"].off2 = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.out2 == 0)

m.unit["unit2"].io = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.out2 == pyo.exp(m.in2 / 1.2) - 1)
m.unit["unit2"].off1 = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.out1 == 0)

m.select_unit = Disjunction(expr=[m.unit[k] for k in m.MODES])
```

Pyomo’s GDP examples use process-unit selection as a canonical disjunction: each disjunct holds the active unit’s input/output relation and zero-flow constraints for absent units. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

---

## 20.9 XOR vs OR semantics

### 20.9.1 Default XOR

```python id="7q2obc"
m.djn = Disjunction(expr=[m.d1, m.d2, m.d3])
```

Meaning:

```text id="n5gczx"
exactly one active disjunct
```

### 20.9.2 Inclusive OR

```python id="o0crgp"
m.djn = Disjunction(expr=[m.d1, m.d2, m.d3], xor=False)
```

Meaning:

```text id="47j2lp"
at least one active disjunct
possibly multiple active disjuncts
```

### 20.9.3 Explicit exactly/atleast/atmost with indicator vars

```python id="bw0f57"
indicators = [m.d[k].indicator_var for k in m.K]

m.exactly_one = pyo.LogicalConstraint(expr=pyo.exactly(1, indicators))
m.at_least_two = pyo.LogicalConstraint(expr=pyo.atleast(2, indicators))
m.at_most_one = pyo.LogicalConstraint(expr=pyo.atmost(1, indicators))
```

### 20.9.4 Decision rule

```text id="fovul0"
Use default Disjunction XOR:
  mutually exclusive alternatives
  if/else
  single mode selection

Use xor=False or LogicalConstraint(atleast/atmost/exactly):
  overlapping conditions
  coverage logic
  custom cardinality logic
  multiple simultaneous active disjuncts
```

---

## 20.10 Reformulation workflows

### 20.10.1 Big-M reformulation

```python id="d2dpm8"
pyo.TransformationFactory("gdp.bigm").apply_to(m)
results = pyo.SolverFactory("highs").solve(m)
```

Big-M creates a smaller transformed model and avoids extra variables, but has a looser continuous relaxation; Pyomo can estimate reasonably tight M values when variables are bounded, but otherwise M values must be supplied through a `BigM` suffix or `bigM` argument, and Pyomo raises `GDP_Error` for missing M values. ([Pyomo Documentation][3])

### 20.10.2 Big-M via suffix

```python id="i2c6b4"
m.BigM = pyo.Suffix(direction=pyo.Suffix.LOCAL)

m.BigM[m.on.lb] = 100.0
m.BigM[m.on.ub] = 100.0
m.BigM[None] = 1_000.0

pyo.TransformationFactory("gdp.bigm").apply_to(m)
```

### 20.10.3 Big-M via argument

```python id="jmwxss"
pyo.TransformationFactory("gdp.bigm").apply_to(
    m,
    bigM=1_000.0,
)
```

Component-specific:

```python id="g1cz11"
M = {
    None: 1_000.0,
    m.on.lb: 90.0,
    m.on.ub: 100.0,
}

pyo.TransformationFactory("gdp.bigm").apply_to(m, bigM=M)
```

### 20.10.4 Multiple Big-M

```python id="s2tj8m"
mbigm = pyo.TransformationFactory("gdp.mbigm")
mbigm.apply_to(m)

M_values = mbigm.get_all_M_values(m)
```

Reuse:

```python id="axizzz"
pyo.TransformationFactory("gdp.mbigm").apply_to(m2, bigM=M_values)
```

The multiple Big-M transformation can solve continuous subproblems to compute M values and export them as a dictionary for reuse; it currently ignores `BigM` suffixes and uses the `bigM` argument for supplied values. ([Pyomo Documentation][3])

### 20.10.5 Hull reformulation

```python id="q9zgoe"
pyo.TransformationFactory("gdp.hull").apply_to(m)
```

Hull introduces disaggregated variables and constraints in a lifted space; all variables appearing in disjuncts need upper and lower bounds, and the reformulation is exact at solution points even for nonconvex GDPs, although the resulting MINLP may remain nonconvex. ([Pyomo Documentation][3])

### 20.10.6 Cutting-plane hybrid

```python id="c3gf1v"
pyo.TransformationFactory("gdp.cuttingplane").apply_to(m)
```

The cutting-plane GDP transformation is currently described as experimental for linear GDP models; it augments Big-M with cutting planes generated from the hull model, aiming for a model smaller than hull but with a stronger relaxation than Big-M. ([Pyomo Documentation][3])

---

## 20.11 Logical transformations

### 20.11.1 Recommended normal practice

```text id="5nlfnj"
For mixed logical/algebraic GDP models:
  pass the entire model directly to gdp.bigm, gdp.hull, gdp.mbigm, gdp.cuttingplane, or GDPopt.
```

Pyomo’s solving docs say the current recommended practice is to pass the entire mixed logical/algebraic model directly to GDP MI(N)LP reformulations or GDPopt, rather than explicitly converting logical propositions first. ([Pyomo Documentation][3])

### 20.11.2 CNF logical-to-linear

```python id="cgq3jh"
pyo.TransformationFactory("core.logical_to_linear").apply_to(m)
```

This transformation uses SymPy to generate conjunctive normal form and creates a constraint list with a unique name starting with `logic_to_linear`; Boolean variables get associated binary counterparts accessible through `get_associated_binary()`. ([Pyomo Documentation][3])

Access binary:

```python id="thrqib"
binary_y = m.Y[1].get_associated_binary()
```

Update Booleans after solve:

```python id="b6fpyv"
from pyomo.core.plugins.transform.logical_to_linear import update_boolean_vars_from_binary

update_boolean_vars_from_binary(m, integer_tolerance=1e-5)
```

### 20.11.3 Factorable logical-to-disjunctive

```python id="8rkjcm"
pyo.TransformationFactory("contrib.logical_to_disjunctive").apply_to(m)
```

`contrib.logical_to_disjunctive` avoids SymPy, traverses each logical expression once, creates additional Boolean variables for operators, and converts simple logical constraints to either MIP or GDP form; Pyomo docs say it is significantly faster than `core.logical_to_linear` but may create a larger model that MIP presolve often reduces. ([Pyomo Documentation][3])

---

## 20.12 Direct GDP solving with GDPopt

### 20.12.1 Generic GDPopt

```python id="xokbr7"
results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt").solve(
    m,
    algorithm="LOA",
    mip_solver="highs",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    tee=True,
)
```

### 20.12.2 Named GDPopt solvers

```python id="ev3955"
results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt.loa").solve(m, mip_solver="highs", nlp_solver="ipopt")
results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt.gloa").solve(m, mip_solver="highs", nlp_solver="ipopt")
results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt.ric").solve(m, mip_solver="highs", nlp_solver="ipopt")
results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt.lbb").solve(m)
results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt.ldsda").solve(m, starting_point=[1, 1])
```

Pyomo includes GDPopt as a contributed direct GDP solver; current GDPopt docs list logic-based outer approximation, global LOA, relaxation with integer cuts, logic-based branch-and-bound, and LD-SDA solver classes. ([Pyomo Documentation][4])

### 20.12.3 LD-SDA XOR requirement

```python id="im5l59"
m.Y_limit = pyo.LogicalConstraint(
    expr=pyo.exactly(1, [m.d[i].indicator_var for i in m.I])
)

results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt.ldsda").solve(
    m,
    starting_point=[1],
    logical_constraint_list=[m.Y_limit],
    direction_norm="Linf",
)
```

GDPopt LD-SDA requires exclusive-OR logic ensuring exactly one disjunct is active in each disjunction; the current implementation requires an explicit `LogicalConstraint` for this condition and a starting point for discrete variables. ([Pyomo Documentation][4])

---

## 20.13 Reformulation vs direct GDP solving

| Path           | Syntax                       | Output model                   | Solver need                      | Use when                                                |
| -------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Big-M          | `gdp.bigm`                   | MILP/MINLP                     | standard MILP/MINLP solver       | smaller model, bounded variables, acceptable relaxation |
| Multiple Big-M | `gdp.mbigm`                  | MILP/MINLP                     | subproblem solves + final solver | reusable/tighter M calculation                          |
| Hull           | `gdp.hull`                   | MILP/MINLP with disaggregation | standard MILP/MINLP solver       | stronger relaxation worth larger model                  |
| Cutting plane  | `gdp.cuttingplane`           | strengthened Big-M             | MILP solver; linear GDP          | experimental hybrid                                     |
| GDPopt         | `SolverFactory("gdpopt...")` | direct algorithmic solve       | MIP/NLP subsolvers               | logic-based decomposition desired                       |

Production decision:

```text id="59wrtk"
Start:
  gdp.bigm with tight bounds/M values
Benchmark:
  gdp.hull
Try:
  gdp.mbigm if M values dominate performance
Use:
  GDPopt when nonlinear GDP/decomposition behavior is advantageous
Avoid:
  blind arbitrary Big-M
```

---

## 20.14 Best practices for Big-M values

### 20.14.1 Bound every variable in disjuncts

```python id="i6y8k3"
m.x = pyo.Var(bounds=(0, 100))
m.y = pyo.Var(bounds=(-10, 10))
```

Big-M automatic estimation relies on variable bounds; hull also requires bounds for variables appearing in disjuncts. ([Pyomo Documentation][3])

### 20.14.2 Data-derived M

```python id="io4b2t"
def derive_M_for_constraint(max_x, min_x, rhs):
    return max(abs(max_x - rhs), abs(min_x - rhs))
```

Example:

```python id="y2ebey"
m.BigM = pyo.Suffix(direction=pyo.Suffix.LOCAL)
m.BigM[m.on.ub] = pyo.value(m.x.ub) - pyo.value(m.limit)
```

### 20.14.3 Component-specific M

```python id="j2hxg3"
M = {
    m.off.zero: 100.0,
    m.on.lb: 10.0,
    m.on.ub: 100.0,
}

pyo.TransformationFactory("gdp.bigm").apply_to(m, bigM=M)
```

### 20.14.4 M validation audit

```python id="v9jmv8"
def bounded_vars_in_disjuncts(m):
    missing = []
    for d in m.component_data_objects(Disjunct, active=True, descend_into=True):
        for v in d.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True):
            if v.lb is None or v.ub is None:
                missing.append((d.name, v.name))
    return missing
```

### 20.14.5 Big-M policy

```text id="wupzwd"
[ ] M values derived from variable/constraint bounds.
[ ] No global 1e9 unless formally justified.
[ ] M values recorded in manifest.
[ ] Bounds and M values unit-tested.
[ ] Big-M and hull objective values compared on small cases.
[ ] LP relaxation quality inspected if MILP performance is poor.
```

## 20.15 Bound tightening before transformation

### 20.15.1 Static bound tightening

```python id="do1696"
m.x.setlb(max(m.x.lb, derived_lb))
m.x.setub(min(m.x.ub, derived_ub))
```

### 20.15.2 Param-derived bounds

```python id="09leja"
m.output = pyo.Var(
    m.UNITS,
    bounds=lambda m, u: (0, m.max_output[u]),
)
```

### 20.15.3 Optional OBBT sketch

```python id="ml611g"
def tighten_var_bound_by_solve(m, v, solver_name="highs"):
    original_obj = next(m.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=True))
    original_obj.deactivate()

    m._tmp_bound_obj = pyo.Objective(expr=v, sense=pyo.minimize)
    solve_checked(m, solver_name)
    lb = pyo.value(v)

    m._tmp_bound_obj.sense = pyo.maximize
    solve_checked(m, solver_name)
    ub = pyo.value(v)

    m._tmp_bound_obj.deactivate()
    original_obj.activate()

    v.setlb(max(v.lb if v.lb is not None else lb, lb))
    v.setub(min(v.ub if v.ub is not None else ub, ub))
```

Use OBBT carefully; transformation and objective-state management must be tested.

## 20.16 GDP result interpretation

### 20.16.1 Indicator values

```python id="kpseci"
for d in m.component_data_objects(Disjunct, descend_into=True):
    print(d.name, pyo.value(d.indicator_var, exception=False))
```

### 20.16.2 Associated binary indicator

```python id="ql1wj4"
b = m.d1.binary_indicator_var
print(pyo.value(b, exception=False))
```

### 20.16.3 Boolean update after logical-to-linear

```python id="cvm2wl"
from pyomo.core.plugins.transform.logical_to_linear import update_boolean_vars_from_binary

update_boolean_vars_from_binary(m, integer_tolerance=1e-5)
```

### 20.16.4 Selected disjuncts report

```python id="xxuxbt"
def selected_disjuncts(m, tol=1e-6):
    selected = []
    for d in m.component_data_objects(Disjunct, active=None, descend_into=True):
        val = pyo.value(d.indicator_var, exception=False)
        if val is True or (isinstance(val, (int, float)) and val >= 1 - tol):
            selected.append(d.name)
    return selected
```

### 20.16.5 Reporting policy

```text id="iem07s"
Report:
  original business variables
  selected disjunct names
  Boolean decisions
  transformation used
  solver status/termination

Avoid reporting:
  generated reformulation auxiliaries as business decisions
  transformed duals as original disjunctive economics without explicit mapping
```

## 20.17 Common GDP modeling patterns

### 20.17.1 Either-or bound

```python id="q7xx99"
m.x = pyo.Var(bounds=(0, 10))

m.low = Disjunct()
m.low.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x <= 2)

m.high = Disjunct()
m.high.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= 8)

m.either_or = Disjunction(expr=[m.low, m.high])
```

### 20.17.2 Choose exactly one technology

```python id="xmh1oe"
m.TECH = pyo.Set(initialize=["solar", "wind", "gas"])

m.use = Disjunct(m.TECH)

def tech_rule(d, tech):
    m = d.model()
    d.min_cap = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.capacity[tech] >= m.min_cap[tech])
    d.max_cap = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.capacity[tech] <= m.max_cap[tech])

for tech in m.TECH:
    tech_rule(m.use[tech], tech)

m.choose_tech = Disjunction(expr=[m.use[t] for t in m.TECH])
```

### 20.17.3 Optional activity

```python id="npfcbr"
m.x = pyo.Var(bounds=(0, 100))

m.off = Disjunct()
m.off.zero = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x == 0)

m.on = Disjunct()
m.on.min = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= 20)
m.on.max = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x <= 100)

m.optional = Disjunction(expr=[m.off, m.on])
```

### 20.17.4 Logical precedence

```python id="7kmpcd"
m.open = pyo.BooleanVar(m.F)
m.install = pyo.BooleanVar(m.F)

m.precedence = pyo.LogicalConstraint(
    m.F,
    rule=lambda m, f: m.install[f].implies(m.open[f]),
)
```

### 20.17.5 At most K selections

```python id="4xae0x"
m.select = pyo.BooleanVar(m.I)
m.limit = pyo.LogicalConstraint(expr=pyo.atmost(3, m.select))
```

## 20.18 Anti-patterns

| Anti-pattern                                                  | Failure mode                          | Replacement                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `m.x == 3 * m.Y` with BooleanVar                              | Boolean used as numeric               | disjunction or binary `Var` if pure MILP        |
| unbounded variables inside Big-M GDP                          | missing M / weak M                    | finite bounds or explicit M                     |
| arbitrary `M = 1e9`                                           | weak relaxation / numerical failure   | data-derived tight M                            |
| hull without bounds                                           | transformation error                  | set finite lb/ub for disjunct vars              |
| multiple overlapping disjunctions with accidental default XOR | infeasible/overrestricted logic       | use `xor=False` or explicit logical constraints |
| logical-to-linear before every GDP solve                      | unnecessary/incorrect normal workflow | pass full GDP to reformulation/GDPopt           |
| compact disjunction syntax in production                      | hard-to-debug generated names         | explicit named Disjuncts                        |
| read Boolean values before solve                              | `None`                                | solve and update Booleans if needed             |
| report auxiliary reformulation variables as decisions         | misleading output                     | report original variables/disjuncts             |
| use GDP for simple linear binary implication without benefit  | overhead                              | direct MILP if clearer and static               |

## 20.20 Deployment advisory

```text id="il04lp"
[ ] Use explicit named Disjuncts for production models.
[ ] Use default Disjunction only when exactly-one semantics are intended.
[ ] Use xor=False or LogicalConstraint for inclusive/custom OR logic.
[ ] Keep BooleanVar out of algebraic numeric expressions.
[ ] Use LogicalConstraint for Boolean implications/cardinality rules.
[ ] Bound every variable appearing in disjuncts.
[ ] Prefer tight data-derived Big-M values.
[ ] Use BigM suffix or bigM argument when automatic M inference is insufficient.
[ ] Test gdp.bigm and gdp.hull on representative instances.
[ ] Record transformation and M-value policy in run manifests.
[ ] Use GDPopt only with documented subsolver configuration and termination handling.
[ ] Report selected disjuncts and original business variables, not generated auxiliaries.
[ ] Add bound audits, transformation smoke tests, and formulation-stat checks to CI.
```

## 20.21 Agent-ready production template

```python id="p2nrt7"
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.gdp import Disjunct, Disjunction
from pyomo.opt import SolverStatus, TerminationCondition


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GDPConfig:
    reformulation: str = "gdp.bigm"  # gdp.bigm | gdp.hull | gdp.mbigm | gdp.cuttingplane
    bigM: Any | None = None
    solver_name: str = "highs"
    solver_options: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    tee: bool = False


def build_optional_activity_model() -> pyo.ConcreteModel:
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel(name="gdp_optional_activity")

    m.x = pyo.Var(bounds=(0, 100))
    m.cost = pyo.Var(bounds=(0, 1000))

    m.off = Disjunct()
    m.off.zero_x = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x == 0)
    m.off.zero_cost = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.cost == 0)

    m.on = Disjunct()
    m.on.min_x = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= 20)
    m.on.max_x = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x <= 100)
    m.on.cost_def = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.cost == 5 * m.x + 10)

    m.activity = Disjunction(expr=[m.off, m.on])

    # Extra logical policy: if on, then a separate Boolean decision must be true.
    m.approved = pyo.BooleanVar()
    m.approval_logic = pyo.LogicalConstraint(
        expr=m.on.indicator_var.implies(m.approved)
    )

    m.demand = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= 30)
    m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.cost, sense=pyo.minimize)

    return m


def require_bounded_disjunct_vars(m: pyo.Block) -> None:
    missing = []
    for d in m.component_data_objects(Disjunct, active=True, descend_into=True):
        for v in d.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True):
            if v.lb is None or v.ub is None:
                missing.append((d.name, v.name))

    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"unbounded variables in disjuncts: {missing[:20]}")


def transform_gdp(m: pyo.ConcreteModel, cfg: GDPConfig):
    require_bounded_disjunct_vars(m)

    xfrm = pyo.TransformationFactory(cfg.reformulation)
    if xfrm is None:
        raise RuntimeError(f"unavailable transformation: {cfg.reformulation}")

    options = {}
    if cfg.bigM is not None and cfg.reformulation in {"gdp.bigm", "gdp.mbigm"}:
        options["bigM"] = cfg.bigM

    xfrm.apply_to(m, **options)
    return m


def solve_checked(m: pyo.ConcreteModel, cfg: GDPConfig):
    opt = pyo.SolverFactory(cfg.solver_name)

    if opt is None or not opt.available(exception_flag=False):
        raise RuntimeError(f"solver unavailable: {cfg.solver_name}")

    results = opt.solve(
        m,
        options=cfg.solver_options,
        tee=cfg.tee,
        load_solutions=False,
    )

    if (
        results.solver.status == SolverStatus.ok
        and results.solver.termination_condition == TerminationCondition.optimal
    ):
        m.solutions.load_from(results)
        return results

    raise RuntimeError(
        f"solve failed: status={results.solver.status}, "
        f"termination={results.solver.termination_condition}"
    )


def selected_disjuncts(m: pyo.Block, tol: float = 1e-6) -> list[str]:
    selected = []
    for d in m.component_data_objects(Disjunct, active=None, descend_into=True):
        val = pyo.value(d.indicator_var, exception=False)
        if val is True or (isinstance(val, (int, float)) and val >= 1 - tol):
            selected.append(d.name)
    return selected


def gdp_manifest(m: pyo.Block, cfg: GDPConfig, results) -> dict:
    vars_ = list(m.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True))
    cons = list(m.component_data_objects(pyo.Constraint, active=True, descend_into=True))

    return {
        "reformulation": cfg.reformulation,
        "solver_name": cfg.solver_name,
        "solver_status": str(results.solver.status),
        "termination_condition": str(results.solver.termination_condition),
        "n_variables": len(vars_),
        "n_binary_variables": sum(v.is_binary() for v in vars_),
        "n_constraints": len(cons),
        "selected_disjuncts": selected_disjuncts(m),
    }


def run():
    cfg = GDPConfig(
        reformulation="gdp.bigm",
        solver_name="highs",
        bigM=None,
        tee=True,
    )

    m = build_optional_activity_model()
    transform_gdp(m, cfg)
    results = solve_checked(m, cfg)

    return {
        "x": pyo.value(m.x),
        "cost": pyo.value(m.cost),
        "selected_disjuncts": selected_disjuncts(m),
        "manifest": gdp_manifest(m, cfg, results),
    }
```

## 20.22 Final checklist

```text id="lk8fol"
[ ] Import Disjunct and Disjunction from pyomo.gdp.
[ ] Use BooleanVar for logical decisions.
[ ] Use LogicalConstraint for Boolean relationships.
[ ] Use Disjunct for conditional algebraic constraint groups.
[ ] Use Disjunction for OR/XOR relationships between disjuncts.
[ ] Remember Disjunction defaults to exactly-one/XOR.
[ ] Use xor=False for inclusive OR where appropriate.
[ ] Use exactly/atleast/atmost for cardinality logic.
[ ] Use indicator_var in logical propositions.
[ ] Do not multiply/add BooleanVars in algebraic expressions.
[ ] Bound all variables appearing in disjuncts.
[ ] Use gdp.bigm for compact reformulation with tight M values.
[ ] Use gdp.hull for stronger relaxation with bounded variables.
[ ] Use gdp.mbigm to compute/reuse M values when appropriate.
[ ] Treat gdp.cuttingplane as experimental.
[ ] Pass full mixed logical/algebraic model directly to GDP reformulations/GDPopt in normal workflows.
[ ] Use update_boolean_vars_from_binary when Boolean values need propagation after logical-to-linear workflows.
[ ] Report selected disjuncts plus original variables.
[ ] Test transformation availability, bound sufficiency, and solve equivalence on small cases.
```

# 21) GDPopt logic-based solver — Pyomo deep dive

Style target: uploaded advanced technical-doc plan. 

GDPopt = Pyomo’s decomposition-based solver family for **nonlinear Generalized Disjunctive Programming** models. It solves GDP models directly with logic-based algorithms rather than first forcing the whole model into a monolithic MINLP reformulation. Its documented advantage is solving subproblems in a reduced space, including nonlinear constraints only for currently `True` logical blocks, which makes it most useful for nonlinear GDPs. Current Pyomo 6.10.0 docs list GDPopt algorithms: **LOA**, **GLOA**, **LBB**, and **LD-SDA**; the docs also document `RIC` as an algorithm-specific solver. ([pyomo.readthedocs.io][1])

---

## 21.0 Mental model

```text
GDPopt input:
  Pyomo ConcreteModel / concrete instance containing:
    Disjunct
    Disjunction
    BooleanVar
    LogicalConstraint
    algebraic Var / Param / Constraint / Objective

GDPopt output:
  solution on original GDP model
  disjunct indicator values
  continuous variable values
  solver Results object

GDPopt internal pattern:
  master/discrete relaxation
  subproblem solves with fixed logical decisions
  cuts / integer cuts / branch-and-bound / local discrete descent
```

Primary value case:

```text
Use GDPopt when:
  model is naturally GDP
  nonlinear constraints live inside disjuncts
  solving all disjunctive nonlinear constraints simultaneously as a reformulated MINLP is weak or expensive
  only active logical blocks should define nonlinear subproblems
  logic-based decomposition is algorithmically preferable to monolithic reformulation
```

---

## 21.1 Canonical imports and model assumptions

```python
import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.gdp import Disjunct, Disjunction
from pyomo.opt import SolverStatus, TerminationCondition
```

GDPopt expects a concrete Pyomo GDP model or instantiated abstract model:

```python
m = pyo.ConcreteModel()
m.x = pyo.Var(bounds=(-1.2, 2))
m.y = pyo.Var(bounds=(-10, 10))
m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x + m.y == 1)

m.fix_x = Disjunct()
m.fix_x.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x == 0)

m.fix_y = Disjunct()
m.fix_y.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.y == 0)

m.d = Disjunction(expr=[m.fix_x, m.fix_y])
m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.x + 0.1 * m.y, sense=pyo.minimize)
```

Pyomo’s GDPopt docs show the same import pattern and a simple `Disjunct`/`Disjunction` example solved through GDPopt-LOA. ([pyomo.readthedocs.io][1])

---

## 21.2 SolverFactory entry points

### 21.2.1 Generic GDPopt solver

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt").solve(
    m,
    algorithm="LOA",
)
```

GDPopt’s generic solver supports algorithm selection through the `algorithm` argument; Pyomo docs show `pyo.SolverFactory('gdpopt').solve(model, algorithm='LOA')`. ([pyomo.readthedocs.io][1])

### 21.2.2 Algorithm-specific solvers

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt.loa").solve(m)
results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt.gloa").solve(m)
results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt.ric").solve(m)
results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt.lbb").solve(m)
results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt.ldsda").solve(m, ...)
```

Pyomo docs recommend algorithm-specific solvers when repeatedly using the same configuration, because the generic GDPopt solver has minimal configuration outside `solve(...)`. ([pyomo.readthedocs.io][1])

---

## 21.3 Algorithm map

| Solver name      | Algorithm                              | Main idea                                                       | Subsolver sensitivity                             | Use case                                          |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `"gdpopt.loa"`   | Logic-based Outer Approximation        | MILP master + NLP subproblems + OA cuts                         | local NLP quality                                 | convex or locally solved nonlinear GDP            |
| `"gdpopt.gloa"`  | Global Logic-based Outer Approximation | LOA using globally solved nonlinear subproblems                 | global NLP/MINLP solver required for global claim | nonconvex GDP where global optimality is required |
| `"gdpopt.ric"`   | Relaxation with Integer Cuts           | MILP relaxation + no-good/integer cuts instead of OA cuts       | global subproblem solving for global claim        | discrete-solution exploration / RIC strategy      |
| `"gdpopt.lbb"`   | Logic-based Branch-and-Bound           | branches through relaxed subproblems with inactive disjunctions | nonlinear subproblem quality                      | experimental/cautious use                         |
| `"gdpopt.ldsda"` | Logic-based Discrete Steepest Descent  | ordered Boolean/disjunctive search with neighborhood directions | start point and discrete neighborhood             | structured ordered disjunctions                   |

Pyomo docs describe GLOA as LOA applied to GDPs with nonconvex nonlinear constraints by solving subproblems globally, warn that `nlp_solver` must be a global solver for GDPopt to return a globally optimal solution, describe RIC as adding no-good cuts for encountered discrete solutions, describe LBB as branching through relaxed subproblems, and state LD-SDA requires XOR constraints plus a discrete starting point. ([pyomo.readthedocs.io][1])

---

## 21.4 Generic `solve(...)` syntax

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt").solve(
    m,
    algorithm="LOA",
    mip_solver="highs",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    tee=True,
)
```

Common keyword categories:

```text
algorithm:
  LOA
  GLOA
  RIC
  LBB
  LDSDA / LD-SDA depending interface spelling/version

mip_solver:
  MILP master/relaxation solver

nlp_solver:
  NLP subproblem solver

minlp_solver:
  optional MINLP subproblem solver in some workflows

tee:
  verbose GDPopt/subsolver output

iterlim:
  iteration limit

time_limit:
  overall seconds allowed, with enforcement between subsolver calls

*_solver_options:
  subsolver-specific option dictionaries, interface/version dependent
```

GDPopt solver API docs list `iterlim`, `time_limit`, `tee`, and `logger` as common solve keywords, and warn that `time_limit` can currently be enforced only between subsolver invocations, so subsolver time limits may also be needed. ([pyomo.readthedocs.io][2])

---

## 21.5 LOA: Logic-based Outer Approximation

### 21.5.1 Minimal call

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt.loa").solve(
    m,
    mip_solver="highs",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    tee=True,
)
```

### 21.5.2 Generic call

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt").solve(
    m,
    algorithm="LOA",
    mip_solver="highs",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    tee=True,
)
```

### 21.5.3 Use when

```text
Use LOA when:
  nonlinear GDP is convex or local NLP solutions are acceptable
  active-disjunct NLP subproblems are much smaller than monolithic MINLP
  MILP master can guide discrete choices effectively
  you want logic-based decomposition, not full reformulation
```

### 21.5.4 Avoid / caution

```text
Caution for LOA:
  nonconvex subproblems solved locally do not imply global optimality
  bad NLP initial values can derail subproblem solves
  missing bounds can damage relaxation quality
  inactive-disjunct constraints are intentionally omitted from NLP subproblems
```

The GDPopt API notes that, for nonconvex problems, LOA may not report rigorous lower/upper bounds. ([pyomo.readthedocs.io][2])

---

## 21.6 GLOA: Global Logic-based Outer Approximation

### 21.6.1 Call

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt.gloa").solve(
    m,
    mip_solver="highs",
    nlp_solver="baron",   # example placeholder: must be available/configured
    tee=True,
)
```

### 21.6.2 Use when

```text
Use GLOA when:
  nonlinear constraints are nonconvex
  global optimality is required
  global NLP/MINLP subsolver is installed/licensed
  subproblem global solves are tractable
```

### 21.6.3 Critical globality rule

```text
GLOA global claim requires global subproblem solves.
If nlp_solver is local, the GDPopt run is not a global optimization certificate.
```

Pyomo docs explicitly warn that the `nlp_solver` option must be set to a global solver for the solution returned by GDPopt-GLOA to also be globally optimal. ([pyomo.readthedocs.io][1])

---

## 21.7 RIC: Relaxation with Integer Cuts

### 21.7.1 Call

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt.ric").solve(
    m,
    mip_solver="highs",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    tee=True,
)
```

### 21.7.2 Behavior

```text
RIC:
  uses the same MILP relaxation family as LOA/GLOA
  solves subproblems
  does not generate outer-approximation cuts
  adds no-good / integer cuts for discrete solutions encountered
```

Pyomo docs describe RIC as using the same MILP relaxation as LOA/GLOA but adding only no-good cuts for every discrete solution encountered rather than OA cuts; the docs also note it may not enumerate every discrete solution because bounds can converge first. ([pyomo.readthedocs.io][1])

### 21.7.3 Use when

```text
Use RIC when:
  discrete exploration is useful
  OA cuts are weak/problematic
  no-good-cut style iteration is preferred
  subproblem quality is still reliable
```

---

## 21.8 LBB: Logic-based Branch-and-Bound

### 21.8.1 Call

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt.lbb").solve(
    m,
    tee=True,
)
```

### 21.8.2 Behavior

```text
LBB:
  branches over relaxed subproblems
  inactive disjunctions remain relaxed at nodes
  explores possibilities based on lower bounds
  activates disjunctions progressively
```

Pyomo’s GDPopt docs describe LBB as branching through relaxed subproblems with inactive disjunctions, exploring possibilities based on best lower bound and eventually activating all disjunctions. The same docs include a warning that the LBB algorithm has known issues and should be used with caution. ([pyomo.readthedocs.io][1])

### 21.8.3 Deployment policy

```text
Use LBB only when:
  you have a reason to test logic-based branch-and-bound
  you can benchmark against Big-M/hull/LOA/GLOA
  you can validate solution quality independently
  warnings/known-issue status are acceptable
```

---

## 21.9 LD-SDA: Logic-based Discrete-Steepest Descent Algorithm

### 21.9.1 Required structures

```text
LD-SDA requires:
  ordered Boolean/disjunctive decisions
  explicit LogicalConstraint enforcing XOR/exactly-one for each disjunction
  starting_point for discrete variables
  direction_norm in {"L2", "Linf"}
```

Pyomo docs state GDPopt-LDSDA exploits ordered Boolean variables, requires an exclusive-OR logical constraint to ensure exactly one disjunct is active in each disjunction, requires a discrete starting point, and supports `L2` and `Linf` direction norms. ([pyomo.readthedocs.io][1])

### 21.9.2 Example structure

```python
m.I = pyo.RangeSet(1, 5)
m.J = pyo.RangeSet(1, 5)

m.a = pyo.Var(bounds=(-0.3, 0.2))
m.b = pyo.Var(bounds=(-0.9, -0.5))

m.Y1 = Disjunct(m.I)
for i in m.I:
    m.Y1[i].fix_a = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.a == -0.3 + 0.1 * (i - 1))

m.Y2 = Disjunct(m.J)
for j in m.J:
    m.Y2[j].fix_b = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.b == -0.9 + 0.1 * (j - 1))

m.d1 = Disjunction(expr=[m.Y1[i] for i in m.I])
m.d2 = Disjunction(expr=[m.Y2[j] for j in m.J])

m.Y1_limit = pyo.LogicalConstraint(
    expr=pyo.exactly(1, [m.Y1[i].indicator_var for i in m.I])
)
m.Y2_limit = pyo.LogicalConstraint(
    expr=pyo.exactly(1, [m.Y2[j].indicator_var for j in m.J])
)

m.obj = pyo.Objective(
    expr=4 * m.a**2 - 2.1 * m.a**4 + (1 / 3) * m.a**6
         + m.a * m.b - 4 * m.b**2 + 4 * m.b**4,
    sense=pyo.minimize,
)
```

### 21.9.3 Solve

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt.ldsda").solve(
    m,
    starting_point=[1, 1],
    logical_constraint_list=[m.Y1_limit, m.Y2_limit],
    direction_norm="Linf",
    tee=True,
)
```

Pyomo’s LD-SDA example uses `starting_point=[1,1]`, passes a list of explicit XOR `LogicalConstraint` objects through `logical_constraint_list`, and sets `direction_norm='Linf'`. ([pyomo.readthedocs.io][1])

---

## 21.10 MIP/NLP solver configuration

### 21.10.1 Baseline open-source local configuration

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt.loa").solve(
    m,
    mip_solver="highs",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    tee=True,
)
```

### 21.10.2 Commercial MILP + local NLP

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt.loa").solve(
    m,
    mip_solver="gurobi",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    tee=True,
)
```

### 21.10.3 Global NLP/GLOA configuration

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt.gloa").solve(
    m,
    mip_solver="gurobi",
    nlp_solver="baron",  # project-specific global solver example
    tee=True,
)
```

### 21.10.4 Subsolver option pattern

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt.loa").solve(
    m,
    mip_solver="gurobi",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    mip_solver_args={
        "options": {
            "TimeLimit": 300,
            "MIPGap": 1e-4,
        }
    },
    nlp_solver_args={
        "options": {
            "max_iter": 3000,
            "tol": 1e-7,
        }
    },
    tee=True,
)
```

Subsolver option keyword names may change across GDPopt versions because GDPopt optional arguments are documented as beta and subject to change; generated agents should wrap them in a project-level configuration and smoke-test the exact Pyomo version. ([pyomo.readthedocs.io][1])

---

## 21.11 Subsolver availability validation

GDPopt itself reports as available even though subsolvers may not be; Pyomo’s GDPopt API says `available()` is always true and subsolvers raise errors later if missing. Therefore, validate subsolvers explicitly before the GDPopt solve. ([pyomo.readthedocs.io][2])

```python
def require_solver(name: str):
    opt = pyo.SolverFactory(name)
    if opt is None or not opt.available(exception_flag=False):
        raise RuntimeError(f"required solver unavailable: {name}")
    if hasattr(opt, "license_is_valid"):
        try:
            if not opt.license_is_valid():
                raise RuntimeError(f"solver license invalid: {name}")
        except NotImplementedError:
            pass
    return opt


def validate_gdpopt_subsolvers(mip_solver=None, nlp_solver=None, minlp_solver=None):
    for name in [mip_solver, nlp_solver, minlp_solver]:
        if name is not None:
            require_solver(name)
```

Usage:

```python
validate_gdpopt_subsolvers(
    mip_solver="highs",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
)

results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt.loa").solve(
    m,
    mip_solver="highs",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
)
```

## 21.12 Result handling

### 21.12.1 Standard check

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt.loa").solve(
    m,
    mip_solver="highs",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    tee=True,
)

if (
    results.solver.status == SolverStatus.ok
    and results.solver.termination_condition == TerminationCondition.optimal
):
    pass
else:
    raise RuntimeError(
        f"GDPopt failed: status={results.solver.status}, "
        f"termination={results.solver.termination_condition}"
    )
```

GDPopt examples show reading `results.solver.status` and `results.solver.termination_condition`, including an LBB example printing `ok` and `optimal`. ([pyomo.readthedocs.io][1])

### 21.12.2 Indicator report

```python
def selected_disjuncts(m: pyo.Block, tol: float = 1e-6) -> list[str]:
    selected = []
    for d in m.component_data_objects(Disjunct, active=None, descend_into=True):
        val = pyo.value(d.indicator_var, exception=False)
        if val is True or (isinstance(val, (int, float)) and val >= 1 - tol):
            selected.append(d.name)
    return selected
```

### 21.12.3 Variable report

```python
def primal_solution(m: pyo.Block) -> dict[str, float | None]:
    return {
        v.name: pyo.value(v, exception=False)
        for v in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True)
    }
```

### 21.12.4 GDPopt manifest

```python
def gdpopt_manifest(m, results, cfg: dict) -> dict:
    return {
        "algorithm": cfg.get("algorithm"),
        "solver_name": cfg.get("solver_name"),
        "mip_solver": cfg.get("mip_solver"),
        "nlp_solver": cfg.get("nlp_solver"),
        "minlp_solver": cfg.get("minlp_solver"),
        "status": str(results.solver.status),
        "termination_condition": str(results.solver.termination_condition),
        "selected_disjuncts": selected_disjuncts(m),
        "objective": pyo.value(next(m.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=True)), exception=False),
        "n_vars": sum(1 for _ in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True)),
        "n_constraints": sum(1 for _ in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Constraint, active=True, descend_into=True)),
    }
```

## 21.13 When GDPopt is better than MINLP reformulation

```text
Prefer GDPopt when:
  nonlinear constraints are localized inside disjuncts
  only a small subset of logical blocks is active in any feasible solution
  monolithic Big-M or hull MINLP has weak relaxations or many generated nonlinear constraints
  subproblem NLPs are much smaller/easier than full MINLP
  logic-based cuts are effective
  discrete decision space is structured
  direct GDP model clarity matters
```

```text
Prefer reformulation when:
  model is linear GDP and MILP solver is strong
  Big-M/hull reformulation is compact and well-conditioned
  global MINLP solver handles the reformulated model well
  production system requires a single solver call
  GDPopt subproblem failures are frequent
  GDPopt optional-argument/API stability is a concern
```

Pyomo’s GDPopt docs explicitly contrast logic-based decomposition with conventional MINLP reformulation and identify reduced-space subproblem solution as the main advantage, particularly for nonlinear GDPs. ([pyomo.readthedocs.io][1])

---

## 21.14 Algorithm selection policy

```text
Linear GDP:
  first try gdp.bigm / gdp.hull + MILP solver
  GDPopt may be less necessary unless decomposition is desired

Convex nonlinear GDP:
  try GDPopt LOA
  compare against gdp.hull/gdp.bigm + MINLP solver
  validate local NLP convergence

Nonconvex nonlinear GDP:
  use GLOA only with global nonlinear subsolver if global guarantee is required
  otherwise label result as local / heuristic / non-certified

Large ordered discrete choices:
  consider LD-SDA if explicit XOR constraints and starting point are natural

Unstable OA cuts or enumeration-like behavior desired:
  test RIC

LBB:
  experimental/cautious benchmarking only
```

---

## 21.15 GDP model preflight checks

### 21.15.1 Exactly one active objective

```python
def require_single_active_objective(m: pyo.Block):
    objs = list(m.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=True, descend_into=True))
    if len(objs) != 1:
        raise ValueError(f"expected exactly one active objective, found {len(objs)}")
    return objs[0]
```

### 21.15.2 Variable bounds audit

```python
def unbounded_vars(m: pyo.Block) -> list[str]:
    return [
        v.name
        for v in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True)
        if not v.fixed and (v.lb is None or v.ub is None)
    ]
```

### 21.15.3 Disjunct variable bounds audit

```python
def unbounded_vars_in_disjuncts(m: pyo.Block) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    bad = []
    for d in m.component_data_objects(Disjunct, active=True, descend_into=True):
        for v in d.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True):
            if not v.fixed and (v.lb is None or v.ub is None):
                bad.append((d.name, v.name))
    return bad
```

### 21.15.4 Disjunction count

```python
def gdp_structure_stats(m: pyo.Block) -> dict:
    return {
        "n_disjuncts": sum(1 for _ in m.component_data_objects(Disjunct, active=True, descend_into=True)),
        "n_disjunctions": sum(1 for _ in m.component_data_objects(Disjunction, active=True, descend_into=True)),
        "n_boolean_vars": sum(1 for _ in m.component_data_objects(pyo.BooleanVar, descend_into=True)),
        "n_logical_constraints": sum(1 for _ in m.component_data_objects(pyo.LogicalConstraint, active=True, descend_into=True)),
    }
```

### 21.15.5 Preflight

```python
def preflight_gdpopt_model(m: pyo.Block, *, require_bounds=True):
    require_single_active_objective(m)

    stats = gdp_structure_stats(m)
    if stats["n_disjunctions"] == 0:
        raise ValueError("GDPopt model has no active Disjunction components")

    if require_bounds:
        bad = unbounded_vars_in_disjuncts(m)
        if bad:
            raise ValueError(f"unbounded variables in disjuncts: {bad[:20]}")

    return stats
```

## 21.17 Troubleshooting: subproblem failures

```text
Common NLP subproblem failure causes:
  bad initial values
  unbounded variables
  log/sqrt/division domain errors
  zero-flow singularities
  infeasible active disjunct combination
  poor scaling
  local NLP solver stuck at infeasible point
  nonlinear constraints in inactive blocks unexpectedly active due to modeling error
```

### 21.17.1 NLP initialization audit

```python
def missing_nlp_starts(m: pyo.Block) -> list[str]:
    return [
        v.name
        for v in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True)
        if v.value is None and not v.fixed and not v.is_binary() and not v.is_integer()
    ]
```

### 21.17.2 Domain-safe starts

```python
for v in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True):
    if v.value is None and v.lb is not None and v.ub is not None:
        v.set_value(0.5 * (pyo.value(v.lb) + pyo.value(v.ub)))
```

### 21.17.3 Bounds audit

```python
bad_bounds = unbounded_vars_in_disjuncts(m)
if bad_bounds:
    raise ValueError(bad_bounds[:20])
```

### 21.17.4 Scaling advisory

```text
If NLP subproblems fail:
  scale variables and constraints
  bound variables away from singularities
  initialize continuous variables inside feasible-like regions
  replace problematic external functions with algebraic/Piecewise approximations if possible
```

---

## 21.18 Troubleshooting: global vs local subsolvers

```text
Local NLP solver:
  fast
  may converge to local optimum
  may fail on bad starts
  does not certify nonconvex global optimum

Global nonlinear solver:
  slower
  may require licenses
  necessary for global optimality claims in nonconvex GLOA/RIC-style workflows
```

Critical claim rule:

```text
Do not write "global optimum" in reports unless:
  GDPopt algorithm supports global reasoning for that model class
  nonlinear subproblems are solved globally
  solver termination conditions support the claim
```

Pyomo docs explicitly state GLOA requires a global `nlp_solver` for GDPopt’s returned solution to also be globally optimal, and RIC is global only if subproblems are solved globally. ([pyomo.readthedocs.io][1])

## 21.20 Safe GDPopt wrapper

```python
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.gdp import Disjunct, Disjunction
from pyomo.opt import SolverStatus, TerminationCondition


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GDPoptConfig:
    solver_name: str = "gdpopt.loa"
    algorithm: str | None = None
    mip_solver: str | None = "highs"
    nlp_solver: str | None = "ipopt"
    minlp_solver: str | None = None
    tee: bool = False
    iterlim: int | None = None
    time_limit: int | None = None
    mip_solver_args: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    nlp_solver_args: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    minlp_solver_args: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    require_optimal: bool = True


def require_solver_available(name: str | None) -> None:
    if name is None:
        return

    opt = pyo.SolverFactory(name)
    if opt is None or not opt.available(exception_flag=False):
        raise RuntimeError(f"required subsolver unavailable: {name}")

    if hasattr(opt, "license_is_valid"):
        try:
            if not opt.license_is_valid():
                raise RuntimeError(f"subsolver license invalid: {name}")
        except NotImplementedError:
            pass


def preflight_gdp_model(m: pyo.Block) -> dict:
    objs = list(m.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=True, descend_into=True))
    if len(objs) != 1:
        raise ValueError(f"expected exactly one active objective, found {len(objs)}")

    stats = {
        "n_disjuncts": sum(1 for _ in m.component_data_objects(Disjunct, active=True, descend_into=True)),
        "n_disjunctions": sum(1 for _ in m.component_data_objects(Disjunction, active=True, descend_into=True)),
        "n_vars": sum(1 for _ in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True)),
        "n_constraints": sum(1 for _ in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Constraint, active=True, descend_into=True)),
    }

    if stats["n_disjunctions"] == 0:
        raise ValueError("model has no active disjunctions")

    return stats


def solve_gdpopt_checked(m: pyo.ConcreteModel, cfg: GDPoptConfig):
    preflight = preflight_gdp_model(m)

    require_solver_available(cfg.mip_solver)
    require_solver_available(cfg.nlp_solver)
    require_solver_available(cfg.minlp_solver)

    opt = pyo.SolverFactory(cfg.solver_name)
    if opt is None or not opt.available(exception_flag=False):
        raise RuntimeError(f"GDPopt solver unavailable: {cfg.solver_name}")

    kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
        "tee": cfg.tee,
    }

    if cfg.algorithm is not None:
        kwargs["algorithm"] = cfg.algorithm
    if cfg.mip_solver is not None:
        kwargs["mip_solver"] = cfg.mip_solver
    if cfg.nlp_solver is not None:
        kwargs["nlp_solver"] = cfg.nlp_solver
    if cfg.minlp_solver is not None:
        kwargs["minlp_solver"] = cfg.minlp_solver

    if cfg.iterlim is not None:
        kwargs["iterlim"] = cfg.iterlim
    if cfg.time_limit is not None:
        kwargs["time_limit"] = cfg.time_limit

    if cfg.mip_solver_args:
        kwargs["mip_solver_args"] = cfg.mip_solver_args
    if cfg.nlp_solver_args:
        kwargs["nlp_solver_args"] = cfg.nlp_solver_args
    if cfg.minlp_solver_args:
        kwargs["minlp_solver_args"] = cfg.minlp_solver_args

    results = opt.solve(m, **kwargs)

    if cfg.require_optimal:
        if not (
            results.solver.status == SolverStatus.ok
            and results.solver.termination_condition == TerminationCondition.optimal
        ):
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"GDPopt failed: status={results.solver.status}, "
                f"termination={results.solver.termination_condition}"
            )

    return results, preflight
```

## 21.21 LD-SDA wrapper

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LDSDAConfig:
    starting_point: list[int]
    logical_constraint_list: list
    direction_norm: str = "Linf"
    tee: bool = False


def solve_ldsda_checked(m: pyo.ConcreteModel, cfg: LDSDAConfig):
    if cfg.direction_norm not in {"L2", "Linf"}:
        raise ValueError("direction_norm must be 'L2' or 'Linf'")

    if not cfg.starting_point:
        raise ValueError("LD-SDA requires starting_point")

    if not cfg.logical_constraint_list:
        raise ValueError("LD-SDA requires explicit XOR logical constraints")

    results = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt.ldsda").solve(
        m,
        starting_point=cfg.starting_point,
        logical_constraint_list=cfg.logical_constraint_list,
        direction_norm=cfg.direction_norm,
        tee=cfg.tee,
    )

    if not (
        results.solver.status == SolverStatus.ok
        and results.solver.termination_condition == TerminationCondition.optimal
    ):
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"LD-SDA failed: status={results.solver.status}, "
            f"termination={results.solver.termination_condition}"
        )

    return results
```
