## 21.22 GDPopt vs reformulation benchmark harness

```python
def solve_reformulated(model, transformation_name: str, solver_name: str, options=None):
    m = model.clone()
    pyo.TransformationFactory(transformation_name).apply_to(m)

    opt = pyo.SolverFactory(solver_name)
    if opt is None or not opt.available(exception_flag=False):
        raise RuntimeError(f"solver unavailable: {solver_name}")

    results = opt.solve(m, options=options or {}, load_solutions=False)

    if results.solver.termination_condition == TerminationCondition.optimal:
        m.solutions.load_from(results)

    obj = next(m.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=True, descend_into=True))

    return {
        "method": transformation_name,
        "status": str(results.solver.status),
        "termination": str(results.solver.termination_condition),
        "objective": pyo.value(obj, exception=False),
        "n_vars": sum(1 for _ in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True)),
        "n_constraints": sum(1 for _ in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Constraint, active=True, descend_into=True)),
    }


def solve_gdpopt_for_benchmark(model, cfg: GDPoptConfig):
    m = model.clone()
    results, stats = solve_gdpopt_checked(m, cfg)

    obj = next(m.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=True, descend_into=True))

    return {
        "method": cfg.solver_name if cfg.algorithm is None else f"gdpopt:{cfg.algorithm}",
        "status": str(results.solver.status),
        "termination": str(results.solver.termination_condition),
        "objective": pyo.value(obj, exception=False),
        "selected_disjuncts": selected_disjuncts(m),
        **stats,
    }
```

Usage:

```python
benchmark = [
    solve_reformulated(base_model, "gdp.bigm", "highs"),
    solve_reformulated(base_model, "gdp.hull", "highs"),
    solve_gdpopt_for_benchmark(
        base_model,
        GDPoptConfig(
            solver_name="gdpopt.loa",
            mip_solver="highs",
            nlp_solver="ipopt",
            tee=True,
        ),
    ),
]
```

### 21.23.4 Reformulation comparison

```python
def test_loa_matches_bigm_on_small_convex_case(model):
    gdp = model.clone()
    res_gdp = pyo.SolverFactory("gdpopt.loa").solve(
        gdp,
        mip_solver="highs",
        nlp_solver="ipopt",
    )

    reform = model.clone()
    pyo.TransformationFactory("gdp.bigm").apply_to(reform)
    opt = pyo.SolverFactory("highs")
    res_ref = opt.solve(reform, load_solutions=False)
    if res_ref.solver.termination_condition == TerminationCondition.optimal:
        reform.solutions.load_from(res_ref)

    obj_gdp = pyo.value(next(gdp.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=True)))
    obj_ref = pyo.value(next(reform.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=True)))

    assert abs(obj_gdp - obj_ref) <= 1e-5
```

## 21.24 Deployment advisory

```text
[ ] Validate GDP structure before GDPopt solve.
[ ] Validate MIP/NLP/MINLP subsolver availability explicitly.
[ ] Use tee=True for first integration runs and all failure investigations.
[ ] Put subsolver options behind version-tested config objects.
[ ] Set both GDPopt time_limit and subsolver limits for runtime control.
[ ] Use LOA for convex/local nonlinear GDP baseline.
[ ] Use GLOA only with global nonlinear subsolver when claiming global optimality.
[ ] Treat RIC as discrete-cut relaxation algorithm, not full enumeration guarantee.
[ ] Use LBB cautiously due to documented known issues.
[ ] Use LD-SDA only with ordered disjunctions, explicit XOR LogicalConstraints, and starting_point.
[ ] Compare GDPopt against gdp.bigm and gdp.hull on small/representative instances.
[ ] Report selected disjuncts, objective, solver status, termination, algorithm, subsolvers, and subsolver options.
[ ] Do not report locally solved nonconvex GDPopt results as globally optimal.
```

---

## 21.25 Anti-pattern table

| Anti-pattern                                                     | Failure mode                                     | Replacement                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| rely on `SolverFactory("gdpopt").available()` as subsolver check | GDPopt available but subsolvers fail later       | validate `mip_solver`, `nlp_solver`, `minlp_solver` explicitly |
| use GLOA with local NLP and claim global optimum                 | false globality claim                            | use global nonlinear subsolver or label local                  |
| use LD-SDA without explicit XOR logical constraints              | solver requirement violation                     | add `LogicalConstraint(expr=exactly(...))`                     |
| use LD-SDA without `starting_point`                              | missing algorithm input                          | pass discrete starting point                                   |
| ignore `tee=True` on failures                                    | opaque subproblem failure                        | enable GDPopt and subsolver logs                               |
| set only GDPopt `time_limit`                                     | long subsolver call can exceed practical runtime | also set subsolver time limits                                 |
| no bounds / poor starts in nonlinear GDP                         | NLP subproblem failure                           | bound and initialize continuous variables                      |
| use LBB as production default                                    | known-issue risk                                 | benchmark/cautious use                                         |
| compare GDPopt to reformulation only on one toy instance         | unreliable method choice                         | benchmark representative instances                             |
| report generated/logical details poorly                          | unclear solution                                 | report selected disjuncts and original business variables      |

## 21.26 Agent-ready production template

```python
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field, asdict
from typing import Any
import json
from pathlib import Path

import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.gdp import Disjunct, Disjunction
from pyomo.opt import SolverStatus, TerminationCondition


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GDPoptRunConfig:
    solver_name: str = "gdpopt.loa"
    algorithm: str | None = None
    mip_solver: str | None = "highs"
    nlp_solver: str | None = "ipopt"
    minlp_solver: str | None = None
    mip_solver_args: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    nlp_solver_args: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    minlp_solver_args: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    iterlim: int | None = None
    time_limit: int | None = None
    tee: bool = False
    require_optimal: bool = True


def require_solver_available(name: str | None) -> None:
    if name is None:
        return

    opt = pyo.SolverFactory(name)
    if opt is None or not opt.available(exception_flag=False):
        raise RuntimeError(f"required solver unavailable: {name}")

    if hasattr(opt, "license_is_valid"):
        try:
            if not opt.license_is_valid():
                raise RuntimeError(f"solver license invalid: {name}")
        except NotImplementedError:
            pass


def selected_disjuncts(m: pyo.Block, tol: float = 1e-6) -> list[str]:
    selected = []
    for d in m.component_data_objects(Disjunct, active=None, descend_into=True):
        val = pyo.value(d.indicator_var, exception=False)
        if val is True or (isinstance(val, (int, float)) and val >= 1 - tol):
            selected.append(d.name)
    return selected


def gdp_stats(m: pyo.Block) -> dict[str, int]:
    return {
        "n_disjuncts": sum(1 for _ in m.component_data_objects(Disjunct, active=True, descend_into=True)),
        "n_disjunctions": sum(1 for _ in m.component_data_objects(Disjunction, active=True, descend_into=True)),
        "n_variables": sum(1 for _ in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True)),
        "n_constraints": sum(1 for _ in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Constraint, active=True, descend_into=True)),
        "n_objectives": sum(1 for _ in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=True, descend_into=True)),
    }


def preflight(m: pyo.Block) -> dict:
    stats = gdp_stats(m)

    if stats["n_objectives"] != 1:
        raise ValueError(f"expected one active objective, found {stats['n_objectives']}")
    if stats["n_disjunctions"] < 1:
        raise ValueError("GDPopt model has no active Disjunction components")

    uninitialized = [
        v.name
        for v in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True)
        if v.value is None and not v.fixed and not v.is_binary() and not v.is_integer()
    ]

    unbounded_disjunct_vars = []
    for d in m.component_data_objects(Disjunct, active=True, descend_into=True):
        for v in d.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True):
            if not v.fixed and (v.lb is None or v.ub is None):
                unbounded_disjunct_vars.append((d.name, v.name))

    return {
        **stats,
        "n_uninitialized_continuous_vars": len(uninitialized),
        "uninitialized_examples": uninitialized[:20],
        "n_unbounded_disjunct_vars": len(unbounded_disjunct_vars),
        "unbounded_disjunct_var_examples": unbounded_disjunct_vars[:20],
    }


def solve_gdpopt(m: pyo.ConcreteModel, cfg: GDPoptRunConfig):
    pre = preflight(m)

    require_solver_available(cfg.mip_solver)
    require_solver_available(cfg.nlp_solver)
    require_solver_available(cfg.minlp_solver)

    opt = pyo.SolverFactory(cfg.solver_name)
    if opt is None or not opt.available(exception_flag=False):
        raise RuntimeError(f"GDPopt solver unavailable: {cfg.solver_name}")

    kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {"tee": cfg.tee}

    if cfg.algorithm is not None:
        kwargs["algorithm"] = cfg.algorithm
    if cfg.mip_solver is not None:
        kwargs["mip_solver"] = cfg.mip_solver
    if cfg.nlp_solver is not None:
        kwargs["nlp_solver"] = cfg.nlp_solver
    if cfg.minlp_solver is not None:
        kwargs["minlp_solver"] = cfg.minlp_solver

    if cfg.mip_solver_args:
        kwargs["mip_solver_args"] = cfg.mip_solver_args
    if cfg.nlp_solver_args:
        kwargs["nlp_solver_args"] = cfg.nlp_solver_args
    if cfg.minlp_solver_args:
        kwargs["minlp_solver_args"] = cfg.minlp_solver_args

    if cfg.iterlim is not None:
        kwargs["iterlim"] = cfg.iterlim
    if cfg.time_limit is not None:
        kwargs["time_limit"] = cfg.time_limit

    results = opt.solve(m, **kwargs)

    if cfg.require_optimal and not (
        results.solver.status == SolverStatus.ok
        and results.solver.termination_condition == TerminationCondition.optimal
    ):
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"GDPopt failed: status={results.solver.status}, "
            f"termination={results.solver.termination_condition}"
        )

    obj = next(m.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=True, descend_into=True))

    report = {
        "config": asdict(cfg),
        "preflight": pre,
        "status": str(results.solver.status),
        "termination_condition": str(results.solver.termination_condition),
        "objective": pyo.value(obj, exception=False),
        "selected_disjuncts": selected_disjuncts(m),
        "variables": {
            v.name: pyo.value(v, exception=False)
            for v in m.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True)
        },
    }

    return results, report


def write_report(path: Path, report: dict) -> None:
    path.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
```

---

## 21.27 Final checklist

```text
[ ] Use SolverFactory("gdpopt").solve(model, algorithm="LOA") for generic calls.
[ ] Prefer SolverFactory("gdpopt.loa") / ".gloa" / ".ric" / ".lbb" / ".ldsda" for repeated configured use.
[ ] Validate subsolver availability separately.
[ ] Configure mip_solver and nlp_solver explicitly.
[ ] Use global nonlinear subsolver for GLOA global-optimality claims.
[ ] Use tee=True for debugging.
[ ] Set GDPopt time_limit and subsolver limits.
[ ] Preflight active objectives, disjunction count, variable bounds, and NLP starts.
[ ] Use LOA as baseline nonlinear GDP decomposition method.
[ ] Use GLOA only with global subproblem solver when globality matters.
[ ] Use RIC when integer-cut exploration is desired.
[ ] Use LBB cautiously because docs flag known issues.
[ ] Use LD-SDA only with explicit XOR LogicalConstraints, starting_point, and valid direction_norm.
[ ] Benchmark GDPopt against gdp.bigm and gdp.hull.
[ ] Record algorithm, subsolvers, options, termination, objective, and selected disjuncts.
[ ] Never label local nonconvex GDPopt results as globally optimal.
```

[1]: https://pyomo.readthedocs.io/en/stable/explanation/solvers/gdpopt.html "GDPopt logic-based solver — Pyomo 6.10.0 documentation"
[2]: https://pyomo.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/pyomo.contrib.gdpopt.GDPopt.GDPoptSolver.html "GDPoptSolver — Pyomo 6.10.0 documentation"

# 22) Mixed-integer nonlinear programming with MindtPy — Pyomo deep dive

Style target: uploaded advanced technical-doc plan. 

MindtPy = **Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Decomposition Toolbox in Pyomo**. It solves MINLPs with decomposition algorithms that usually alternate between **MILP main problems** and **NLP subproblems**. Current Pyomo docs list available MindtPy algorithm families including **Outer Approximation**, **LP/NLP branch-and-bound**, **Extended Cutting Plane**, **Global Outer Approximation**, **Regularized Outer Approximation**, and **Feasibility Pump**. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

---

## 22.0 Mental model

```text
MINLP model:
  continuous variables x ∈ R
  discrete/integer/binary variables y ∈ Z
  smooth nonlinear objective/constraints
  linear constraints may also be present

MindtPy:
  Pyomo meta-solver
  does not solve MINLP directly by itself
  decomposes MINLP into:
    MIP / MILP master or main problem
    NLP fixed-discrete subproblems
    optional regularization problems
    optional feasibility-pump subproblems
    optional single-tree callback cuts
```

Canonical call:

```python
import pyomo.environ as pyo

results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="OA",
    mip_solver="highs",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    tee=True,
)
```

MindtPy’s documented basic usage for convex MINLP is `pyo.SolverFactory('mindtpy').solve(model, mip_solver='glpk', nlp_solver='ipopt')`; `tee=True` is recommended by the docs for troubleshooting. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

---

## 22.1 Input model contract

MindtPy targets MINLPs with continuous variables, discrete/integer variables, smooth nonlinear functions, and linear constraints. The docs present the general model class as continuous variables `x`, integer variables `y`, smooth nonlinear functions `f, g_j`, and linear constraints. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

Minimal convex-ish example:

```python
import pyomo.environ as pyo

m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

m.x = pyo.Var(bounds=(1.0, 10.0), initialize=5.0)
m.y = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.Binary)

m.c1 = pyo.Constraint(expr=(m.x - 4.0) ** 2 - m.x <= 50.0 * (1 - m.y))
m.c2 = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x * pyo.log(m.x) + 5.0 <= 50.0 * m.y)

m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.x, sense=pyo.minimize)

results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    m,
    strategy="OA",
    mip_solver="highs",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    tee=True,
)
```

Agent preflight:

```text
[ ] Exactly one active objective.
[ ] At least one integer/binary/discrete variable.
[ ] Nonlinear expressions are smooth enough for NLP subsolver.
[ ] Variables in log/sqrt/division/power expressions have safe bounds.
[ ] Continuous NLP variables have initialization values.
[ ] MIP subsolver installed and available.
[ ] NLP subsolver installed and available.
[ ] Solver option names are solver-specific.
```

---

## 22.2 SolverFactory entry point

### 22.2.1 Standard MindtPy solve

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="OA",
    mip_solver="highs",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
)
```

### 22.2.2 Verbose solve

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="OA",
    mip_solver="highs",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    tee=True,
    mip_solver_tee=True,
    nlp_solver_tee=True,
)
```

MindtPy exposes `tee`, `solver_tee`, `mip_solver_tee`, and `nlp_solver_tee` options for logging MindtPy and subsolver output. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

### 22.2.3 Subsolver option passing

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="OA",
    time_limit=3600,
    mip_solver="gurobi",
    mip_solver_args={
        "options": {
            "TimeLimit": 600,
            "MIPGap": 1e-4,
            "Threads": 8,
        }
    },
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    nlp_solver_args={
        "options": {
            "max_iter": 3000,
            "tol": 1e-7,
        }
    },
    tee=True,
)
```

The docs show `mip_solver_args` and `nlp_solver_args` for passing options to MIP and NLP subsolvers, and the option list documents `nlp_solver_args`, `mip_solver_args`, `mip_solver_mipgap`, `threads`, and solver-output flags. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

---

## 22.3 Strategy map

| MindtPy strategy / mode | Main syntax                             | Model class target                    | Solver requirements             | Notes                                      |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| OA                      | `strategy="OA"`                         | convex MINLP baseline                 | MILP + NLP                      | default decomposition strategy             |
| ECP                     | `strategy="ECP"`                        | convex MINLP, cutting-plane style     | MILP + NLP/cut evaluations      | default init differs from OA               |
| GOA                     | `strategy="GOA"`                        | nonconvex MINLP with globality intent | MILP + global NLP solver        | uses global outer approximation            |
| FP                      | `strategy="FP"`                         | feasibility search                    | MIP + NLP                       | feasibility pump as decomposition strategy |
| FP initialization       | `init_strategy="FP"` with OA            | hard-to-initialize convex MINLP       | MIP + NLP                       | feasibility pump as initializer            |
| Regularized OA          | `strategy="OA", add_regularization=...` | highly nonlinear convex MINLP         | MILP + NLP + regularization MIP | trust-region/level/Lagrangian variants     |
| LP/NLP BB single-tree   | `strategy="OA", single_tree=True`       | callback-enabled OA                   | persistent CPLEX/Gurobi + NLP   | lazy callback implementation               |

Current documented `strategy` values include `OA`, `ECP`, `GOA`, and `FP`; regularized OA is activated through `add_regularization`, and single-tree LP/NLP branch-and-bound is activated through `single_tree=True` with persistent CPLEX/Gurobi interfaces. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

---

## 22.4 Outer Approximation, OA

### 22.4.1 Basic OA

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="OA",
    mip_solver="highs",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    tee=True,
)
```

### 22.4.2 OA with solver options

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="OA",
    mip_solver="gurobi",
    mip_solver_args={"options": {"TimeLimit": 300, "MIPGap": 1e-4}},
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    nlp_solver_args={"options": {"max_iter": 2000, "tol": 1e-7}},
    mip_solver_tee=True,
    nlp_solver_tee=True,
)
```

Use OA when:

```text
convex MINLP
good NLP subproblem behavior
linearizations/OA cuts are valid and strong
MIP master gives useful discrete proposals
```

Caution:

```text
OA is not a generic global nonconvex guarantee.
Bad NLP starts can cause subproblem failure.
Weak scaling and loose bounds degrade cuts.
```

---

## 22.5 LP/NLP branch-and-bound single-tree mode

### 22.5.1 Syntax

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="OA",
    mip_solver="gurobi_persistent",  # or "cplex_persistent"
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    single_tree=True,
    tee=True,
)
```

The LP/NLP branch-and-bound implementation in MindtPy is a single-tree implementation of OA based on lazy-constraint callbacks in commercial solvers; Pyomo persistent solvers are necessary to register callback functions, and the documented supported interfaces are `cplex_persistent` and `gurobi_persistent`. CPLEX requires IBM CPLEX Optimization Studio plus the CPLEX Python modules, while Gurobi requires `gurobipy`. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

### 22.5.2 Deployment requirements

```text
[ ] Commercial solver installed.
[ ] Python API installed: gurobipy or cplex module.
[ ] Solver license valid.
[ ] Persistent solver interface available.
[ ] MIP solver is "gurobi_persistent" or "cplex_persistent".
[ ] single_tree=True.
[ ] Callback behavior smoke-tested in CI/protected environment.
```

### 22.5.3 Use when

```text
single-tree OA cuts should be generated inside branch-and-bound
commercial MIP solver callbacks are available
standard iterative OA is slower
problem benefits from lazy-cut integration
```

### 22.5.4 Avoid when

```text
open-source-only deployment
no solver Python API
license-server uncertainty
untrusted production environment
callback behavior is not regression-tested
```

---

## 22.6 Extended Cutting Plane, ECP

### 22.6.1 Syntax

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="ECP",
    mip_solver="highs",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    tee=True,
)
```

### 22.6.2 Initialization default

MindtPy documents three initialization strategies: `rNLP`, `initial_binary`, and `max_binary`; OA and GOA default to `rNLP`, while ECP defaults to `max_binary`. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

### 22.6.3 Use when

```text
convex MINLP
cutting-plane approximations are attractive
NLP solves are expensive relative to cut generation
OA has subproblem difficulties
```

---

## 22.7 Global Outer Approximation, GOA

### 22.7.1 Syntax

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="GOA",
    mip_solver="gurobi",
    nlp_solver="baron",
    tee=True,
)
```

The docs describe GOA as a nonconvex MINLP strategy that uses Generalized McCormick envelopes through MC++ to guarantee the validity of the MILP relaxation, and state that NLP subproblems must be solved to global optimality using global NLP solvers such as BARON or SCIP. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

### 22.7.2 Globality rule

```text
GOA + local NLP solver:
  heuristic / local / not global certificate

GOA + global NLP solver:
  candidate for global optimality claim, subject to solver termination
```

### 22.7.3 Single-tree GOA

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="GOA",
    mip_solver="gurobi_persistent",
    nlp_solver="baron",
    single_tree=True,
    tee=True,
)
```

The docs note GOA also has a single-tree implementation with `cplex_persistent` and `gurobi_persistent`, but warn that GOA is more computationally expensive than convex-MINLP strategies such as OA and ECP. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

### 22.7.4 Use when

```text
nonconvex MINLP
global optimality matters
global NLP solver available/licensed
runtime budget accepts expensive subproblem solves
MC++ / relaxation tooling is configured where required
```

---

## 22.8 Regularized OA / ROA

### 22.8.1 Syntax

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="OA",
    mip_solver="cplex",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    add_regularization="level_L1",
    tee=True,
)
```

Alternative regularizations:

```text
level_L1
level_L2
level_L_infinity
grad_lag
hess_lag
hess_only_lag
sqp_lag
```

MindtPy’s regularization feature solves an extra MIP at each decomposition iteration or incumbent solution to provide a point closer to the nonlinear feasible region; the docs list the regularization modes above and describe the method as useful for highly nonlinear convex MINLPs. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

### 22.8.2 Use when

```text
OA stalls or cycles
NLP subproblem starts are poor
linearization points are far from nonlinear feasible region
highly nonlinear convex MINLP
trust-region-like stabilization is useful
```

### 22.8.3 Regularization-specific solver

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="OA",
    mip_solver="gurobi",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    add_regularization="level_L2",
    mip_regularization_solver="gurobi",
    regularization_mip_threads=4,
)
```

The option list includes `mip_regularization_solver` and `regularization_mip_threads` for the regularization problem. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

---

## 22.9 Feasibility Pump, FP

### 22.9.1 FP as initialization strategy

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="OA",
    init_strategy="FP",
    mip_solver="highs",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    tee=True,
)
```

### 22.9.2 FP as decomposition strategy

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="FP",
    mip_solver="highs",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    tee=True,
)
```

MindtPy’s Feasibility Pump is designed to find feasible solutions for convex MINLPs quickly. It alternates between integer-feasible MIP solutions that may violate nonlinear constraints and NLP solutions that satisfy nonlinear constraints but may violate integrality, minimizing the distance between these two solution types. It can be used either as `init_strategy="FP"` or as `strategy="FP"`. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

### 22.9.3 FP options

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="OA",
    init_strategy="FP",
    mip_solver="highs",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    fp_iteration_limit=20,
    fp_main_norm="L1",
    fp_discrete_only=True,
    fp_mipgap=0.01,
    tee=True,
)
```

The option list documents FP controls including `fp_iteration_limit`, `fp_mipgap`, `fp_discrete_only`, `fp_main_norm`, `fp_norm_constraint`, and related feasibility-pump settings. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

---

## 22.10 Initialization strategies

### 22.10.1 Documented strategies

```text
rNLP
initial_binary
max_binary
FP
```

The docs list `rNLP`, `initial_binary`, and `max_binary` as MindtPy initialization strategies, with `rNLP` as the default for OA/GOA and `max_binary` as the default for ECP. FP is additionally documented as an initialization strategy for OA. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

### 22.10.2 Relaxed NLP initialization

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="OA",
    init_strategy="rNLP",
    mip_solver="highs",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
)
```

### 22.10.3 Initial binary strategy

```python
for i in model.I:
    model.y[i].value = 1 if heuristic_select[i] else 0

results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="OA",
    init_strategy="initial_binary",
    mip_solver="highs",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
)
```

### 22.10.4 Max binary strategy

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="ECP",
    init_strategy="max_binary",
    mip_solver="highs",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
)
```

### 22.10.5 Agent initialization policy

```text
Convex MINLP baseline:
  init_strategy="rNLP"

Known feasible binary incumbent:
  initialize binary Var values
  init_strategy="initial_binary"

ECP baseline:
  accept max_binary default or set explicitly

Hard feasibility:
  init_strategy="FP"

Nonlinear domain-sensitive models:
  initialize all continuous variables
  bound variables away from singularities
```

## 22.11 MIP and NLP subsolver selection

### 22.11.1 Documented MIP solver choices

```text
gurobi
cplex
cbc
glpk
gams
gurobi_persistent
cplex_persistent
appsi_cplex
appsi_gurobi
appsi_highs
```

### 22.11.2 Documented NLP solver choices

```text
ipopt
appsi_ipopt
gams
baron
cyipopt
```

MindtPy’s option list documents the MIP and NLP subsolver choices above; `mip_solver` defaults to `glpk`, and `nlp_solver` defaults to `ipopt`. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

### 22.11.3 Availability preflight

```python
def require_solver(name: str):
    opt = pyo.SolverFactory(name)
    if opt is None or not opt.available(exception_flag=False):
        raise RuntimeError(f"solver unavailable: {name}")
    if hasattr(opt, "license_is_valid"):
        try:
            if not opt.license_is_valid():
                raise RuntimeError(f"solver license invalid: {name}")
        except NotImplementedError:
            pass


require_solver("highs")
require_solver("ipopt")
```

### 22.11.4 Solver selection policy

```text
Open-source convex baseline:
  mip_solver="highs" or "cbc"
  nlp_solver="ipopt" or "appsi_ipopt"

Commercial MILP speed:
  mip_solver="gurobi" or "cplex"

Single-tree:
  mip_solver="gurobi_persistent" or "cplex_persistent"

Nonconvex global:
  strategy="GOA"
  nlp_solver must be global, e.g. BARON/SCIP-type route if available

GAMS route:
  use mip_solver="gams" / nlp_solver="gams" with solver-specific args
```

---

## 22.12 Convex vs nonconvex workflows

### 22.12.1 Convex MINLP

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="OA",
    mip_solver="highs",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    init_strategy="rNLP",
    tee=True,
)
```

Convex workflow policy:

```text
[ ] Use OA/ECP/regularized OA.
[ ] Local NLP solver can be sufficient for convex NLP subproblems.
[ ] Confirm convexity assumptions outside Pyomo if global certificate matters.
[ ] Use FP for feasible starts when OA has trouble.
[ ] Use ROA when OA stalling/linearization-point quality is poor.
```

### 22.12.2 Nonconvex MINLP

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="GOA",
    mip_solver="gurobi",
    nlp_solver="baron",
    tee=True,
)
```

Nonconvex workflow policy:

```text
[ ] Do not claim global optimality with local NLP subsolver.
[ ] Use GOA with global NLP subsolver for global-optimality intent.
[ ] Expect higher computational cost than convex strategies.
[ ] Use OA/ECP only as heuristics if globality is not claimed.
[ ] Initialize continuous variables aggressively.
[ ] Tighten bounds and scale nonlinear constraints.
```

The docs explicitly identify GOA as MindtPy’s nonconvex MINLP strategy, require global optimality for NLP subproblems through global NLP solvers such as BARON or SCIP, and note GOA can be more computationally expensive than OA/ECP. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

---

## 22.13 Single-tree and persistent callback workflow

### 22.13.1 CPLEX single-tree

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="OA",
    mip_solver="cplex_persistent",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    single_tree=True,
    tee=True,
)
```

### 22.13.2 Gurobi single-tree

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="OA",
    mip_solver="gurobi_persistent",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    single_tree=True,
    tee=True,
)
```

Single-tree MindtPy uses lazy-constraint callbacks in commercial solvers and currently works with `cplex_persistent` and `gurobi_persistent`; the docs identify CPLEX `LazyConstraintCallback` and Gurobi `cbLazy` as the relevant callback functions. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

### 22.13.3 Add cuts at incumbent

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="OA",
    mip_solver="gurobi_persistent",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    single_tree=True,
    add_cuts_at_incumbent=True,
    tee=True,
)
```

The option list includes `add_cuts_at_incumbent`, which controls whether lazy cuts are added to the main problem at incumbent solutions found in the branch-and-bound tree. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

### 22.13.4 Tabu list / no-good cuts

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="GOA",
    mip_solver="cplex_persistent",
    nlp_solver="baron",
    use_tabu_list=True,
    single_tree=True,
    tee=True,
)
```

For GOA convergence, MindtPy supports no-good cuts and a tabu list; the docs state the tabu list is supported only with `cplex_persistent`, with `gurobi_persistent` pending in the cited section. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

---

## 22.14 Solution pool

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="OA",
    mip_solver="gurobi_persistent",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    solution_pool=True,
    num_solution_iteration=10,
    tee=True,
)
```

MindtPy supports MILP solver solution pools for CPLEX and Gurobi; the docs show `solution_pool=True` and `num_solution_iteration=10`, with the solution pool used to explore several integer combinations in one iteration. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

Use when:

```text
MIP master has many alternative integer solutions
exploring multiple discrete candidates per iteration is beneficial
commercial solver solution-pool feature is available
```

---

## 22.15 Tolerances and stopping controls

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="OA",
    mip_solver="highs",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    iteration_limit=100,
    stalling_limit=20,
    time_limit=3600,
    absolute_bound_tolerance=1e-4,
    relative_bound_tolerance=1e-3,
    integer_tolerance=1e-5,
    constraint_tolerance=1e-6,
    variable_tolerance=1e-8,
    zero_tolerance=1e-8,
    tee=True,
)
```

MindtPy exposes `iteration_limit`, `stalling_limit`, `time_limit`, absolute/relative bound tolerances, integer/constraint/variable/zero tolerances, and warns that its `time_limit` is enforced between subsolver invocations, so subsolver-specific time limits may also be necessary. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

Deployment rule:

```text
Set both:
  MindtPy time_limit
  MIP subsolver time limit
  NLP subsolver iteration/time controls
```

---

## 22.16 Preflight checks

```python
def mindtpy_preflight(model: pyo.Block) -> dict:
    objs = list(model.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=True, descend_into=True))
    if len(objs) != 1:
        raise ValueError(f"expected one active objective, found {len(objs)}")

    vars_ = list(model.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True))
    cons = list(model.component_data_objects(pyo.Constraint, active=True, descend_into=True))

    n_int = sum(v.is_integer() for v in vars_)
    n_bin = sum(v.is_binary() for v in vars_)

    missing_starts = [
        v.name for v in vars_
        if v.value is None and not v.fixed and not v.is_binary() and not v.is_integer()
    ]

    unbounded_nonlinear_candidates = [
        v.name for v in vars_
        if not v.fixed and (v.lb is None or v.ub is None)
    ]

    return {
        "n_variables": len(vars_),
        "n_constraints": len(cons),
        "n_binary_variables": n_bin,
        "n_integer_variables": n_int,
        "n_continuous_variables": sum(v.is_continuous() for v in vars_),
        "missing_continuous_starts": missing_starts[:20],
        "unbounded_variable_examples": unbounded_nonlinear_candidates[:20],
    }
```

Agent rule:

```text
Before MindtPy:
  check one active objective
  check at least one discrete variable
  initialize continuous NLP variables
  bound variables in nonlinear expressions
  validate solver availability
```

---

## 22.17 Safe MindtPy wrapper

```python
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.opt import SolverStatus, TerminationCondition


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MindtPyConfig:
    strategy: str = "OA"
    mip_solver: str = "highs"
    nlp_solver: str = "ipopt"
    init_strategy: str | None = None
    add_regularization: str | None = None
    mip_solver_args: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    nlp_solver_args: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    tee: bool = False
    solver_tee: bool = False
    mip_solver_tee: bool = False
    nlp_solver_tee: bool = False
    iteration_limit: int | None = None
    time_limit: int | None = None
    single_tree: bool = False
    solution_pool: bool = False
    num_solution_iteration: int | None = None
    require_optimal: bool = True


def require_solver_available(name: str) -> None:
    opt = pyo.SolverFactory(name)
    if opt is None or not opt.available(exception_flag=False):
        raise RuntimeError(f"solver unavailable: {name}")

    if hasattr(opt, "license_is_valid"):
        try:
            if not opt.license_is_valid():
                raise RuntimeError(f"solver license invalid: {name}")
        except NotImplementedError:
            pass


def solve_mindtpy_checked(model: pyo.ConcreteModel, cfg: MindtPyConfig):
    require_solver_available(cfg.mip_solver)
    require_solver_available(cfg.nlp_solver)

    preflight = mindtpy_preflight(model)

    kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
        "strategy": cfg.strategy,
        "mip_solver": cfg.mip_solver,
        "nlp_solver": cfg.nlp_solver,
        "tee": cfg.tee,
        "solver_tee": cfg.solver_tee,
        "mip_solver_tee": cfg.mip_solver_tee,
        "nlp_solver_tee": cfg.nlp_solver_tee,
        "single_tree": cfg.single_tree,
        "solution_pool": cfg.solution_pool,
    }

    if cfg.init_strategy is not None:
        kwargs["init_strategy"] = cfg.init_strategy
    if cfg.add_regularization is not None:
        kwargs["add_regularization"] = cfg.add_regularization
    if cfg.mip_solver_args:
        kwargs["mip_solver_args"] = cfg.mip_solver_args
    if cfg.nlp_solver_args:
        kwargs["nlp_solver_args"] = cfg.nlp_solver_args
    if cfg.iteration_limit is not None:
        kwargs["iteration_limit"] = cfg.iteration_limit
    if cfg.time_limit is not None:
        kwargs["time_limit"] = cfg.time_limit
    if cfg.num_solution_iteration is not None:
        kwargs["num_solution_iteration"] = cfg.num_solution_iteration

    results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(model, **kwargs)

    if cfg.require_optimal:
        if not (
            results.solver.status == SolverStatus.ok
            and results.solver.termination_condition == TerminationCondition.optimal
        ):
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"MindtPy failed: status={results.solver.status}, "
                f"termination={results.solver.termination_condition}"
            )

    return results, preflight
```

## 22.23 Troubleshooting playbook

### 22.23.1 Enable logs

```python
results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(
    model,
    strategy="OA",
    mip_solver="highs",
    nlp_solver="ipopt",
    tee=True,
    solver_tee=True,
    mip_solver_tee=True,
    nlp_solver_tee=True,
)
```

### 22.23.2 If MIP main problem fails

```text
Check:
  MIP solver availability
  linearization validity
  MIP option names
  missing finite bounds
  objective epigraph reformulation
  integer_to_binary / no-good cut settings
  solver logs
```

### 22.23.3 If NLP subproblem fails

```text
Check:
  continuous variable initial values
  log/sqrt/division domains
  nonlinear constraint scaling
  Ipopt tolerances / max_iter
  fixed binary configuration feasibility
  local infeasibility from selected integer solution
```

### 22.23.4 If OA stalls/cycles

```text
Try:
  cycling_check=True
  add_regularization="level_L1" or "level_L2"
  init_strategy="FP"
  tighter variable bounds
  better NLP initial values
  different MIP/NLP solvers
```

### 22.23.5 If nonconvex solution quality is suspect

```text
Use:
  strategy="GOA"
  global NLP solver
  tighter bounds
  use_fbbt=True
  compare against reformulated/global solver
```

MindtPy includes `cycling_check`, `use_fbbt`, `differentiate_mode`, bound tolerances, small-dual tolerance, and other numerical controls in its documented option list. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

## 22.26 Deployment advisory

```text
[ ] Treat MindtPy optional arguments as version-sensitive beta configuration.
[ ] Validate MIP and NLP subsolver availability before solve.
[ ] Pin Pyomo, MIP solver, NLP solver, and solver Python packages.
[ ] Use tee=True and subsolver tee flags during integration.
[ ] Set MindtPy time_limit and subsolver time limits.
[ ] Initialize continuous variables before NLP subproblems.
[ ] Bound nonlinear variables tightly.
[ ] Use FP initialization for difficult feasible-start problems.
[ ] Use regularization for OA stalling/highly nonlinear convex MINLP.
[ ] Use GOA only with global NLP solver for global nonconvex claims.
[ ] Use single_tree only with cplex_persistent/gurobi_persistent and required Python APIs.
[ ] Record strategy, init_strategy, add_regularization, subsolvers, tolerances, and options in manifests.
```

MindtPy docs explicitly warn that optional arguments should be considered beta code and subject to change. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

---

## 22.27 Anti-pattern table

| Anti-pattern                                                      | Failure mode                 | Replacement                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| call MindtPy without installing subsolvers                        | runtime failure              | validate MIP/NLP solvers first                 |
| use Ipopt for nonconvex GOA and claim global optimum              | false globality claim        | global NLP solver or local-label result        |
| uninitialized nonlinear variables                                 | NLP failure                  | set `.value` / `initialize=`                   |
| variables in `log`, `sqrt`, division without safe bounds          | domain errors                | bound away from singularities                  |
| one solver option dict for all subsolvers                         | rejected/ignored options     | `mip_solver_args`, `nlp_solver_args`           |
| rely only on MindtPy `time_limit`                                 | subsolver calls may run long | also set subsolver limits                      |
| use `single_tree=True` with nonpersistent solver                  | unsupported callback path    | `cplex_persistent` / `gurobi_persistent`       |
| use single-tree without Python solver API/license                 | callback failure             | install/license CPLEX Python or gurobipy       |
| use OA on difficult model without FP/regularization               | infeasible/stalled search    | `init_strategy="FP"`, `add_regularization=...` |
| report global optimality without convexity/global solver evidence | invalid report               | label local/heuristic/noncertified             |

## 22.28 Agent-ready production template

```python
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field, asdict
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any
import json

import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.opt import SolverStatus, TerminationCondition


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MindtPyRunConfig:
    strategy: str = "OA"
    mip_solver: str = "highs"
    nlp_solver: str = "ipopt"
    init_strategy: str | None = None
    add_regularization: str | None = None
    mip_solver_args: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    nlp_solver_args: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    tee: bool = False
    solver_tee: bool = False
    mip_solver_tee: bool = False
    nlp_solver_tee: bool = False
    iteration_limit: int | None = None
    stalling_limit: int | None = None
    time_limit: int | None = None
    single_tree: bool = False
    solution_pool: bool = False
    num_solution_iteration: int | None = None
    add_cuts_at_incumbent: bool = False
    use_fbbt: bool = False
    require_optimal: bool = True


def require_solver(name: str) -> None:
    opt = pyo.SolverFactory(name)
    if opt is None or not opt.available(exception_flag=False):
        raise RuntimeError(f"solver unavailable: {name}")

    if hasattr(opt, "license_is_valid"):
        try:
            if not opt.license_is_valid():
                raise RuntimeError(f"solver license invalid: {name}")
        except NotImplementedError:
            pass


def preflight_minlp(model: pyo.Block) -> dict:
    objs = list(model.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=True, descend_into=True))
    if len(objs) != 1:
        raise ValueError(f"expected one active objective, found {len(objs)}")

    vars_ = list(model.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True))
    cons = list(model.component_data_objects(pyo.Constraint, active=True, descend_into=True))

    missing_starts = [
        v.name
        for v in vars_
        if v.value is None and not v.fixed and v.is_continuous()
    ]

    missing_bounds = [
        v.name
        for v in vars_
        if not v.fixed and (v.lb is None or v.ub is None)
    ]

    stats = {
        "n_variables": len(vars_),
        "n_constraints": len(cons),
        "n_binary_variables": sum(v.is_binary() for v in vars_),
        "n_integer_variables": sum(v.is_integer() for v in vars_),
        "n_continuous_variables": sum(v.is_continuous() for v in vars_),
        "n_missing_continuous_starts": len(missing_starts),
        "missing_continuous_start_examples": missing_starts[:20],
        "n_missing_bounds": len(missing_bounds),
        "missing_bound_examples": missing_bounds[:20],
    }

    if stats["n_binary_variables"] + stats["n_integer_variables"] == 0:
        raise ValueError("MindtPy model has no discrete variables")

    return stats


def solve_mindtpy(model: pyo.ConcreteModel, cfg: MindtPyRunConfig):
    require_solver(cfg.mip_solver)
    require_solver(cfg.nlp_solver)

    preflight = preflight_minlp(model)

    kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
        "strategy": cfg.strategy,
        "mip_solver": cfg.mip_solver,
        "nlp_solver": cfg.nlp_solver,
        "tee": cfg.tee,
        "solver_tee": cfg.solver_tee,
        "mip_solver_tee": cfg.mip_solver_tee,
        "nlp_solver_tee": cfg.nlp_solver_tee,
        "single_tree": cfg.single_tree,
        "solution_pool": cfg.solution_pool,
        "add_cuts_at_incumbent": cfg.add_cuts_at_incumbent,
        "use_fbbt": cfg.use_fbbt,
    }

    optional = {
        "init_strategy": cfg.init_strategy,
        "add_regularization": cfg.add_regularization,
        "mip_solver_args": cfg.mip_solver_args or None,
        "nlp_solver_args": cfg.nlp_solver_args or None,
        "iteration_limit": cfg.iteration_limit,
        "stalling_limit": cfg.stalling_limit,
        "time_limit": cfg.time_limit,
        "num_solution_iteration": cfg.num_solution_iteration,
    }

    kwargs.update({k: v for k, v in optional.items() if v is not None})

    results = pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(model, **kwargs)

    if cfg.require_optimal and not (
        results.solver.status == SolverStatus.ok
        and results.solver.termination_condition == TerminationCondition.optimal
    ):
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"MindtPy failed: status={results.solver.status}, "
            f"termination={results.solver.termination_condition}"
        )

    return results, preflight


def mindtpy_manifest(model: pyo.Block, results, cfg: MindtPyRunConfig, preflight: dict) -> dict:
    obj = next(model.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=True, descend_into=True))

    return {
        "solver": "mindtpy",
        "config": asdict(cfg),
        "preflight": preflight,
        "status": str(results.solver.status),
        "termination_condition": str(results.solver.termination_condition),
        "objective": pyo.value(obj, exception=False),
        "variables": {
            v.name: pyo.value(v, exception=False)
            for v in model.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True)
        },
    }


def write_manifest(path: Path, manifest: dict) -> None:
    path.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
```

## 22.29 Final checklist

```text
[ ] Use pyo.SolverFactory("mindtpy").solve(model, ...).
[ ] Set strategy explicitly: OA, ECP, GOA, or FP.
[ ] Use add_regularization for regularized OA variants.
[ ] Use init_strategy for rNLP / initial_binary / max_binary / FP initialization.
[ ] Configure mip_solver and nlp_solver explicitly.
[ ] Validate MIP/NLP solver availability before MindtPy.
[ ] Pass subsolver options via mip_solver_args and nlp_solver_args.
[ ] Use tee / solver_tee / mip_solver_tee / nlp_solver_tee for debugging.
[ ] Initialize continuous variables for NLP subproblems.
[ ] Bound nonlinear variables tightly.
[ ] Use FP when feasible starts are hard.
[ ] Use regularization when OA stalls on highly nonlinear convex MINLPs.
[ ] Use GOA with global NLP solver for nonconvex global workflows.
[ ] Do not claim global optimality with local NLP subsolver on nonconvex models.
[ ] Use single_tree only with cplex_persistent or gurobi_persistent.
[ ] Install and license CPLEX Python API or gurobipy for single-tree callbacks.
[ ] Set both MindtPy and subsolver time limits.
[ ] Treat optional arguments as version-sensitive beta configuration.
[ ] Record strategy, solvers, options, tolerances, status, termination, and objective in reports.
```
