## 30.21 Deployment advisory

```text
[ ] Use alternative_solutions for context, not as replacement for a primary solve.
[ ] Record method, solver, gap policy, search mode, seed, and solver options.
[ ] Use enumerate_binary_solutions for binary-structure alternatives.
[ ] Use enumerate_linear_solutions for LP/MILP alternatives with continuous diversity.
[ ] Use Gurobi solution-pool methods when Gurobi is installed/licensed and many alternatives are needed.
[ ] Use OBBT-style analysis only on selected variables unless model is small.
[ ] Use absolute and relative gaps deliberately.
[ ] Report objective values and gaps for every alternative.
[ ] Compute diversity metrics for solution sets.
[ ] Do not claim all feasible alternatives were found unless the selected method/solver termination guarantees support that claim.
[ ] Validate Gurobi PoolSearchMode semantics before making n-best claims.
```

---

## 30.22 Anti-pattern table

| Anti-pattern                                                              | Failure mode                          | Replacement                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| treat near-optimal alternatives as optimal                                | false optimality claim                | report gap and objective         |
| omit solver/options/seed in reports                                       | irreproducible alternatives           | run manifest                     |
| run full OBBT on every variable in huge MIP                               | excessive runtime                     | selected variables               |
| use arbitrary `num_solutions=10000`                                       | runaway solve time                    | limit + time budget              |
| use Gurobi pool without checking license                                  | runtime failure                       | availability/license preflight   |
| ignore `PoolSearchMode`                                                   | wrong solution-quality interpretation | set/report `PoolSearchMode`      |
| no diversity metric                                                       | indistinguishable alternatives        | Hamming/L1/L2 distance           |
| manual no-good cuts on nonbinary variables                                | invalid exclusion logic               | linear enumeration or pool tools |
| report generated solution order as preference order without objective/gap | misleading ranking                    | explicit ranking columns         |
| temporarily load solution and forget restore                              | corrupted model state                 | context manager                  |

---

## 30.23 Final checklist

```text
[ ] Import pyomo.contrib.alternative_solutions as aos.
[ ] Use enumerate_binary_solutions for binary alternatives via no-good cuts.
[ ] Use search_mode="optimal", "random", or "hamming" for binary enumeration.
[ ] Use enumerate_linear_solutions for linear model alternatives.
[ ] Use search_mode="optimal", "random", or "norm" for linear enumeration.
[ ] Use enumerate_linear_solutions_soln_pool for mixed-binary linear Gurobi solution-pool alternatives.
[ ] Use gurobi_generate_solutions for Gurobi discrete solution-pool extraction.
[ ] Use PoolSearchMode=2 for systematic n-best Gurobi search when needed.
[ ] Use rel_opt_gap / abs_opt_gap intentionally.
[ ] Use obbt_analysis for variable ranges.
[ ] Use obbt_analysis_bounds_and_solutions for ranges plus solution snapshots.
[ ] Extract values through Solution methods, not model.solutions.
[ ] Compute objective gaps and diversity metrics.
[ ] Store JSON/CSV reports and run manifest.
[ ] Use solver time limits and selected variable lists for expensive workflows.
[ ] Verify solution-pool guarantees before claiming completeness.
```

# 31) Infeasibility diagnostics — IIS, MIS, repair explanations, and production workflow

Pyomo documents two closely related infeasibility-diagnosis tools: **IIS** and **MIS**. IIS is a conduit to commercial solvers that compute an irreducible infeasible system for LP/MILP models; Pyomo supports CPLEX, Gurobi, and Xpress for this route. MIS is Pyomo-contributed logic that searches for relaxations that recover feasibility and then attempts to compute a **minimal intractable system**: constraints and variable bounds that appear mutually conflicting, minimal in the sense that removing any single item would make the subsystem feasible. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

---

## 31.0 Mental model

```text id="svv7ge"
Infeasible model:
  solver proves no feasible solution under current constraints/bounds/domains

IIS:
  solver-native infeasibility certificate artifact
  mostly LP/MILP-focused
  returns file listing irreducible infeasible subsystem
  requires CPLEX, Gurobi, or Xpress

MIS:
  Pyomo-side diagnostic workflow
  relaxes variable bounds / constraints to find repair options
  attempts minimal intractable system
  requires a solver, documented workflow uses Ipopt even for LPs
  useful for NLP-style infeasibility investigation
```

Operational distinction:

```text id="lu88ey"
IIS answers:
  "Which small solver-native subset of rows/bounds is infeasible?"

MIS answers:
  "Which relaxations would make the model feasible, and which constraints/bounds form a minimal conflict set?"
```

---

## 31.1 Tool-selection matrix

| Need                                       |      Prefer IIS |             Prefer MIS |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------: | ---------------------: |
| LP/MILP infeasibility                      |             yes |   possible but heavier |
| CPLEX/Gurobi/Xpress available              |             yes |               optional |
| nonlinear model                            |      usually no |                    yes |
| repair options                             |              no |                    yes |
| minimal infeasible/intractable explanation | yes, solver IIS |         yes, Pyomo MIS |
| commercial solver unavailable              |              no | yes if Ipopt available |
| need `.ilp` / solver artifact              |             yes |                     no |
| need bounds-relaxation suggestions         |              no |                    yes |
| model contains nonlinear constraints       |         limited |                    yes |
| production automated diagnosis             | yes for LP/MILP |      yes, with caution |

---

## 31.2 Imports

### 31.2.1 IIS

```python id="hgbfq9"
import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.iis import write_iis
```

`write_iis(pyomo_model, iis_file_name, solver=None, logger=...)` writes an irreducible infeasible set for a Pyomo `Block` or `ConcreteModel`. The `solver` argument must be one of `"cplex"`, `"gurobi"`, or `"xpress"`; if `solver=None`, Pyomo uses the first available supported solver. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

### 31.2.2 MIS

Current/robust import pattern:

```python id="rtelml"
try:
    from pyomo.contrib.iis.mis import compute_infeasibility_explanation
except ImportError:
    from pyomo.contrib.mis import compute_infeasibility_explanation
```

The latest API path documents `pyomo.contrib.iis.mis.compute_infeasibility_explanation(model, solver, tee=False, tolerance=1e-8, logger=...)`, while the infeasibility-diagnostics quick-start shows importing the function from `pyomo.contrib.mis`; using a fallback import makes generated code more robust across Pyomo versions. ([Pyomo Documentation][3])

## 31.3 Minimal infeasible model example

```python id="km3nuq"
import pyomo.environ as pyo

m = pyo.ConcreteModel(name="toy_infeasible")

m.x = pyo.Var(bounds=(0, 1))

m.lb = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= 2)
m.ub = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x <= 1)

m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.x)
```

Solve check:

```python id="d4wyrk"
from pyomo.opt import SolverStatus, TerminationCondition

opt = pyo.SolverFactory("highs")
results = opt.solve(m, load_solutions=False)

if results.solver.termination_condition == TerminationCondition.infeasible:
    print("model is infeasible")
```

### 31.4.6 IIS availability preflight

```python id="ovput3"
def first_available_iis_solver(candidates=("gurobi", "cplex", "xpress")) -> str | None:
    for name in candidates:
        opt = pyo.SolverFactory(name)
        if opt is not None and opt.available(exception_flag=False):
            if hasattr(opt, "license_is_valid"):
                try:
                    if not opt.license_is_valid():
                        continue
                except NotImplementedError:
                    pass
            return name
    return None
```

### 31.4.7 IIS wrapper

```python id="dj2e2q"
from pathlib import Path
import logging

from pyomo.contrib.iis import write_iis


def run_iis(
    model: pyo.Block,
    output_dir: str | Path,
    solver: str | None = None,
    filename: str = "infeasible_model.ilp",
) -> dict:
    output_dir = Path(output_dir)
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    if solver is None:
        solver = first_available_iis_solver()
        if solver is None:
            raise RuntimeError("No IIS-capable solver available: expected gurobi, cplex, or xpress")

    logger = logging.getLogger("pyomo.contrib.iis")
    logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)

    path = output_dir / filename
    written = write_iis(
        pyomo_model=model,
        iis_file_name=str(path),
        solver=solver,
        logger=logger,
    )

    return {
        "tool": "iis",
        "solver": solver,
        "iis_file": str(written),
    }
```

---

## 31.5 IIS interpretation

```text id="uxggxx"
IIS output file:
  solver-native artifact
  identifies a subset of constraints/bounds sufficient for infeasibility
  irreducible with respect to that solver's IIS algorithm
  not necessarily unique
```

Practical interpretation rules:

```text id="gnsycm"
[ ] The IIS is a diagnostic subset, not a full explanation of all modeling errors.
[ ] Multiple IISs may exist.
[ ] Variable bounds may appear alongside named constraints.
[ ] If symbolic solver labels are poor, map generated row names back to Pyomo names carefully.
[ ] Preserve the exact model data used to generate the IIS.
```

IIS is most valuable when the generated file uses recognizable row and variable names. Use stable component names and, where possible, export/diagnose with symbolic labels.

---

## 31.6 MIS workflow

### 31.6.1 Basic MIS call

```python id="9361d8"
ipopt = pyo.SolverFactory("ipopt")

compute_infeasibility_explanation(
    model=m,
    solver=ipopt,
)
```

The Pyomo quick start shows creating an Ipopt solver and calling `compute_infeasibility_explanation(m, solver=ipopt)` instead of solving the model. The docs note that, at the time of writing, Ipopt is needed even for LPs. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

### 31.6.2 MIS with `tee`

```python id="j6slus"
compute_infeasibility_explanation(
    model=m,
    solver=ipopt,
    tee=True,
)
```

### 31.6.3 MIS with tolerance

```python id="of33zq"
compute_infeasibility_explanation(
    model=m,
    solver=ipopt,
    tee=True,
    tolerance=1e-7,
)
```

The documented function parameters are `model`, `solver`, `tee`, `tolerance`, and `logger`; `tolerance` is the feasibility tolerance used when declaring a constraint feasible. ([Pyomo Documentation][3])

### 31.6.4 MIS wrapper

```python id="qkm0m8"
import logging
from pathlib import Path


def run_mis(
    model: pyo.Block,
    solver_name: str = "ipopt",
    tee: bool = False,
    tolerance: float = 1e-8,
) -> dict:
    solver = pyo.SolverFactory(solver_name)
    if solver is None or not solver.available(exception_flag=False):
        raise RuntimeError(f"MIS solver unavailable: {solver_name}")

    logger = logging.getLogger("pyomo.contrib.iis")
    logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)

    compute_infeasibility_explanation(
        model=model,
        solver=solver,
        tee=tee,
        tolerance=tolerance,
        logger=logger,
    )

    return {
        "tool": "mis",
        "solver": solver_name,
        "tolerance": tolerance,
        "logged": True,
    }
```

---

## 31.7 MIS output interpretation

MIS reports two main classes of information:

```text id="zjxhbs"
repair options:
  independent sets of bounds/constraints whose relaxation can make model feasible

minimal intractable system:
  constraints and/or variable bounds appearing mutually conflicting
  minimal under the implemented deletion test
```

The docs show repair options such as relaxing an upper bound of one variable, a lower bound of another variable, or a constraint by a reported amount; then the MIS report lists constraints/bounds in the computed minimal intractable system. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

### 31.7.1 Example repair interpretation

```text id="dvev0e"
"ub of var x[1] by 4.46e-05":
  increasing x[1]'s upper bound by that amount was enough in one repair attempt

"constraint: c by 1.0":
  relaxing constraint c by approximately 1.0 was enough in one repair attempt

"lb of var x[2]":
  x[2]'s lower bound is part of the final minimal intractable system
```

### 31.7.2 Repair options are not modeling fixes

```text id="rqcvuo"
Repair option:
  a mathematically sufficient relaxation found by the diagnostic algorithm

Modeling fix:
  domain/business decision about which data, bound, or equation is wrong
```

Agent rule:

```text id="rn0l89"
Never automatically apply MIS relaxations in production optimization.
Present relaxations as diagnostic candidates.
Require domain-owner approval before changing model/data.
```

---

## 31.8 Guard constraints in MIS

For NLPs, MIS may report **guard** constraints or bounds. These are components that caused solver failure when removed during the diagnostic reduction process, so the tool keeps them for stability; they are not necessarily proven causes of infeasibility. The docs warn that this is a nonlinear-programming issue and that the implementation can interpret failure to get a results object as infeasibility even though solver nonconvergence is not the same as mathematical infeasibility. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

Interpretation:

```text id="ia9cnf"
guard set:
  "removing this made the diagnostic solve unstable/fail"
  not necessarily "this causes infeasibility"

MIS set:
  constraints/bounds found in a minimal conflicting subsystem
```

Best practice:

```text id="es5s47"
When guards appear:
  inspect solver logs
  try better scaling/initialization
  try backup NLP solvers
  rerun with different tolerance
  do not overinterpret guard membership
```

---

## 31.9 Internal MIS mechanics worth knowing

The MIS implementation clones the input model, converts variable bounds/domain information into constraints, removes the original variable bounds/domain restrictions, and adds slack variables to search for repairs. This matters because MIS diagnostics can mention variable bounds as generated constraints and because the original model is intended to remain harmlessly unchanged. ([Pyomo Documentation][4])

Operational implications:

```text id="yc6o4q"
[ ] MIS works on a clone.
[ ] Variable bounds are treated as relaxable constraints.
[ ] Fixed variables are skipped by the bound-to-constraint conversion.
[ ] Diagnostic output may mix original constraints and generated bound constraints.
[ ] Existing variable values are copied into the modified model when possible.
```

---

## 31.10 Best-practice infeasibility workflow

### 31.10.1 Stage 0 — fail fast during data/model build

```text id="onwhdv"
Before solve:
  validate data schema
  validate missing/extra keys
  validate sign/range domains
  validate obvious aggregate feasibility
  validate units
  validate variable bounds
  validate exactly one active objective
  validate no empty-set constraints becoming booleans
```

### 31.10.2 Stage 1 — solve with status-gated result handling

```python id="21d9xu"
def solve_for_status(model, solver_name="highs", tee=True):
    opt = pyo.SolverFactory(solver_name)
    if opt is None or not opt.available(exception_flag=False):
        raise RuntimeError(f"solver unavailable: {solver_name}")

    results = opt.solve(model, tee=tee, load_solutions=False)
    return results
```

### 31.10.3 Stage 2 — classify termination

```python id="64ztsb"
from pyomo.opt import SolverStatus, TerminationCondition

def classify_infeasibility_status(results) -> str:
    term = results.solver.termination_condition

    if term == TerminationCondition.optimal:
        return "optimal"
    if term == TerminationCondition.infeasible:
        return "infeasible"
    if term == TerminationCondition.infeasibleOrUnbounded:
        return "infeasible_or_unbounded"
    if term == TerminationCondition.unbounded:
        return "unbounded"
    return f"other:{term}"
```

### 31.10.4 Stage 3 — if infeasible, run IIS first for LP/MILP

```python id="1l5zrr"
def diagnose_lp_milp_infeasibility(model, output_dir):
    try:
        return run_iis(model, output_dir=output_dir, solver=None)
    except Exception as exc:
        return {
            "tool": "iis",
            "error": str(exc),
        }
```

### 31.10.5 Stage 4 — run MIS when IIS unavailable or NLP model

```python id="bmrf4t"
def diagnose_with_mis(model, solver_name="ipopt"):
    return run_mis(
        model,
        solver_name=solver_name,
        tee=True,
        tolerance=1e-8,
    )
```

### 31.10.6 Stage 5 — build human-readable model audit

```python id="hkrrh9"
def model_infeasibility_audit(model: pyo.Block) -> dict:
    vars_ = list(model.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True))
    cons = list(model.component_data_objects(pyo.Constraint, active=True, descend_into=True))
    objs = list(model.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=True, descend_into=True))

    return {
        "n_active_vars": len(vars_),
        "n_active_constraints": len(cons),
        "n_active_objectives": len(objs),
        "unbounded_vars": [
            {
                "name": v.name,
                "lb": v.lb,
                "ub": v.ub,
                "fixed": v.fixed,
                "domain": str(v.domain),
            }
            for v in vars_
            if not v.fixed and (v.lb is None or v.ub is None)
        ],
        "fixed_vars": [
            {
                "name": v.name,
                "value": pyo.value(v, exception=False),
            }
            for v in vars_
            if v.fixed
        ],
        "inactive_constraints": [
            c.name
            for c in model.component_data_objects(pyo.Constraint, active=False, descend_into=True)
        ],
    }
```

## 31.11 Automated diagnostic router

```python id="x0vsc4"
from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any
import json


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class InfeasibilityConfig:
    primary_solver: str = "highs"
    iis_solver: str | None = None
    mis_solver: str = "ipopt"
    output_dir: Path = Path("infeasibility_diagnostics")
    tee: bool = True
    mis_tolerance: float = 1e-8
    run_mis_after_iis: bool = False


def diagnose_infeasible_model(model: pyo.ConcreteModel, cfg: InfeasibilityConfig) -> dict:
    cfg.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    audit = model_infeasibility_audit(model)

    results = solve_for_status(model, solver_name=cfg.primary_solver, tee=cfg.tee)
    classification = classify_infeasibility_status(results)

    report = {
        "primary_solver": cfg.primary_solver,
        "primary_status": str(results.solver.status),
        "primary_termination": str(results.solver.termination_condition),
        "classification": classification,
        "audit": audit,
        "diagnostics": [],
    }

    if classification == "optimal":
        model.solutions.load_from(results)
        report["loaded_solution"] = True
        return report

    if classification not in {"infeasible", "infeasible_or_unbounded"}:
        return report

    # IIS route.
    try:
        iis_info = run_iis(
            model=model,
            output_dir=cfg.output_dir,
            solver=cfg.iis_solver,
            filename="model_iis.ilp",
        )
        report["diagnostics"].append(iis_info)
    except Exception as exc:
        report["diagnostics"].append({
            "tool": "iis",
            "error": str(exc),
        })

    # MIS route.
    if cfg.run_mis_after_iis or not any(d.get("tool") == "iis" and "iis_file" in d for d in report["diagnostics"]):
        try:
            mis_info = run_mis(
                model=model,
                solver_name=cfg.mis_solver,
                tee=cfg.tee,
                tolerance=cfg.mis_tolerance,
            )
            report["diagnostics"].append(mis_info)
        except Exception as exc:
            report["diagnostics"].append({
                "tool": "mis",
                "error": str(exc),
            })

    manifest_path = cfg.output_dir / "infeasibility_report.json"
    manifest_path.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2, sort_keys=True))

    return report
```

## 31.12 Constraint/bound relaxation modeling pattern

Sometimes a production system needs a **controlled feasibility-relaxation model** separate from IIS/MIS diagnostics.

### 31.12.1 Slack-relax selected constraints

```python id="9gp18g"
def add_elastic_constraint(model, con, penalty: float, name: str):
    slack_pos = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    slack_neg = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    body = con.body
    lb = con.lower
    ub = con.upper

    elastic_block = pyo.Block()
    elastic_block.slack_pos = slack_pos
    elastic_block.slack_neg = slack_neg

    if lb is not None and ub is not None and pyo.value(lb) == pyo.value(ub):
        elastic_block.relaxed = pyo.Constraint(
            expr=body + slack_pos - slack_neg == lb
        )
    elif lb is not None and ub is not None:
        elastic_block.relaxed_lb = pyo.Constraint(expr=body + slack_pos >= lb)
        elastic_block.relaxed_ub = pyo.Constraint(expr=body - slack_neg <= ub)
    elif lb is not None:
        elastic_block.relaxed_lb = pyo.Constraint(expr=body + slack_pos >= lb)
    elif ub is not None:
        elastic_block.relaxed_ub = pyo.Constraint(expr=body - slack_neg <= ub)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"constraint has no finite side: {con.name}")

    elastic_block.penalty = pyo.Expression(expr=penalty * (slack_pos + slack_neg))

    con.deactivate()
    model.add_component(name, elastic_block)

    return elastic_block
```

### 31.12.2 Minimize relaxation

```python id="kgb8dt"
m.relax_penalty = pyo.Expression(expr=sum(b.penalty for b in relaxation_blocks))
m.original_obj.deactivate()
m.relax_obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.relax_penalty, sense=pyo.minimize)
```

Use this as a controlled model-repair workflow, not as a replacement for IIS/MIS.

## 31.13 Common root causes checklist

```text id="0ndvog"
Data errors:
  missing demand/capacity entries
  wrong sign
  wrong units
  duplicate records
  scenario data outside feasible design domain

Modeling errors:
  reversed inequality
  equality too strict
  lower bound above upper bound
  variable fixed inconsistently
  all alternatives deactivated
  multiple policies enforced simultaneously
  empty support sum creates impossible constant constraint

Numerical/formulation errors:
  Big-M too small
  badly scaled constraints
  nonlinear domain violation
  hidden singularity
  presolve detects contradiction

Workflow errors:
  mutating AbstractModel template instead of instance
  stale persistent solver state
  wrong scenario data loaded
  constraints left active from previous solve
```

---

## 31.14 IIS vs MIS limitations

### 31.14.1 IIS limitations

```text id="i45d9h"
[ ] LP/MILP-oriented.
[ ] Requires commercial solver support.
[ ] IIS is not unique.
[ ] File interpretation depends on solver naming.
[ ] May not directly diagnose nonlinear infeasibility.
[ ] Reports conflict subset, not repair magnitude.
```

### 31.14.2 MIS limitations

```text id="xs2dnj"
[ ] Requires solver; documented workflow uses Ipopt.
[ ] Nonlinear solver failures can contaminate interpretation.
[ ] MIS is not guaranteed unique.
[ ] Repair options are diagnostic, not automatically valid business fixes.
[ ] Equality relaxation may produce noisy suggestions in models with definitional/property equations.
[ ] Output is logger-oriented, not a rich returned structured object.
```

The MIS docs explicitly state that the computed MIS is not guaranteed unique and warn that guard constraints in NLP workflows are kept for stability when removing them causes solver failure; this requires careful interpretation. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

```python id="pd5tw6"
def make_file_logger(path: str | Path, name="pyomo.contrib.iis"):
    logger = logging.getLogger(name)
    logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)

    handler = logging.FileHandler(path)
    handler.setLevel(logging.INFO)
    handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("%(levelname)s:%(name)s:%(message)s"))

    logger.addHandler(handler)
    return logger
```

## 31.16 Production-safe infeasibility manifest

```python id="7gueuk"
def infeasibility_manifest(
    model: pyo.Block,
    results,
    diagnostics: list[dict],
    cfg: InfeasibilityConfig,
) -> dict:
    return {
        "primary_solver": cfg.primary_solver,
        "primary_status": str(results.solver.status),
        "primary_termination": str(results.solver.termination_condition),
        "iis_solver": cfg.iis_solver,
        "mis_solver": cfg.mis_solver,
        "mis_tolerance": cfg.mis_tolerance,
        "model_audit": model_infeasibility_audit(model),
        "diagnostics": diagnostics,
        "component_counts": {
            "variables": sum(1 for _ in model.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True)),
            "constraints": sum(1 for _ in model.component_data_objects(pyo.Constraint, active=True, descend_into=True)),
            "objectives": sum(1 for _ in model.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=True, descend_into=True)),
        },
    }
```

## 31.18 Deployment advisory

```text id="lhh9eu"
[ ] Validate data before model construction.
[ ] Solve with load_solutions=False.
[ ] Branch on TerminationCondition before reading variable values.
[ ] Use IIS first for LP/MILP when CPLEX/Gurobi/Xpress is available.
[ ] Use MIS for nonlinear models or when repair explanations are desired.
[ ] Archive IIS files and MIS logs.
[ ] Preserve model data snapshots.
[ ] Use symbolic names and stable component names.
[ ] Treat repair options as diagnostic suggestions, not automatic fixes.
[ ] Interpret guard constraints cautiously in NLP MIS output.
[ ] Re-run solve after any proposed model/data correction.
[ ] Add infeasibility smoke tests to CI for known bad cases.
```

---

## 31.19 Anti-pattern table

| Anti-pattern                                | Failure mode                   | Replacement                                |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| read variable values after infeasible solve | stale/uninitialized values     | branch on termination first                |
| call IIS with CBC/GLPK/HiGHS                | unsupported IIS route          | CPLEX/Gurobi/Xpress                        |
| call MIS without solver                     | function requires solver       | pass Ipopt or solver string/object         |
| auto-apply MIS repair values                | invalid business/model changes | report candidates for review               |
| ignore variable bounds in diagnostics       | missing conflict source        | treat bounds as first-class constraints    |
| use generated unnamed constraints           | unreadable IIS                 | stable component names/symbolic labels     |
| overinterpret guard constraints             | false root-cause attribution   | inspect logs and rerun                     |
| assume IIS/MIS is unique                    | missed alternative conflicts   | run after incremental fixes; compare tools |
| solve transformed/persistent stale model    | wrong diagnosis                | diagnose current concrete instance         |
| no data snapshot                            | irreproducible diagnosis       | archive input data and model manifest      |

## 31.20 Agent-ready integrated template

```python id="qkzsxy"
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict
from pathlib import Path
import json
import logging

import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.opt import SolverStatus, TerminationCondition
from pyomo.contrib.iis import write_iis

try:
    from pyomo.contrib.iis.mis import compute_infeasibility_explanation
except ImportError:
    from pyomo.contrib.mis import compute_infeasibility_explanation


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class InfeasibilityConfig:
    primary_solver: str = "highs"
    iis_solver: str | None = None
    mis_solver: str = "ipopt"
    output_dir: Path = Path("infeasibility_diagnostics")
    tee: bool = True
    mis_tolerance: float = 1e-8
    run_mis_after_iis: bool = False


def make_toy_infeasible_model() -> pyo.ConcreteModel:
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel(name="toy_infeasible")
    m.x = pyo.Var(bounds=(0, 1))
    m.lb = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x >= 2)
    m.ub = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x <= 1)
    m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.x)
    return m


def first_available_iis_solver(candidates=("gurobi", "cplex", "xpress")) -> str | None:
    for name in candidates:
        opt = pyo.SolverFactory(name)
        if opt is None or not opt.available(exception_flag=False):
            continue

        if hasattr(opt, "license_is_valid"):
            try:
                if not opt.license_is_valid():
                    continue
            except NotImplementedError:
                pass

        return name

    return None


def solve_for_status(model: pyo.Block, solver_name: str, tee: bool):
    opt = pyo.SolverFactory(solver_name)
    if opt is None or not opt.available(exception_flag=False):
        raise RuntimeError(f"primary solver unavailable: {solver_name}")

    return opt.solve(model, tee=tee, load_solutions=False)


def classify(results) -> str:
    term = results.solver.termination_condition

    if term == TerminationCondition.optimal:
        return "optimal"
    if term == TerminationCondition.infeasible:
        return "infeasible"
    if term == TerminationCondition.infeasibleOrUnbounded:
        return "infeasible_or_unbounded"
    if term == TerminationCondition.unbounded:
        return "unbounded"

    return f"other:{term}"


def model_audit(model: pyo.Block) -> dict:
    vars_ = list(model.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True))
    cons_active = list(model.component_data_objects(pyo.Constraint, active=True, descend_into=True))
    cons_inactive = list(model.component_data_objects(pyo.Constraint, active=False, descend_into=True))
    objs = list(model.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=True, descend_into=True))

    return {
        "n_active_variables": len(vars_),
        "n_active_constraints": len(cons_active),
        "n_inactive_constraints": len(cons_inactive),
        "n_active_objectives": len(objs),
        "unbounded_variables": [
            {
                "name": v.name,
                "lb": v.lb,
                "ub": v.ub,
                "fixed": bool(v.fixed),
                "value": pyo.value(v, exception=False),
                "domain": str(v.domain),
            }
            for v in vars_
            if not v.fixed and (v.lb is None or v.ub is None)
        ],
        "fixed_variables": [
            {
                "name": v.name,
                "value": pyo.value(v, exception=False),
            }
            for v in vars_
            if v.fixed
        ],
        "active_objectives": [obj.name for obj in objs],
    }


def run_iis_diagnostic(model: pyo.Block, cfg: InfeasibilityConfig) -> dict:
    solver = cfg.iis_solver or first_available_iis_solver()
    if solver is None:
        raise RuntimeError("No IIS-capable solver available; expected gurobi, cplex, or xpress")

    iis_path = cfg.output_dir / "model_iis.ilp"

    logger = logging.getLogger("pyomo.contrib.iis")
    logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)

    written = write_iis(
        pyomo_model=model,
        iis_file_name=str(iis_path),
        solver=solver,
        logger=logger,
    )

    return {
        "tool": "iis",
        "solver": solver,
        "iis_file": str(written),
    }


def run_mis_diagnostic(model: pyo.Block, cfg: InfeasibilityConfig) -> dict:
    solver = pyo.SolverFactory(cfg.mis_solver)
    if solver is None or not solver.available(exception_flag=False):
        raise RuntimeError(f"MIS solver unavailable: {cfg.mis_solver}")

    log_path = cfg.output_dir / "mis.log"
    logger = logging.getLogger("pyomo.contrib.iis")
    logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)

    # Avoid duplicate handlers in repeated test runs.
    if not any(isinstance(h, logging.FileHandler) and h.baseFilename == str(log_path) for h in logger.handlers):
        handler = logging.FileHandler(log_path)
        handler.setLevel(logging.INFO)
        handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("%(levelname)s:%(name)s:%(message)s"))
        logger.addHandler(handler)

    compute_infeasibility_explanation(
        model=model,
        solver=solver,
        tee=cfg.tee,
        tolerance=cfg.mis_tolerance,
        logger=logger,
    )

    return {
        "tool": "mis",
        "solver": cfg.mis_solver,
        "tolerance": cfg.mis_tolerance,
        "log_file": str(log_path),
    }


def diagnose(model: pyo.ConcreteModel, cfg: InfeasibilityConfig) -> dict:
    cfg.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    results = solve_for_status(model, cfg.primary_solver, tee=cfg.tee)
    status = classify(results)

    report = {
        "config": {
            "primary_solver": cfg.primary_solver,
            "iis_solver": cfg.iis_solver,
            "mis_solver": cfg.mis_solver,
            "mis_tolerance": cfg.mis_tolerance,
            "run_mis_after_iis": cfg.run_mis_after_iis,
        },
        "primary_solve": {
            "solver_status": str(results.solver.status),
            "termination_condition": str(results.solver.termination_condition),
            "classification": status,
        },
        "model_audit": model_audit(model),
        "diagnostics": [],
    }

    if status == "optimal":
        model.solutions.load_from(results)
        report["solution_loaded"] = True
    elif status in {"infeasible", "infeasible_or_unbounded"}:
        try:
            report["diagnostics"].append(run_iis_diagnostic(model, cfg))
        except Exception as exc:
            report["diagnostics"].append({
                "tool": "iis",
                "error": str(exc),
            })

        iis_succeeded = any(
            d.get("tool") == "iis" and "iis_file" in d
            for d in report["diagnostics"]
        )

        if cfg.run_mis_after_iis or not iis_succeeded:
            try:
                report["diagnostics"].append(run_mis_diagnostic(model, cfg))
            except Exception as exc:
                report["diagnostics"].append({
                    "tool": "mis",
                    "error": str(exc),
                })

    output_path = cfg.output_dir / "infeasibility_report.json"
    output_path.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2, sort_keys=True))

    return report
```

## 31.21 Final checklist

```text id="v262c0"
[ ] Use write_iis for LP/MILP IIS with CPLEX, Gurobi, or Xpress.
[ ] Use compute_infeasibility_explanation for MIS repair/MIS reports.
[ ] Pass an Ipopt solver to MIS unless your pinned Pyomo workflow supports another solver reliably.
[ ] Do not read variable values after infeasible solves.
[ ] Use load_solutions=False in infeasibility workflows.
[ ] Archive IIS files, MIS logs, model/data manifests, and solver logs.
[ ] Treat variable bounds as first-class infeasibility sources.
[ ] Interpret MIS repair options as suggestions, not automatic corrections.
[ ] Interpret MIS guard constraints cautiously.
[ ] Use stable component names and symbolic labels for debuggability.
[ ] Re-solve after every data/model fix.
[ ] Add known-infeasible diagnostic smoke tests to CI.
```

[1]: https://pyomo.readthedocs.io/en/latest/explanation/analysis/iis.html "Infeasibility Diagnostics — Pyomo 6.10.1.dev0 documentation"
[2]: https://pyomo.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/pyomo.contrib.iis.iis.write_iis.html "write_iis — Pyomo 6.10.0 documentation"
[3]: https://pyomo.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/pyomo.contrib.iis.mis.compute_infeasibility_explanation.html "compute_infeasibility_explanation — Pyomo 6.10.1.dev0 documentation"
[4]: https://pyomo.readthedocs.io/en/6.9.5/_modules/pyomo/contrib/iis/mis.html "pyomo.contrib.iis.mis — Pyomo 6.9.5 documentation"


# 32) Sensitivity, parameter estimation, and design of experiments — Pyomo deep dive

Pyomo’s calibration/uncertainty toolchain spans three distinct layers: **Sensitivity Toolbox** for local NLP perturbation analysis with `sIPOPT`/`k_aug`, **parmest** for parameter estimation, confidence regions, bootstrap/cross-validation, and scenario creation, and **Pyomo.DoE** for model-based experimental design using Fisher-information-based criteria. The Sensitivity Toolbox computes approximate NLP solutions for small parameter perturbations; `parmest` estimates model parameters from experimental data and can create stochastic-programming scenarios; Pyomo.DoE uses science-based Pyomo models to design experiments that improve parameter precision. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

---

## 32.0 Calibration/uncertainty workflow map

```text id="9zo6is"
raw experimental data
  -> Pyomo model with unknown parameters
  -> parmest parameter estimation
  -> covariance / bootstrap / confidence region
  -> parameter uncertainty representation
  -> Pyomo.DoE for next experiment design
  -> new experiment data
  -> repeat

small parameter perturbation around solved NLP
  -> sensitivity toolbox
  -> approximate perturbed solution
  -> screening / local what-if / warm-start insight

estimated parameter distribution
  -> parmest scenario creation
  -> stochastic/robust/what-if optimization
```

Tool boundary:

```text id="nu8rxb"
Sensitivity Toolbox:
  local differential sensitivity around solved NLP

parmest:
  estimate θ from experiment data and quantify uncertainty

Pyomo.DoE:
  select experiment inputs/measurements to maximize information about θ
```

---

## 32.1 Sensitivity Toolbox: capability boundary

```text id="8gt5nc"
Purpose:
  approximate solution change for small parameter perturbations in NLPs

Backends:
  sIPOPT
  k_aug + dot_sens

Input:
  solved or well-initialized Pyomo model/block
  list of mutable Params or fixed Vars
  list of perturbed values

Output:
  manipulated model containing approximate perturbed solution information

Not for:
  large perturbations
  active-set changes
  discrete variables
  global sensitivity
  uncertainty quantification by itself
```

The Sensitivity Toolbox requires either `sIPOPT` or `k_aug` to be installed and available on `PATH`; missing `ipopt_sens`, `k_aug`, or `dot_sens` executables are installation/PATH problems, not ordinary Pyomo modeling errors. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

---

## 32.2 `sensitivity_calculation(...)` syntax

```python id="g9moeh"
from pyomo.contrib.sensitivity_toolbox.sens import sensitivity_calculation
```

Signature:

```python id="qjrr2u"
sensitivity_calculation(
    method,
    instance,
    paramList,
    perturbList,
    cloneModel=True,
    tee=False,
    keepfiles=False,
    solver_options=None,
)
```

Documented arguments:

```text id="cwklfd"
method:
  "sipopt" or "k_aug"

instance:
  Pyomo Block / ConcreteModel

paramList:
  mutable Params or fixed Vars

perturbList:
  perturbed parameter values

cloneModel:
  True -> work on clone
  False -> mutate original model

tee:
  stream solver logs

keepfiles:
  preserve solver files

solver_options:
  options passed to backend solver/executable workflow
```

The function accepts a Pyomo model/block, parameter list, and perturbation list, augments the model with dummy constraints needed by `sIPOPT` or `k_aug`, and returns the model manipulated by the sensitivity interface. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

---

## 32.3 Sensitivity Toolbox: minimal NLP example

```python id="n96spd"
import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.sensitivity_toolbox.sens import sensitivity_calculation


def build_model() -> pyo.ConcreteModel:
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    m.x1 = pyo.Var(initialize=0.15, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    m.x2 = pyo.Var(initialize=0.15, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    m.x3 = pyo.Var(initialize=0.0, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    m.eta1 = pyo.Param(initialize=4.5, mutable=True)
    m.eta2 = pyo.Param(initialize=1.0, mutable=True)

    m.const1 = pyo.Constraint(
        expr=6 * m.x1 + 3 * m.x2 + 2 * m.x3 - m.eta1 == 0
    )
    m.const2 = pyo.Constraint(
        expr=m.eta2 * m.x1 + m.x2 - m.x3 - 1 == 0
    )

    m.cost = pyo.Objective(expr=m.x1**2 + m.x2**2 + m.x3**2)

    return m


m = build_model()

# Base NLP solve recommended before sensitivity call.
ipopt = pyo.SolverFactory("ipopt")
ipopt.solve(m, tee=True)

# Perturbed parameter values.
m.perturbed_eta1 = pyo.Param(initialize=4.0)
m.perturbed_eta2 = pyo.Param(initialize=1.0)

m_sens = sensitivity_calculation(
    "k_aug",
    m,
    [m.eta1, m.eta2],
    [m.perturbed_eta1, m.perturbed_eta2],
    cloneModel=True,
    tee=True,
)
```

## 32.6 Sensitivity Toolbox production wrapper

```python id="sj4qd9"
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict
from shutil import which
from typing import Literal

import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.sensitivity_toolbox.sens import sensitivity_calculation


SensitivityMethod = Literal["sipopt", "k_aug"]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SensitivityConfig:
    method: SensitivityMethod = "k_aug"
    clone_model: bool = True
    tee: bool = False
    keepfiles: bool = False
    solver_options: dict | None = None


def require_sensitivity_executables(method: SensitivityMethod) -> None:
    if method == "sipopt":
        if which("ipopt_sens") is None:
            raise RuntimeError("ipopt_sens executable not found on PATH")
    elif method == "k_aug":
        missing = [exe for exe in ("k_aug", "dot_sens") if which(exe) is None]
        if missing:
            raise RuntimeError(f"required sensitivity executables missing: {missing}")
    else:
        raise ValueError(method)


def require_sensitivity_params(params) -> None:
    for p in params:
        if isinstance(p, pyo.Param):
            if not p.mutable:
                raise ValueError(f"sensitivity Param must be mutable: {p.name}")
        elif isinstance(p, pyo.Var):
            if not p.fixed:
                raise ValueError(f"sensitivity Var must be fixed: {p.name}")
        else:
            raise TypeError(f"unsupported sensitivity parameter object: {p!r}")


def run_sensitivity(
    model: pyo.ConcreteModel,
    params,
    perturbations,
    cfg: SensitivityConfig,
):
    if len(params) != len(perturbations):
        raise ValueError("params and perturbations must have equal length")

    require_sensitivity_executables(cfg.method)
    require_sensitivity_params(params)

    return sensitivity_calculation(
        cfg.method,
        model,
        list(params),
        list(perturbations),
        cloneModel=cfg.clone_model,
        tee=cfg.tee,
        keepfiles=cfg.keepfiles,
        solver_options=cfg.solver_options,
    )
```

Deployment rule:

```text id="77456l"
Use sensitivity_calculation only after solving or initializing the base NLP well.
Treat output as local approximation, not full re-optimization.
Validate by full re-solve on sampled perturbations before production reliance.
```

---

## 32.7 Sensitivity Toolbox validation pattern

```python id="j3e0nf"
def full_resolve_at_perturbation(model, param_updates, solver_name="ipopt"):
    m = model.clone()

    for component_name, value in param_updates.items():
        comp = m.find_component(component_name)
        if comp is None:
            raise KeyError(component_name)
        comp.set_value(value)

    opt = pyo.SolverFactory(solver_name)
    res = opt.solve(m, tee=False, load_solutions=False)

    if res.solver.termination_condition == pyo.TerminationCondition.optimal:
        m.solutions.load_from(res)

    return m, res


def compare_sensitivity_to_resolve(base_model, sens_model, param_updates):
    full_model, full_res = full_resolve_at_perturbation(base_model, param_updates)

    rows = []
    for v in base_model.component_data_objects(pyo.Var, active=True, descend_into=True):
        sv = sens_model.find_component(v.name)
        fv = full_model.find_component(v.name)
        if sv is not None and fv is not None:
            rows.append({
                "var": v.name,
                "sensitivity_value": pyo.value(sv, exception=False),
                "full_resolve_value": pyo.value(fv, exception=False),
            })

    return rows
```

Use this on representative perturbations before accepting sensitivity approximations.

---

## 32.8 `parmest`: parameter estimation capability boundary

```text id="xst13z"
parmest estimates θ from experimental data:
  one labeled model per experiment
  measured outputs with data values
  unknown parameters marked by suffix
  objective usually SSE or weighted SSE
  optional two-stage stochastic-programming interpretation
  optional bootstrap / likelihood / confidence-region workflows
```

`parmest` requires a Pyomo model, experimental data defining multiple scenarios, and parameters to estimate. It can use Pyomo and optionally mpi-sppy to solve a two-stage stochastic-programming problem in which experiment data defines a scenario tree. Its required model convention uses `FirstStageCost` set to zero and `SecondStageCost` as the model-observation deviation, usually sum of squared deviations; alternatively, users can supply a custom second-stage objective function. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

---

## 32.9 `parmest` labeled-model contract

A parmest experiment returns a labeled Pyomo model through `get_labeled_model()`. The core suffixes include:

```text id="2tgdd4"
experiment_outputs:
  model outputs mapped to observed data values

unknown_parameters:
  mutable Params or Vars to estimate

measurement_error:
  measurement standard deviation/error model, used by weighted objectives/DoE

experiment_inputs:
  design/input values, especially for DoE compatibility
```

The parmest docs state that a labeled model has `experiment_outputs` and `unknown_parameters`, where `experiment_outputs` maps output objects to data values and `unknown_parameters` identifies mutable Params or Vars to estimate; parameters to estimate are converted to unfixed variables inside parmest. Pyomo.DoE extends the same suffix-labeling convention with `experiment_inputs`, `experiment_outputs`, `measurement_error`, and `unknown_parameters`. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

---

## 32.10 `parmest` Experiment skeleton

```python id="ecz8ri"
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

import pandas as pd
import pyomo.environ as pyo
import pyomo.contrib.parmest.parmest as parmest


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Observation:
    x: float
    y: float
    sigma: float = 1.0


class LinearExperiment:
    def __init__(self, obs: Observation, theta_init=None):
        self.obs = obs
        self.theta_init = theta_init or {"a": 1.0, "b": 0.0}
        self.model = None

    def create_model(self):
        m = self.model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

        m.x_data = pyo.Param(initialize=self.obs.x)
        m.y_pred = pyo.Var(initialize=self.obs.y)

        # Unknown parameters.
        m.a = pyo.Var(initialize=self.theta_init["a"])
        m.b = pyo.Var(initialize=self.theta_init["b"])

        m.response = pyo.Constraint(
            expr=m.y_pred == m.a * m.x_data + m.b
        )

        return m

    def label_model(self):
        m = self.model

        m.experiment_outputs = pyo.Suffix(direction=pyo.Suffix.LOCAL)
        m.experiment_outputs[m.y_pred] = self.obs.y

        m.unknown_parameters = pyo.Suffix(direction=pyo.Suffix.LOCAL)
        m.unknown_parameters[m.a] = pyo.value(m.a)
        m.unknown_parameters[m.b] = pyo.value(m.b)

        m.measurement_error = pyo.Suffix(direction=pyo.Suffix.LOCAL)
        m.measurement_error[m.y_pred] = self.obs.sigma

        m.experiment_inputs = pyo.Suffix(direction=pyo.Suffix.LOCAL)
        m.experiment_inputs[m.x_data] = self.obs.x

    def get_labeled_model(self):
        if self.model is None:
            self.create_model()
            self.label_model()
        return self.model
```

---

## 32.11 `parmest.Estimator(...)` workflow

```python id="v5zcmr"
data = [
    Observation(x=0.0, y=1.1, sigma=0.2),
    Observation(x=1.0, y=2.9, sigma=0.2),
    Observation(x=2.0, y=5.2, sigma=0.2),
    Observation(x=3.0, y=7.1, sigma=0.2),
]

experiments = [LinearExperiment(obs) for obs in data]

pest = parmest.Estimator(
    experiments,
    obj_function="SSE",
    solver_options={"max_iter": 6000},
)

obj_val, theta_val = pest.theta_est()
```

Core `Estimator` methods:

```python id="eoozxc"
obj_val, theta_val = pest.theta_est()
theta_bootstrap = pest.theta_est_bootstrap()
leave_n_out = pest.theta_est_leaveNout()
obj_at_theta = pest.objective_at_theta(theta_values=...)
confidence = pest.confidence_region_test(theta_values=..., distribution="MVN")
likelihood = pest.likelihood_ratio_test(theta_values=...)
```

Documented parmest methods include `theta_est`, `theta_est_bootstrap`, `theta_est_leaveNout`, `objective_at_theta`, `confidence_region_test`, `likelihood_ratio_test`, and `leaveNout_bootstrap_test`; parmest also includes plotting/distribution-fitting functions such as pairwise plots and rectangular, multivariate-normal, and KDE fits. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

---

## 32.12 `parmest` objective patterns

### 32.12.1 Built-in SSE

```python id="kpr5zu"
pest = parmest.Estimator(experiments, obj_function="SSE")
```

### 32.12.2 Built-in weighted SSE

```python id="7jeo2o"
pest = parmest.Estimator(experiments, obj_function="SSE_weighted")
```

### 32.12.3 Custom objective

```python id="y92nkh"
def robust_abs_error_objective(m):
    return sum(
        abs(model_value - observed_value)
        for model_value, observed_value in m.experiment_outputs.items()
    )


pest = parmest.Estimator(
    experiments,
    obj_function=robust_abs_error_objective,
)
```

For generated code, avoid Python `abs(...)` if the objective must be algebraic and solver-compatible; use positive/negative deviation variables inside the model or a smooth robust loss. parmest supports custom objective functions with a single model argument returning a Pyomo expression used as `SecondStageCost`. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

---

## 32.13 `parmest` initialization strategy

Recommended parmest initialization procedure:

```text id="65u8ja"
1. Build Estimator.
2. Use objective_at_theta(initialize_parmest_model=True) to solve/initialize square instances.
3. Solve full parameter estimation with theta_est().
```

The docs recommend solving a square instance first to check fitted-parameter initial guesses; they specifically mention `objective_at_theta(initialize_parmest_model=True)` and then `theta_est()`. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

Code skeleton:

```python id="xqgxeg"
theta_guess_df = pd.DataFrame(
    [{"a": 2.0, "b": 1.0}]
)

pest.objective_at_theta(
    theta_values=theta_guess_df,
    initialize_parmest_model=True,
)

obj_val, theta_val = pest.theta_est()
```

## 32.14 `parmest` scenario creation

```python id="y8aym7"
import pyomo.contrib.parmest.scenariocreator as sc

scenmaker = sc.ScenarioCreator(pest, "ipopt")

experimentscens = sc.ScenarioSet("Experiments")
scenmaker.ScenariosFromExperiments(experimentscens)
experimentscens.write_csv("experiment_scenarios.csv")

bootscens = sc.ScenarioSet("Bootstrap")
scenmaker.ScenariosFromBootstrap(bootscens, 100)

for scen in bootscens.ScensIterator():
    print(scen.name, scen.probability, scen.ThetaVals)
```

parmest’s scenario-creation workflow creates an `Estimator`, then a `ScenarioCreator`, then fills a `ScenarioSet` with `ParmestScen` objects that can be written to CSV or iterated; documented methods include scenarios from experiments and bootstrap-generated scenarios. ([Pyomo Documentation][3])

Use case:

```text id="2xi3jl"
parameter-estimation uncertainty
  -> theta scenarios with probabilities
  -> stochastic optimization
  -> robust optimization stress testing
  -> design optimization under calibrated uncertainty
```

---

## 32.15 Pyomo.DoE capability boundary

```text id="ib03pe"
Pyomo.DoE:
  model-based design of experiments
  uses science-based Pyomo models
  computes sensitivity matrix Q
  constructs Fisher information matrix M
  optimizes or enumerates experimental design variables
  supports algebraic models and Pyomo.DAE / PDAE-type models
```

Pyomo.DoE’s methodology docs state that model-based design of experiments maximizes experiment information gain, currently focuses on increasing parameter precision, and integrates exploratory analysis, parameter estimation, uncertainty analysis, and optimized experimental design. The user provides one Pyomo model, nominal parameter values, allowable design spaces, and an observation-error model; Pyomo.DoE supports continuous-variable models, equality constraints defining state variables, Pyomo.DAE/PDAE models, and algebraic-only models. ([Pyomo Documentation][4])

---

## 32.16 Fisher Information Matrix concepts

```text id="7rbfl7"
Q:
  dynamic sensitivity matrix
  partial derivatives of outputs y with respect to parameters θ

M:
  Fisher information matrix
  roughly Qᵀ Σ⁻¹ Q plus prior information

large M:
  more information about parameters

criterion Ψ(M):
  scalar objective for experiment quality
```

DoE criteria:

```text id="9nhmnt"
D-optimality:
  determinant(FIM)

A-optimality:
  trace or trace-related measure

E-optimality:
  minimum eigenvalue

ME / modified E-optimality:
  condition-number-related criterion
```

Pyomo.DoE’s API exposes objective options such as `determinant` for D-optimality and `trace` for A-optimality; its full-factorial output reports D-, A-, E-, and modified-E-related metrics such as determinant, trace, minimum/maximum eigenvalues, and condition metrics. ([Pyomo Documentation][5])

---

## 32.17 Pyomo.DoE required experiment labels

```text id="f9fec0"
Required suffixes in documented DoE workflow:
  experiment_inputs
  experiment_outputs
  measurement_error
  unknown_parameters
```

The Pyomo.DoE docs state the required input is an `Experiment` object with a `get_labeled_model()` method returning a Pyomo model with suffixes identifying experiment design decisions, measured outputs, measurement errors, and unknown parameters. The current API reference also notes that DoE was refactored and mentions labeled sets/suffixes named `unknown_parameters`, `experimental_inputs`, and `experimental_outputs`; wrappers that support multiple Pyomo versions should validate the suffix names used by the pinned version. ([Pyomo Documentation][4])

---

## 32.18 Pyomo.DoE Experiment skeleton

```python id="gdig0x"
import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.doe import DesignOfExperiments


class StaticLinearDoEExperiment:
    def __init__(self, theta_nominal=None, design_init=None):
        self.theta_nominal = theta_nominal or {"a": 2.0, "b": 1.0}
        self.design_init = design_init or {"x": 1.0}
        self.model = None

    def create_model(self):
        m = self.model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

        # Design variable.
        m.x = pyo.Var(
            initialize=self.design_init["x"],
            bounds=(0.0, 10.0),
        )

        # Unknown parameters.
        m.a = pyo.Var(initialize=self.theta_nominal["a"])
        m.b = pyo.Var(initialize=self.theta_nominal["b"])

        # Predicted output.
        m.y = pyo.Var(initialize=0.0)

        m.response = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.y == m.a * m.x + m.b)

        return m

    def finalize_model(self):
        # Use for discretization, fixing known values, applying design bounds, etc.
        return self.model

    def label_model(self):
        m = self.model

        m.experiment_inputs = pyo.Suffix(direction=pyo.Suffix.LOCAL)
        m.experiment_inputs[m.x] = pyo.value(m.x)

        m.experiment_outputs = pyo.Suffix(direction=pyo.Suffix.LOCAL)
        m.experiment_outputs[m.y] = None

        m.measurement_error = pyo.Suffix(direction=pyo.Suffix.LOCAL)
        m.measurement_error[m.y] = 0.1

        m.unknown_parameters = pyo.Suffix(direction=pyo.Suffix.LOCAL)
        m.unknown_parameters[m.a] = pyo.value(m.a)
        m.unknown_parameters[m.b] = pyo.value(m.b)

    def get_labeled_model(self):
        if self.model is None:
            self.create_model()
            self.finalize_model()
            self.label_model()
        return self.model
```

---

## 32.19 Pyomo.DoE usage patterns

### 32.19.1 Construct DoE object

```python id="rqu1ia"
solver = pyo.SolverFactory("ipopt")

experiment = StaticLinearDoEExperiment()

doe = DesignOfExperiments(
    experiment=experiment,
    fd_formula="central",
    step=1e-3,
    objective_option="determinant",
    solver=solver,
    tee=True,
)
```

### 32.19.2 Check labels

```python id="d6lrr8"
model = experiment.get_labeled_model()
doe.check_model_labels(model)
```

### 32.19.3 Compute FIM for current design

```python id="u9qbqg"
FIM = doe.compute_FIM(model=model, method="sequential")
```

or:

```python id="q5ip7k"
FIM = doe.compute_FIM(model=model, method="kaug")
```

`DesignOfExperiments.compute_FIM(model=None, method='sequential')` computes the FIM for the design initialized by `get_labeled_model()`; documented method options are `kaug` and `sequential`. ([Pyomo Documentation][5])

### 32.19.4 Full factorial enumeration

```python id="2zjrn5"
factorial_results = doe.compute_FIM_full_factorial(
    model=model,
    design_ranges={
        "x": [0.0, 10.0, 11],
    },
    method="sequential",
)
```

`compute_FIM_full_factorial(...)` performs a grid search/parameter sweep over experiment-input ranges and returns FIM-related metrics including log10 D-, A-, E-, and ME-optimality, eigenvalues, determinant, trace, and solve time. ([Pyomo Documentation][5])

### 32.19.5 Optimize experiment design

```python id="mf7gyw"
doe_model = doe.create_doe_model(model=model)
result = doe.run_doe(model=doe_model, results_file="doe_results.json")
```

`create_doe_model(...)` adds sensitivity, FIM, and objective equations to the Pyomo model and alters the model input; `run_doe(...)` solves the single-experiment DoE problem and can save JSON results. ([Pyomo Documentation][5])

---

## 32.20 Pyomo.DoE with DAE

```python id="5nkr99"
from pyomo.dae import ContinuousSet, DerivativeVar


class DynamicDoEExperiment:
    def __init__(self, data, nfe=20, ncp=3):
        self.data = data
        self.nfe = nfe
        self.ncp = ncp
        self.model = None

    def create_model(self):
        m = self.model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

        m.t = ContinuousSet(bounds=(0, 1))

        m.CA = pyo.Var(m.t, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
        m.T = pyo.Var(m.t, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

        m.A = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
        m.E = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
        m.R = pyo.Param(initialize=8.314)

        m.dCAdt = DerivativeVar(m.CA, wrt=m.t)

        @m.Expression(m.t)
        def k(m, t):
            return m.A * pyo.exp(-m.E / (m.R * m.T[t]))

        @m.Constraint(m.t)
        def ode(m, t):
            return m.dCAdt[t] == -m.k[t] * m.CA[t]

        return m

    def finalize_model(self):
        m = self.model

        m.CA[0].fix(self.data["CA0"])
        m.A.fix(self.data["A_nominal"])
        m.E.fix(self.data["E_nominal"])

        for t in m.t:
            m.T[t].setlb(self.data["T_bounds"][0])
            m.T[t].setub(self.data["T_bounds"][1])
            m.T[t].set_value(self.data["T_init"])

        pyo.TransformationFactory("dae.collocation").apply_to(
            m,
            nfe=self.nfe,
            ncp=self.ncp,
            wrt=m.t,
        )

        return m

    def label_model(self):
        m = self.model

        m.experiment_inputs = pyo.Suffix(direction=pyo.Suffix.LOCAL)
        for t in m.t:
            m.experiment_inputs[m.T[t]] = pyo.value(m.T[t])

        m.experiment_outputs = pyo.Suffix(direction=pyo.Suffix.LOCAL)
        for t in self.data["measurement_times"]:
            m.experiment_outputs[m.CA[t]] = None

        m.measurement_error = pyo.Suffix(direction=pyo.Suffix.LOCAL)
        for t in self.data["measurement_times"]:
            m.measurement_error[m.CA[t]] = self.data["sigma_CA"]

        m.unknown_parameters = pyo.Suffix(direction=pyo.Suffix.LOCAL)
        m.unknown_parameters[m.A] = pyo.value(m.A)
        m.unknown_parameters[m.E] = pyo.value(m.E)

    def get_labeled_model(self):
        if self.model is None:
            self.create_model()
            self.finalize_model()
            self.label_model()
        return self.model
```

Pyomo.DoE’s documented reaction-kinetics example builds a Pyomo.DAE model, finalizes it by adding data and collocation discretization, then labels experiment outputs, measurement errors, and unknown parameters via suffixes. ([Pyomo Documentation][4])

## 32.21 Calibration and uncertainty workflow: integrated stages

### 32.21.1 Stage A — Estimate parameters

```python id="kzp4i9"
experiments = [LinearExperiment(obs) for obs in data]

pest = parmest.Estimator(
    experiments,
    obj_function="SSE_weighted",
    solver_options={"max_iter": 6000},
)

obj_val, theta_hat = pest.theta_est()
```

### 32.21.2 Stage B — Quantify parameter uncertainty

```python id="61kmrc"
theta_boot = pest.theta_est_bootstrap()
cov = pest.cov_est()
```

### 32.21.3 Stage C — Create parameter scenarios

```python id="px61ie"
import pyomo.contrib.parmest.scenariocreator as sc

scenmaker = sc.ScenarioCreator(pest, "ipopt")

bootscens = sc.ScenarioSet("Bootstrap")
scenmaker.ScenariosFromBootstrap(bootscens, 100)
bootscens.write_csv("theta_scenarios.csv")
```

### 32.21.4 Stage D — Design next experiment

```python id="zvfvg6"
experiment = DynamicDoEExperiment(data=doe_data)
doe = DesignOfExperiments(
    experiment=experiment,
    objective_option="determinant",
    solver=pyo.SolverFactory("ipopt"),
)

model = experiment.get_labeled_model()
FIM = doe.compute_FIM(model=model, method="sequential")
doe_model = doe.create_doe_model(model=model)
doe.run_doe(model=doe_model, results_file="next_experiment.json")
```

### 32.21.5 Stage E — Local perturbation sensitivity for operational what-if

```python id="b9yg9x"
m_sens = sensitivity_calculation(
    "k_aug",
    fitted_model,
    [fitted_model.theta1, fitted_model.theta2],
    [new_theta1, new_theta2],
    cloneModel=True,
)
```

## 32.22 Decision matrix

| Need                                             | Tool                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- |
| Fast local estimate after small parameter change | Sensitivity Toolbox                     |
| Exact solution after parameter change            | full re-solve                           |
| Estimate parameters from experiments             | parmest                                 |
| Confidence regions / bootstrap distributions     | parmest                                 |
| Convert estimated θ uncertainty to scenarios     | parmest ScenarioCreator                 |
| Pick next experiment design                      | Pyomo.DoE                               |
| Quantify expected information at fixed design    | Pyomo.DoE `compute_FIM`                 |
| Grid search over design space                    | Pyomo.DoE `compute_FIM_full_factorial`  |
| Dynamic experiment design                        | Pyomo.DoE + Pyomo.DAE                   |
| Stochastic optimization over parameter scenarios | parmest scenarios + mpi-sppy / EF       |
| Robust optimization over continuous uncertainty  | PyROS / robust model, not parmest alone |

## 32.23 Validation and QA checks

### 32.23.1 Sensitivity input checks

```python id="oqt5vg"
def validate_sensitivity_inputs(params, perturbations):
    if len(params) != len(perturbations):
        raise ValueError("params and perturbations must have the same length")

    for p in params:
        if isinstance(p, pyo.Param) and not p.mutable:
            raise ValueError(f"Param is not mutable: {p.name}")
        if isinstance(p, pyo.Var) and not p.fixed:
            raise ValueError(f"Var is not fixed: {p.name}")
```

### 32.23.2 parmest experiment checks

```python id="ycsbyf"
def validate_parmest_experiment(exp):
    m = exp.get_labeled_model()

    required = ["experiment_outputs", "unknown_parameters"]
    missing = [name for name in required if not hasattr(m, name)]

    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"parmest labeled model missing suffixes: {missing}")

    if len(m.experiment_outputs) == 0:
        raise ValueError("experiment_outputs suffix is empty")

    if len(m.unknown_parameters) == 0:
        raise ValueError("unknown_parameters suffix is empty")
```

### 32.23.3 DoE label checks

```python id="b32prp"
def validate_doe_experiment(exp):
    m = exp.get_labeled_model()

    required = [
        "experiment_inputs",
        "experiment_outputs",
        "measurement_error",
        "unknown_parameters",
    ]

    missing = [name for name in required if not hasattr(m, name)]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"DoE model missing suffixes: {missing}")

    for name in required:
        if len(getattr(m, name)) == 0:
            raise ValueError(f"DoE suffix is empty: {name}")
```

### 32.23.4 Calibration sanity checks

```python id="p8a5pr"
def validate_theta_estimate(theta_val):
    if theta_val is None:
        raise ValueError("theta estimate is None")

    for name, value in theta_val.items():
        if not pyo.value(value, exception=False) == pyo.value(value, exception=False):
            raise ValueError(f"theta estimate is NaN: {name}")
```

## 32.24 Common failure modes

| Failure                                 | Likely cause                                          | Replacement                                                      |
| --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ipopt_sens` not found                  | sIPOPT not on `PATH`                                  | install/build sIPOPT and export PATH                             |
| `k_aug` or `dot_sens` not found         | k_aug install/PATH issue                              | install k_aug and add executables to PATH                        |
| sensitivity approximation poor          | perturbation too large / active set changed           | full re-solve                                                    |
| parmest cannot identify outputs         | missing `experiment_outputs` suffix                   | label model outputs                                              |
| parmest unknown parameter not estimated | missing `unknown_parameters` suffix                   | label unknown Params/Vars                                        |
| parmest solver failure                  | bad initial θ / poor scaling                          | square initialization, bounds, scaling                           |
| DoE label failure                       | missing required suffixes                             | implement `get_labeled_model()` correctly                        |
| DoE direct_kaug issue                   | parameters/design not Vars                            | use Vars for direct_kaug; Params only when not using direct_kaug |
| FIM singular                            | unidentifiable parameters / insufficient measurements | add measurements/design variables or fix parameters              |
| D-opt objective unstable                | nearly singular FIM                                   | regularize/prior FIM, E/A criteria, bounds                       |
| scenario creation fails                 | Ipopt/linear solver issue                             | check Ipopt build and parmest scenario workflow                  |

Pyomo.DoE notes that parameters and design variables should be Pyomo `Var` components for `direct_kaug` mode and can be `Param` objects if not using `direct_kaug`; parmest scenario creation notes that Ipopt linear-solver quality can affect examples. ([Pyomo Documentation][4])

---

## 32.25 Deployment advisory

```text id="lv5s0m"
[ ] Pin Pyomo version; DoE APIs were refactored in recent releases.
[ ] Pin Ipopt, k_aug, sIPOPT, and solver executable paths.
[ ] Add preflight checks for executable availability.
[ ] Use stable Experiment classes with deterministic get_labeled_model().
[ ] Keep model creation, finalization, labeling, estimation, DoE, and reporting separate.
[ ] Archive data, theta estimates, covariance/bootstrap samples, FIM, solver logs, and scenario CSVs.
[ ] Validate sensitivity approximations by full re-solve on sample perturbations.
[ ] Use DoE after calibration uncertainty assessment, not before understanding model identifiability.
[ ] Treat FIM criteria as design heuristics tied to local parameter nominal values.
[ ] Never interpret singular/ill-conditioned FIM as strong identifiability.
```

---

## 32.26 Anti-pattern table

| Anti-pattern                                                        | Failure mode                          | Replacement                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| sensitivity toolbox for large perturbations                         | inaccurate approximation              | full re-solve / scenario sweep           |
| mutable Param omitted from sensitivity list                         | no sensitivity computed               | pass every perturbed parameter           |
| non-mutable Param in sensitivity                                    | invalid input                         | `mutable=True` Param or fixed Var        |
| parmest model without suffix labels                                 | estimator cannot build objective      | implement labeled Experiment             |
| unknown parameter left fixed as Var                                 | not estimated                         | label and allow parmest to unfix         |
| DoE without measurement error model                                 | invalid FIM weighting                 | fill `measurement_error` suffix          |
| DoE with unbounded design variables                                 | unrealistic experiment recommendation | design bounds                            |
| FIM determinant maximization on singular FIM without regularization | numerical failure                     | prior FIM / alternative criterion        |
| scenario CSV without provenance                                     | irreproducible uncertainty            | manifest with estimator/bootstrap config |
| global claims from local sensitivity                                | false interpretation                  | label as local approximation             |

---

## 32.27 Agent-ready integrated template

```python id="82dhsx"
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict
from pathlib import Path
from shutil import which
import json

import pandas as pd
import pyomo.environ as pyo
import pyomo.contrib.parmest.parmest as parmest
import pyomo.contrib.parmest.scenariocreator as sc
from pyomo.contrib.doe import DesignOfExperiments
from pyomo.contrib.sensitivity_toolbox.sens import sensitivity_calculation


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CalibrationConfig:
    parmest_solver_options: dict | None = None
    sensitivity_method: str = "k_aug"
    doe_objective_option: str = "determinant"
    doe_fd_formula: str = "central"
    doe_step: float = 1e-3
    scenario_solver: str = "ipopt"
    output_dir: Path = Path("calibration_outputs")


def require_executable(name: str) -> None:
    if which(name) is None:
        raise RuntimeError(f"required executable not found on PATH: {name}")


def preflight_sensitivity(method: str) -> None:
    if method == "sipopt":
        require_executable("ipopt_sens")
    elif method == "k_aug":
        require_executable("k_aug")
        require_executable("dot_sens")
    else:
        raise ValueError(method)


class LinearExperiment:
    def __init__(self, row, theta_init=None):
        self.row = row
        self.theta_init = theta_init or {"a": 1.0, "b": 0.0}
        self.model = None

    def create_model(self):
        m = self.model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

        m.x_data = pyo.Param(initialize=float(self.row["x"]))
        m.y_pred = pyo.Var(initialize=float(self.row["y"]))

        m.a = pyo.Var(initialize=self.theta_init["a"])
        m.b = pyo.Var(initialize=self.theta_init["b"])

        m.response = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.y_pred == m.a * m.x_data + m.b)

        return m

    def label_model(self):
        m = self.model

        m.experiment_outputs = pyo.Suffix(direction=pyo.Suffix.LOCAL)
        m.experiment_outputs[m.y_pred] = float(self.row["y"])

        m.unknown_parameters = pyo.Suffix(direction=pyo.Suffix.LOCAL)
        m.unknown_parameters[m.a] = pyo.value(m.a)
        m.unknown_parameters[m.b] = pyo.value(m.b)

        m.measurement_error = pyo.Suffix(direction=pyo.Suffix.LOCAL)
        m.measurement_error[m.y_pred] = float(self.row.get("sigma", 1.0))

        m.experiment_inputs = pyo.Suffix(direction=pyo.Suffix.LOCAL)
        m.experiment_inputs[m.x_data] = float(self.row["x"])

    def get_labeled_model(self):
        if self.model is None:
            self.create_model()
            self.label_model()
        return self.model


class LinearDoEExperiment:
    def __init__(self, theta_nominal):
        self.theta_nominal = theta_nominal
        self.model = None

    def create_model(self):
        m = self.model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

        m.x = pyo.Var(bounds=(0.0, 10.0), initialize=1.0)
        m.y = pyo.Var(initialize=0.0)

        m.a = pyo.Var(initialize=float(self.theta_nominal["a"]))
        m.b = pyo.Var(initialize=float(self.theta_nominal["b"]))

        m.response = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.y == m.a * m.x + m.b)

        return m

    def label_model(self):
        m = self.model

        m.experiment_inputs = pyo.Suffix(direction=pyo.Suffix.LOCAL)
        m.experiment_inputs[m.x] = pyo.value(m.x)

        m.experiment_outputs = pyo.Suffix(direction=pyo.Suffix.LOCAL)
        m.experiment_outputs[m.y] = None

        m.measurement_error = pyo.Suffix(direction=pyo.Suffix.LOCAL)
        m.measurement_error[m.y] = 1.0

        m.unknown_parameters = pyo.Suffix(direction=pyo.Suffix.LOCAL)
        m.unknown_parameters[m.a] = pyo.value(m.a)
        m.unknown_parameters[m.b] = pyo.value(m.b)

    def get_labeled_model(self):
        if self.model is None:
            self.create_model()
            self.label_model()
        return self.model


def validate_experiment(exp):
    m = exp.get_labeled_model()
    required = ["experiment_outputs", "unknown_parameters"]
    missing = [name for name in required if not hasattr(m, name)]
    if missing:
        raise RuntimeError(f"experiment missing parmest labels: {missing}")


def estimate_parameters(data: pd.DataFrame, cfg: CalibrationConfig):
    experiments = [LinearExperiment(row) for _, row in data.iterrows()]
    for exp in experiments:
        validate_experiment(exp)

    pest = parmest.Estimator(
        experiments,
        obj_function="SSE_weighted",
        solver_options=cfg.parmest_solver_options or {"max_iter": 6000},
    )

    obj_val, theta_val = pest.theta_est()

    return pest, obj_val, theta_val


def create_parmest_scenarios(pest, cfg: CalibrationConfig, n_bootstrap: int = 100):
    scenmaker = sc.ScenarioCreator(pest, cfg.scenario_solver)

    experiments = sc.ScenarioSet("Experiments")
    scenmaker.ScenariosFromExperiments(experiments)

    bootstrap = sc.ScenarioSet("Bootstrap")
    scenmaker.ScenariosFromBootstrap(bootstrap, n_bootstrap)

    cfg.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    experiments.write_csv(str(cfg.output_dir / "experiment_scenarios.csv"))
    bootstrap.write_csv(str(cfg.output_dir / "bootstrap_scenarios.csv"))

    return experiments, bootstrap


def run_doe(theta_val, cfg: CalibrationConfig):
    experiment = LinearDoEExperiment(theta_val)

    solver = pyo.SolverFactory("ipopt")
    if solver is None or not solver.available(exception_flag=False):
        raise RuntimeError("Ipopt unavailable for DoE")

    doe = DesignOfExperiments(
        experiment=experiment,
        fd_formula=cfg.doe_fd_formula,
        step=cfg.doe_step,
        objective_option=cfg.doe_objective_option,
        solver=solver,
        tee=True,
    )

    model = experiment.get_labeled_model()
    doe.check_model_labels(model)

    FIM = doe.compute_FIM(model=model, method="sequential")
    doe_model = doe.create_doe_model(model=model)
    doe_results = doe.run_doe(
        model=doe_model,
        results_file=str(cfg.output_dir / "doe_results.json"),
    )

    return FIM, doe_results


def run_local_sensitivity(model, param_pairs, cfg: CalibrationConfig):
    preflight_sensitivity(cfg.sensitivity_method)

    params = [pair[0] for pair in param_pairs]
    perturbations = [pair[1] for pair in param_pairs]

    return sensitivity_calculation(
        cfg.sensitivity_method,
        model,
        params,
        perturbations,
        cloneModel=True,
        tee=True,
        keepfiles=True,
    )


def write_calibration_manifest(path: Path, cfg: CalibrationConfig, obj_val, theta_val, FIM):
    payload = {
        "config": {
            "sensitivity_method": cfg.sensitivity_method,
            "doe_objective_option": cfg.doe_objective_option,
            "doe_fd_formula": cfg.doe_fd_formula,
            "doe_step": cfg.doe_step,
            "scenario_solver": cfg.scenario_solver,
        },
        "parmest": {
            "objective": float(obj_val),
            "theta": {k: float(v) for k, v in dict(theta_val).items()},
        },
        "doe": {
            "FIM": FIM.tolist() if hasattr(FIM, "tolist") else FIM,
        },
    }

    path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True))


def run_calibration_workflow(data: pd.DataFrame, cfg: CalibrationConfig = CalibrationConfig()):
    cfg.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    pest, obj_val, theta_val = estimate_parameters(data, cfg)
    create_parmest_scenarios(pest, cfg, n_bootstrap=100)
    FIM, doe_results = run_doe(theta_val, cfg)

    write_calibration_manifest(
        cfg.output_dir / "calibration_manifest.json",
        cfg,
        obj_val,
        theta_val,
        FIM,
    )

    return {
        "estimator": pest,
        "objective": obj_val,
        "theta": theta_val,
        "FIM": FIM,
        "doe_results": doe_results,
    }
```
