## 39.8 CI solver matrix: deployment-grade

### 39.8.1 Matrix principle

```text id="msk3yv"
CI tiers:
  unit tests:
    no solver
    validate data contracts
    model shape / component counts

  open-source smoke:
    HiGHS / GLPK / CBC
    tiny known-solution models
    always-on

  optional commercial:
    Gurobi / CPLEX / Xpress
    protected runner
    license secret
    not for fork PRs

  HPC/container:
    image build
    solver availability probe
    one tiny solve
```

### 39.8.2 GitHub Actions open-source smoke

```yaml id="jqser4"
name: pyomo-ci

on:
  push:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  test-open-source:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.11", "3.12"]
        solver: ["highs"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}

      - run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          python -m pip install pyomo highspy pytest

      - run: |
          python - <<'PY'
          import pyomo.environ as pyo
          s = pyo.SolverFactory("${{ matrix.solver }}")
          assert s is not None and s.available(exception_flag=False)
          PY

      - run: pytest -q
```

### 39.8.4 Pytest markers

```python id="qmvnkg"
# conftest.py

import pytest
import pyomo.environ as pyo


def solver_available(name: str) -> bool:
    solver = pyo.SolverFactory(name)
    return bool(solver and solver.available(exception_flag=False))


def pytest_configure(config):
    config.addinivalue_line("markers", "solver(name): requires a solver")
    config.addinivalue_line("markers", "gurobi: requires Gurobi license")


def pytest_collection_modifyitems(config, items):
    for item in items:
        marker = item.get_closest_marker("solver")
        if marker:
            name = marker.args[0]
            if not solver_available(name):
                item.add_marker(pytest.mark.skip(reason=f"solver unavailable: {name}"))
```

Usage:

```python id="hitutn"
@pytest.mark.solver("highs")
def test_tiny_lp_highs():
    ...
```

## 39.9 Advanced deployment anti-patterns

| Anti-pattern                                                      | Failure mode                        | Replacement                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| Pyomo installed but solver omitted                                | runtime solver unavailable          | package solver explicitly                 |
| one output file appended by all ranks                             | corrupted logs/results              | per-case artifacts, rank-0 summary        |
| MPI ranks × solver threads > cores                                | oversubscription, slow solves       | set rank/thread product                   |
| unrestricted commercial solver probes                             | license token exhaustion            | centralized/throttled availability checks |
| container contains private license                                | security/compliance failure         | runtime secret mount/env                  |
| persistent solver shared without lock                             | cross-request state corruption      | one worker/lock per persistent solver     |
| replacing Pyomo component under persistent solver without removal | stale solver-side component remains | remove from solver, delete, recreate, add |
| treating time limit as optimal                                    | false claims                        | status/termination policy                 |
| no solver option manifest                                         | unreproducible results              | record options and seeds                  |
| no solver version pin                                             | performance/solution drift          | pin solver binary/binding                 |
| no input snapshot                                                 | impossible audit                    | write input artifact                      |
| no symbolic solver labels in debug exports                        | unreadable LP/IIS files             | `symbolic_solver_labels=True`             |
| scheduler array ignores license capacity                          | mass failures                       | cap array concurrency                     |
| cloud workers use mutable global model                            | state leakage                       | request-local or locked manager           |

## 39.10 Deployment checklists

### 39.10.1 Batch study checklist

```text id="ya3x31"
[ ] Case schema versioned.
[ ] Input data validated before solve.
[ ] Output directory unique per case.
[ ] Solver log per case.
[ ] Manifest per case.
[ ] Summary file generated by single process/rank.
[ ] Failed cases write error artifact.
[ ] Time limit configured.
[ ] Status/termination recorded.
[ ] Values extracted only after checked solution load.
```

### 39.10.2 MPI checklist

```text id="faizhu"
[ ] mpi4py installed against runtime MPI.
[ ] mpirun/srun command documented.
[ ] Case partitioning deterministic.
[ ] Rank-local model construction.
[ ] Rank-local solver construction.
[ ] No shared writes except rank-0 summary.
[ ] Thread count set to avoid oversubscription.
[ ] License concurrency below token count.
[ ] Failures gathered and summarized.
```

### 39.10.3 Container checklist

```text id="dzcjg1"
[ ] Python version pinned.
[ ] Pyomo version pinned.
[ ] Solver package/binary installed.
[ ] Solver availability smoke test at build or startup.
[ ] Commercial licenses injected at runtime, not baked.
[ ] Entrypoint uses normal package CLI.
[ ] Non-root user where possible.
[ ] Scratch/output volumes configured.
[ ] Image digest recorded in manifest.
```

### 39.10.4 Service checklist

```text id="dfquy2"
[ ] Payload validation before model build.
[ ] Model-size limits.
[ ] Solver time limits.
[ ] Worker concurrency limits.
[ ] License-aware queue.
[ ] Request IDs in artifacts/logs.
[ ] Solution loading status-gated.
[ ] Persistent solver state locked or per worker.
[ ] License release policy documented.
[ ] Health endpoint checks solver availability separately from license availability.
```

### 39.10.5 Reproducibility checklist

```text id="4osc0s"
[ ] Input data snapshot.
[ ] Git commit / package version.
[ ] Python version.
[ ] Pyomo version.
[ ] Solver name/version.
```

## 39.11 Final implementation skeleton

```text id="4keiam"
myopt/
  domain.py           # data classes
  validation.py       # data validation
  model.py            # build_model(data)
  solve.py            # solve_checked, SolverConfig
  batch.py            # BatchCase, run_case, run_batch_serial
  parallel_mpi.py     # mpi4py scatter/gather runner
  service.py          # request-local or persistent service
  manifest.py         # runtime/environment/solver manifests
  diagnostics.py      # infeasibility/logging/model stats
  cli.py              # user entrypoint

deploy/
  Dockerfile.highs
  Dockerfile.gurobi
  environment.yml
  requirements.lock
  slurm_mpi.sh
  slurm_array.sh

tests/
  test_validation.py
  test_model_shape.py
  test_tiny_solve.py
  test_batch_runner.py
  test_manifest.py
```

Core rule:

```text id="zqstdh"
Correctness path:
  single tiny solve
  model-shape tests
  serial batch
  reproducibility artifacts
  parallel execution
  persistent/APPSI optimization
  cloud/HPC/container hardening
```

Do not start with persistent solvers, MPI, or cloud job arrays. First make one checked solve deterministic, artifacted, and testable.

## 40) Extension ecosystem and related packages — Pyomo deep dive

Source frame: expands the uploaded Pyomo advanced plan’s **Section 40** and preserves the uploaded Cyclopts-style, dense, agent-oriented documentation pattern.  

Pyomo ecosystem layers:

```text id="xsdxs6"
pyomo core:
  AML components, expression system, transformations, solver interfaces, base utilities

pyomo.contrib:
  in-tree optional / contributed / specialized packages
  analysis tools, meta-solvers, decomposition, interfaces, diagnostics, utilities

external Pyomo ecosystem:
  independently versioned packages built on Pyomo models
  domain applications, stochastic programming, process systems, water systems, ML-in-optimization

solver/runtime ecosystem:
  third-party solvers, Python bindings, MPI, scientific stack, domain libraries

publication/citation ecosystem:
  core Pyomo citation
  subpackage papers
  external package papers
```

Core deployment invariant:

```text id="ksp70q"
Importing pyomo.environ is not ecosystem readiness.
For every extension:
  identify package namespace
  identify optional Python dependencies
  identify external solvers
  identify solver licenses
  identify citation requirements
  identify API stability expectations
  add availability tests
```

## 40.1 `pyomo.contrib` role and stability model

`pyomo.contrib` currently exposes many contributed modules, including `alternative_solutions`, `appsi`, `benders`, `community_detection`, `cp`, `doe`, `fbbt`, `fme`, `gdpopt`, `iis`, `incidence_analysis`, `mindtpy`, `mpc`, `multistart`, `parmest`, `pynumero`, `pyros`, `sensitivity_toolbox`, `trustregion`, `viewer`, and others. The stable library reference lists these modules under `pyomo.contrib`, so agents should treat `pyomo.contrib` as an inventory of specialized capabilities rather than a single coherent API surface. ([Pyomo Documentation][1])

Pyomo’s contribution guide distinguishes the core framework from extension/experimental namespaces and states that contributed packages are optional, may not be maintained by the core developer team, and can require optional dependencies; new non-core code is also described in terms of `pyomo.addons`, `pyomo.devel`, and `pyomo.unsupported` stability tiers. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

```text id="zwjl2z"
Agent interpretation:
  pyomo.core / pyomo.environ:
    stable modeling surface

  pyomo.contrib:
    use with explicit docs, dependencies, tests, and version pins

  pyomo.addons:
    mostly stable supported extensions under newer namespace policy

  pyomo.devel:
    active research / experimental; APIs may change

  pyomo.unsupported:
    no reliability expectation
```

---

## 40.2 `pyomo.contrib` inventory by capability

### 40.2.1 Analysis and diagnostics

| Module                                | Capability                                     | Use when                                           |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `pyomo.contrib.alternative_solutions` | enumerate alternative / near-optimal solutions | solution diversity, trade-off exploration          |
| `pyomo.contrib.iis`                   | IIS workflow via commercial solvers            | LP/MILP infeasibility explanation                  |
| `pyomo.contrib.mis`                   | MIS / repair explanations                      | infeasibility diagnosis, often NLP/IPOPT-backed    |
| `pyomo.contrib.incidence_analysis`    | variable-constraint incidence graphs           | decomposition, structural debugging                |
| `pyomo.contrib.community_detection`   | graph/community decomposition                  | block structure discovery                          |
| `pyomo.contrib.sensitivity_toolbox`   | sensitivity via external tools                 | perturbation analysis                              |
| `pyomo.contrib.doe`                   | design of experiments                          | model-based experimental design                    |
| `pyomo.contrib.parmest`               | parameter estimation                           | calibration, confidence regions, scenario creation |

The alternative-solutions library provides functions such as `enumerate_binary_solutions`, `enumerate_linear_solutions`, Gurobi solution-pool routines, and OBBT-style analysis, returning custom `Solution` objects rather than normal Pyomo solver result objects. ([Pyomo Documentation][3])

### 40.2.2 Meta-solvers and advanced algorithms

| Module                         | Capability                    | Use when                                             |
| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `pyomo.contrib.gdpopt`         | GDP decomposition algorithms  | nonlinear/logical GDP solving                        |
| `pyomo.contrib.mindtpy`        | MINLP decomposition           | OA, ECP, GOA, feasibility-pump-style MINLP workflows |
| `pyomo.contrib.pyros`          | robust optimization solver    | two-stage adjustable robust optimization             |
| `pyomo.contrib.benders`        | Benders decomposition support | decomposition algorithms                             |
| `pyomo.contrib.multistart`     | multistart NLP                | nonconvex local NLP exploration                      |
| `pyomo.contrib.trustregion`    | trust-region solver framework | model-based nonlinear black-box / hybrid workflows   |
| `pyomo.contrib.interior_point` | interior-point utilities      | algorithm development                                |

### 40.2.3 Solver/interface infrastructure

| Module                    | Capability                                            | Use when                                               |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `pyomo.contrib.appsi`     | auto-persistent solver interfaces                     | repeated solves with small updates                     |
| `pyomo.contrib.pynumero`  | nonlinear programming / linear algebra infrastructure | custom NLP algorithms, block matrices                  |
| `pyomo.contrib.mcpp`      | MC++ interface                                        | expression convexity/interval analysis where available |
| `pyomo.contrib.satsolver` | SAT / SMT-adjacent interface utilities                | logical/CP experiments                                 |
| `pyomo.contrib.cp`        | constraint-programming-related support                | CP-style integrations                                  |

APPSI is documented as “Auto-Persistent Pyomo Solver Interfaces,” intended to behave similarly to standard Pyomo solver interfaces while improving repeated-solve efficiency; documented APPSI solvers include Gurobi, Ipopt, Cplex, Cbc, HiGHS, and MAiNGO. ([Pyomo Documentation][4])

### 40.2.4 Modeling utilities

| Module                         | Capability                         | Use when                        |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `pyomo.contrib.fbbt`           | feasibility-based bound tightening | preprocessing, Big-M tightening |
| `pyomo.contrib.fme`            | Fourier-Motzkin elimination        | projection/elimination          |
| `pyomo.contrib.preprocessing`  | preprocessing transformations      | structural simplification       |
| `pyomo.contrib.piecewise`      | specialized piecewise utilities    | piecewise formulations          |
| `pyomo.contrib.gdp_bounds`     | GDP bound utilities                | GDP reformulation support       |
| `pyomo.contrib.simplification` | expression/model simplification    | model cleanup                   |
| `pyomo.contrib.latex_printer`  | LaTeX expression/model output      | documentation, debugging        |
| `pyomo.contrib.viewer`         | interactive tree viewer            | notebook/model inspection       |

## 40.3 High-value `pyomo.contrib` syntax patterns

### 40.3.1 Alternative solutions

```python id="ish62r"
import pyomo.environ as pyo
import pyomo.contrib.alternative_solutions as aos

m = build_milp_model(data)

solutions = aos.enumerate_binary_solutions(
    m,
    num_solutions=25,
    solver="highs",
    solver_options={"time_limit": 300},
    tee=False,
    seed=123,
)

for sol in solutions:
    print(sol.objective_value)
    print(sol.get_variable_name_values())
```

Use case:

```text id="ywa4kp"
Use alternative solutions when:
  optimal solution is not enough
  model has degeneracy
  user wants feasible tradeoffs
  downstream business rules are unmodeled
  robustness to formulation misspecification matters
```

### 40.3.2 APPSI repeated solve

```python id="qetwpi"
from pyomo.contrib import appsi

m = build_parametric_model(data)
opt = appsi.solvers.Highs()

for scenario in scenarios:
    update_mutable_params(m, scenario)

    res = opt.solve(m)

    if res.termination_condition != appsi.base.TerminationCondition.optimal:
        raise RuntimeError(f"bad APPSI termination: {res.termination_condition}")

    report = extract_solution(m)
```

Use case:

```text id="zosf9e"
Use APPSI when:
  same model structure
  many small numeric updates
  repeated solve overhead matters
  supported solver is available
  solver interface semantics are tested
```

### 40.3.3 IIS

```python id="topdq0"
from pyomo.contrib.iis import write_iis

iis_path = write_iis(
    pyomo_model=m,
    iis_file_name="diagnostics/model_iis.ilp",
    solver="gurobi",  # "cplex" | "gurobi" | "xpress" | None
)
```

Pyomo’s IIS tool is a conduit to commercial solvers that compute irreducible infeasible systems; the documented solver choices are CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress, or `None` to select an available solver. ([Pyomo Documentation][5])

### 40.3.4 Parmest

```python id="ybng8d"
from pyomo.contrib.parmest.parmest import Estimator

est = Estimator(
    experiment_list,
    theta_names=["k1", "k2"],
    obj_function="SSE",
)

theta_est = est.theta_est(solver="ipopt")
```

`parmest` is documented as a Pyomo-based package for parameter estimation using experimental data, confidence regions, and subsequent stochastic-programming scenario creation. ([Pyomo Documentation][6])

### 40.3.5 Pyomo.DoE

```python id="d0s7iv"
# High-level schematic only; concrete API depends on model/experiment abstraction.
from pyomo.contrib.doe import DesignOfExperiments

doe = DesignOfExperiments(
    experiment,
    fd_formula="central",
)

result = doe.run_doe(
    model=m,
    solver="ipopt",
)
```

Pyomo.DoE is documented as a Python library for model-based design of experiments using science-based models; it focuses on exploratory analysis and MBDoE, supports continuous-variable optimization models, equality-constrained state-variable models, Pyomo.DAE/PDAE models, and algebraic-constraint models. ([Pyomo Documentation][7])

## 40.4 External ecosystem packages

Pyomo’s related-packages page lists packages that utilize or build off Pyomo and explicitly notes that the list is not comprehensive and is not necessarily an endorsement by the Pyomo team. Listed examples include modeling extensions such as Coramin, PAO, and OMLT; solution strategies such as mpi-sppy, Parapint, Galini, and Suspect; and domain applications such as Chama, Egret, IDAES, Prescient, PrOMMiS, and WaterTAP. ([Pyomo Documentation][8])

### 40.4.1 `mpi-sppy`

```text id="tm18p1"
Package:
  mpi-sppy

Primary use:
  scenario-based stochastic programming
  multi-stage optimization under uncertainty
  parallel decomposition / extensive form / PH-style workflows

Core integration:
  scenario_creator returns Pyomo model instances
  MPI parallelization
  solver per scenario/subproblem
```

`mpi-sppy` documentation states that it supports solving multi-stage stochastic programs based on scenario discretization and uses MPI for parallelization; its docs emphasize building a model file with a `scenario_creator` function and running with `generic_cylinders`. ([mpi-sppy][9])

Schematic model module:

```python id="y6bfk2"
# my_stoch_model.py

import pyomo.environ as pyo

def scenario_creator(scenario_name: str, **kwargs):
    data = load_scenario_data(scenario_name, **kwargs)

    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=data["items"])
    m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    m.y = pyo.Var(m.I, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # required stochastic-programming metadata is added per mpi-sppy conventions
    attach_nonanticipativity_metadata(m, scenario_name, data)

    return m
```

Deployment notes:

```text id="d3p1ce"
mpi-sppy deployment:
  install mpi-sppy
  install mpi4py
  install MPI runtime matching mpi4py build
  install subproblem solvers
  test with small scenario count
  control solver threads × MPI ranks
  use rank-local logs/artifacts
```

### 40.4.2 IDAES

```text id="7xf47l"
Package:
  idaes-pse

Primary use:
  process systems engineering
  flowsheets
  property packages
  unit models
  initialization workflows
  scaling/diagnostics
  process optimization

Core integration:
  IDAES models are Pyomo models
  Pyomo components remain inspectable
  standard Pyomo solver interfaces are generally used
```

IDAES documentation states that IDAES is based on Pyomo and that Pyomo documentation covers the underlying sets, parameters, variables, objectives, constraints, expressions, and suffixes; the same page describes IDAES top-level components as flowsheets, property packages, and unit models. ([idaes-pse.readthedocs.io][10]) IDAES solver docs state that standard Pyomo solver interfaces and features are generally used in IDAES, while IDAES adds extensions such as default solver configuration, solver logging, and solver feature checks. ([idaes-pse.readthedocs.io][11])

Schematic IDAES-style boundary:

```python id="cppoja"
# IDAES imports intentionally kept in IDAES modules, not generic Pyomo modules.
from idaes.core import FlowsheetBlock
from idaes.core.solvers import get_solver

m = pyo.ConcreteModel()
m.fs = FlowsheetBlock(dynamic=False)

# add property packages, unit models, arcs, initialization, scaling

solver = get_solver("ipopt")
results = solver.solve(m, tee=True)
```

Deployment notes:

```text id="jx2744"
IDAES deployment:
  pin idaes-pse version
  pin Pyomo version compatible with IDAES
  install IDAES extensions/solvers as required
  use IDAES initialization and scaling workflows
  expose underlying Pyomo diagnostics for debugging
```

### 40.4.3 WaterTAP

```text id="yc74u3"
Package:
  watertap

Primary use:
  water treatment process modeling
  technoeconomic assessment
  treatment-train simulation/optimization
  unit/property/costing model libraries

Core integration:
  WaterTAP leverages IDAES
  IDAES uses Pyomo
  WaterTAP flowsheets remain equation-oriented optimization models
```

NAWI describes WaterTAP as an open-source Python package for technoeconomic assessment of full water treatment trains; it further states that WaterTAP leverages IDAES and represents models with Pyomo, enabling simulation and optimization through open-source and commercial solvers. ([nawihub.org][12]) WaterTAP documentation also states that WaterTAP is based on IDAES conventions and that new users should be familiar with Python and Pyomo. ([watertap.readthedocs.io][13])

Deployment notes:

```text id="pq0a0f"
WaterTAP deployment:
  install watertap with compatible idaes-pse
  install nonlinear solvers, usually Ipopt-class
  validate property/costing packages
  run provided tutorial/example smoke tests
  version-pin water, IDAES, Pyomo, solver stack together
```

### 40.4.4 Parmest

```text id="4tjuba"
Package:
  pyomo.contrib.parmest

Primary use:
  parameter estimation
  data reconciliation
  covariance estimation
  confidence regions
  scenario creation

Core integration:
  Pyomo model + experiment data
  often solves many scenario-like models
  may use nonlinear solvers and optionally stochastic-programming tooling
```

`parmest` is in `pyomo.contrib` rather than an external package in current Pyomo docs, but deployment semantics are ecosystem-like because it pulls in data, nonlinear solves, optional plotting/scientific stack, and often parallel workflows. The parmest documentation states that parameter estimation requires a Pyomo model, experimental data defining scenarios, and parameters to estimate. ([Pyomo Documentation][14])

### 40.4.5 Pyomo.DoE

```text id="e6i1s2"
Package:
  pyomo.contrib.doe

Primary use:
  model-based design of experiments
  Fisher-information / parameter precision workflows
  digital-twin calibration design
  DAE/algebraic model experiment design

Core integration:
  Pyomo model / experiment abstraction
  solver-backed design optimization
  complements parmest
```

Pyomo.DoE documentation describes an iterative workflow linking exploratory analysis, parameter estimation, uncertainty analysis, and MBDoE; it also states that Parmest can infer parameter values and approximate covariance while MBDoE recommends new experimental conditions when uncertainty remains large. ([Pyomo Documentation][7])

---

## 40.5 Core Pyomo vs `pyomo.contrib` vs external package

| Requirement                              |      Use core Pyomo |      Use `pyomo.contrib` |         Use external package |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------: | -----------------------: | ---------------------------: |
| basic LP/MILP/NLP model                  |                 yes |                       no |                           no |
| GDP/MINLP meta-solver                    |               maybe | yes: `gdpopt`, `mindtpy` |                        maybe |
| repeated solves                          | yes: mutable Params |               yes: APPSI |                        maybe |
| formal stochastic programming algorithms |                  no |                  limited |              yes: `mpi-sppy` |
| flowsheet/unit/property process modeling |                  no |                       no |                   yes: IDAES |
| water-treatment technoeconomics          |                  no |                       no |                yes: WaterTAP |
| parameter estimation                     |   possible manually |           yes: `parmest` | domain-specific alternatives |
| model-based experimental design          |   possible manually |           yes: Pyomo.DoE | domain-specific alternatives |
| incidence/decomposition analysis         |              manual |                      yes |                        maybe |
| production-grade stable core API         |                 yes |         module-dependent |            package-dependent |
| domain library reuse                     |                  no |                  limited |                          yes |
| specialized citations needed             |          Pyomo only |       Pyomo + subpackage |       Pyomo + package papers |

Agent rule:

```text id="h1f71r"
Stay in core Pyomo when:
  algebraic model is straightforward
  custom formulation is clearer than framework abstraction
  dependency footprint must be minimal
  solver workflow is one-shot or simple repeated solve

Use pyomo.contrib when:
  capability is already implemented and documented
  dependency footprint is acceptable
  tests pin the module behavior
  solver requirements are explicit

Use external packages when:
  domain abstractions dominate algebraic formulation
  package supplies validated model libraries
  package supplies algorithms not in core Pyomo
  package conventions are worth adopting
```

## 40.6 Dependency management for optional packages

Pyomo installation docs state that extensions and many `pyomo.contrib` packages can depend on additional third-party packages, including `matplotlib`, `networkx`, `numpy`, `openpyxl`, `pandas`, `pint`, `scipy`, `sympy`, and `xlrd`; missing optional dependencies generally raise errors when the extension is used. The docs show `pip install 'pyomo[optional]'` for all optional dependencies and explain that solvers are not installed with Pyomo. ([Pyomo Documentation][15])

### 40.6.1 Minimal core environment

```text id="ntbbhn"
requirements-core.txt
  pyomo==<pin>
  highspy==<pin>      # optional solver binding, example
```

### 40.6.2 Analysis environment

```text id="mtccyv"
requirements-analysis.txt
  pyomo==<pin>
  numpy==<pin>
  scipy==<pin>
  pandas==<pin>
  networkx==<pin>
  matplotlib==<pin>
  openpyxl==<pin>
  sympy==<pin>
  pint==<pin>
```

### 40.6.3 Full optional Pyomo environment

```bash id="csv0he"
python -m pip install "pyomo[optional]"
```

Use for:

```text id="rcenlx"
developer workstation
notebooks
contrib exploration
documentation examples
CI extension coverage
```

Avoid for:

```text id="2wc8r1"
minimal containers
production microservices
serverless functions
strict dependency surface areas
```

### 40.6.5 Feature-specific extras map

| Feature              | Python deps                                     | Non-Python deps                | Solver deps                |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | -------------------------- |
| APPSI HiGHS          | `highspy`                                       | none                           | HiGHS via Python binding   |
| APPSI Gurobi         | `gurobipy`                                      | Gurobi runtime/license         | Gurobi                     |
| Parmest              | `numpy`, `pandas`, plotting/scipy stack as used | none typical                   | Ipopt / selected solver    |
| Pyomo.DoE            | `numpy`, `scipy`, plotting stack as used        | none typical                   | Ipopt-class NLP solver     |
| mpi-sppy             | `mpi-sppy`, `mpi4py`                            | MPI implementation             | subproblem solver(s)       |
| IDAES                | `idaes-pse`                                     | IDAES extensions as needed     | Ipopt-class solvers common |
| WaterTAP             | `watertap`, `idaes-pse`                         | IDAES/WaterTAP extension stack | Ipopt-class solvers common |
| incidence/community  | `networkx`, `scipy`                             | none                           | optional                   |
| units                | `pint`                                          | none                           | none                       |
| Excel data workflows | `openpyxl`, `xlrd`                              | none                           | none                       |

### 40.6.6 Runtime dependency probe

```python id="rkbqd2"
from importlib.util import find_spec

def require_python_package(import_name: str, feature: str) -> None:
    if find_spec(import_name) is None:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Missing optional dependency {import_name!r} required for {feature}."
        )


def require_solver(name: str) -> None:
    solver = pyo.SolverFactory(name)
    if solver is None or not solver.available(exception_flag=False):
        raise RuntimeError(f"Missing solver {name!r}.")


def check_feature_environment(feature: str) -> None:
    if feature == "doe":
        require_python_package("numpy", "Pyomo.DoE")
        require_python_package("scipy", "Pyomo.DoE")
        require_solver("ipopt")

    elif feature == "parmest":
        require_python_package("pandas", "parmest")
        require_solver("ipopt")

    elif feature == "mpi-sppy":
        require_python_package("mpisppy", "mpi-sppy")
        require_python_package("mpi4py", "mpi-sppy")

    elif feature == "idaes":
        require_python_package("idaes", "IDAES")

    elif feature == "watertap":
        require_python_package("watertap", "WaterTAP")
        require_python_package("idaes", "WaterTAP")
```

## 40.7 Import design for LLM agents

### 40.7.1 Keep optional imports local

```python id="q89cmw"
def enumerate_alternative_solutions(model, solver="highs"):
    import pyomo.contrib.alternative_solutions as aos

    return aos.enumerate_binary_solutions(
        model,
        num_solutions=20,
        solver=solver,
    )
```

Avoid top-level optional imports in core model modules:

```python id="2ijmf9"

import pandas as pd
import idaes
import pyomo.contrib.doe
import mpi4py
```

```text id="g4lt2q"
idaes_flowsheet.py:
  import idaes

stochastic_driver.py:
  import mpisppy
```

```python id="h71uq2"
    attach_stochastic_metadata(m, scenario_name, kwargs)
```


Workflow:

```text id="5plqh6"
data -> experiment objects -> Pyomo model factory
  -> parmest parameter estimation
  -> covariance/confidence analysis
  -> Pyomo.DoE design recommendation
  -> new experiment data
  -> repeat
```

Pyomo.DoE docs explicitly describe this iterative calibration/uncertainty/MBDoE loop and connect Parmest to parameter estimation and covariance approximation. ([Pyomo Documentation][7])

## 40.9 Testing and CI for ecosystem features

### 40.9.1 Pytest markers

```python id="cz2o1s"
# conftest.py

import pytest
from importlib.util import find_spec
import pyomo.environ as pyo


def package_available(name: str) -> bool:
    return find_spec(name) is not None


def solver_available(name: str) -> bool:
    solver = pyo.SolverFactory(name)
    return bool(solver and solver.available(exception_flag=False))


def pytest_configure(config):
    for marker in [
        "contrib",
        "doe",
        "parmest",
        "mpisppy",
        "idaes",
        "watertap",
        "solver(name)",
        "commercial_solver",
    ]:
        config.addinivalue_line("markers", marker)


def pytest_collection_modifyitems(config, items):
    for item in items:
        if item.get_closest_marker("doe") and not package_available("scipy"):
            item.add_marker(pytest.mark.skip(reason="Pyomo.DoE optional stack unavailable"))

        if item.get_closest_marker("parmest") and not package_available("pandas"):
            item.add_marker(pytest.mark.skip(reason="parmest optional stack unavailable"))

        if item.get_closest_marker("mpisppy") and not package_available("mpisppy"):
            item.add_marker(pytest.mark.skip(reason="mpi-sppy unavailable"))

        if item.get_closest_marker("idaes") and not package_available("idaes"):
            item.add_marker(pytest.mark.skip(reason="IDAES unavailable"))

        if item.get_closest_marker("watertap") and not package_available("watertap"):
            item.add_marker(pytest.mark.skip(reason="WaterTAP unavailable"))

        solver_marker = item.get_closest_marker("solver")
        if solver_marker:
            solver_name = solver_marker.args[0]
            if not solver_available(solver_name):
                item.add_marker(pytest.mark.skip(reason=f"solver unavailable: {solver_name}"))
```

### 40.9.2 CI tiers

```text id="np1sqq"
Tier 0:
  core Pyomo model tests
  no optional ecosystem packages

Tier 1:
  pyomo[optional]
  analysis/contrib smoke tests
  open-source solvers

Tier 2:
  mpi-sppy + mpi4py + MPI runtime
  small stochastic-programming smoke

Tier 3:
  IDAES / WaterTAP workflows
  domain examples
  nonlinear solver stack

Tier 4:
  commercial solvers
  IIS, solution pools, commercial APPSI
  protected runners only
```

Pyomo’s contribution guide states optional packages that are unavailable cause tests to skip, and it describes guarded optional-dependency testing using availability flags; agents should mirror that style in downstream packages. ([Pyomo Documentation][2])

## 40.10 Citing Pyomo and subpackages

### 40.10.1 Citation policy

```text id="asbmjq"
Always cite:
  Pyomo core when Pyomo is used

Also cite:
  Pyomo.DAE if using pyomo.dae
  Pyomo.DoE if using Pyomo.DoE
  parmest if using parmest
  mpi-sppy if using mpi-sppy
  IDAES if using IDAES
  WaterTAP if using WaterTAP
  solver software if required by solver license/publication norms
```

Pyomo’s citation page asks users to cite both the Pyomo book and the Pyomo journal paper when using Pyomo; it also gives separate guidance for PySP and Pyomo.DAE. ([Pyomo][16]) Pyomo.DoE documentation gives the Wang and Dowling 2022 AIChE Journal citation, and parmest documentation asks users to cite the parmest paper. ([Pyomo Documentation][7])

### 40.10.2 Citation metadata file

```yaml id="8j13ad"
core:

subpackages:

  parmest:

solvers:

    used: false
```

## 40.11 Anti-pattern table

| Anti-pattern                                                      | Failure mode                    | Replacement                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| importing ecosystem packages in `model.py` unconditionally        | minimal installs fail           | local imports in feature modules             |
| assuming `pyomo.contrib` APIs are uniformly stable                | version drift                   | pin Pyomo, cite module docs, add smoke tests |
| using `pyomo[optional]` in every production image                 | bloated dependency surface      | feature-specific extras                      |
| using IDAES/WaterTAP for simple algebraic LP                      | unnecessary framework overhead  | core Pyomo                                   |
| manually coding stochastic decomposition when `mpi-sppy` fits     | duplicated algorithms           | use mpi-sppy with scenario API               |
| using mpi-sppy for a few deterministic scenarios                  | unnecessary MPI complexity      | normal batch loop                            |
| using Parmest for one scalar least-squares estimate               | framework overhead              | direct SciPy/Pyomo workflow                  |
| using Pyomo.DoE before model calibration contract exists          | invalid experiment design       | validate model/measurements first            |
| mixing external package versions without lock                     | incompatible Pyomo/solver stack | environment lock and smoke tests             |
| not recording optional-feature dependencies                       | unreproducible deployment       | feature manifest                             |
| not citing subpackages                                            | publication/compliance gap      | citation manifest                            |
| commercial solver feature used in contrib workflow without marker | CI failures                     | optional protected solver jobs               |
| treating related-packages list as endorsement                     | inappropriate trust assumption  | independent package evaluation               |

---

## 40.12 Agent checklist

```text id="noedp3"
[ ] Identify whether requirement is core Pyomo, pyomo.contrib, or external package.
[ ] Inspect official docs for the exact package namespace.
[ ] Keep optional imports local.
[ ] Add runtime package probes.
[ ] Add solver availability probes.
[ ] Add pytest markers for optional packages and solvers.
[ ] Pin Pyomo version.
[ ] Pin external package versions.
[ ] Pin solver package/binary versions.
[ ] Avoid pyomo[optional] in minimal production images unless justified.
[ ] Use conda for compiled/scientific/solver-heavy environments when practical.
[ ] Use mpi-sppy for multi-stage stochastic programs requiring scenario decomposition/MPI.
[ ] Use IDAES for process-system flowsheets, property packages, and unit models.
[ ] Use WaterTAP for water-treatment train modeling and technoeconomic analysis.
[ ] Use Parmest for Pyomo-based parameter estimation and confidence/scenario workflows.
[ ] Use Pyomo.DoE for model-based design of experiments.
[ ] Use APPSI for high-frequency repeated solves with supported solvers.
[ ] Treat IIS/MIS, alternative-solutions, incidence, and sensitivity tools as analysis workflows with solver dependencies.
[ ] Maintain a feature-to-dependency matrix.
[ ] Maintain a feature-to-citation matrix.
[ ] Cite Pyomo core and every used subpackage/package with a publication request.
```

## SMARTREF Implementation Note - 2026-05-14

SMARTREF now uses pre-solver Math IR enrichment before Pyomo realization. The adapter consumes `MathSolverPreAnalysisReport` for scaling suffixes, derived variable bounds, transformation-readiness provenance, structural preflight, Ipopt scaling options, and derivative-strategy options. Realized Pyomo incidence and scaling remain authoritative observations, but they are reconciled against pre-analysis predictions instead of being the only planning evidence.
